ayt, enough with the memes.. (but logically speaking its something like that)
Tekken 7, this is among the first of the entire Franchise to be ported officially in the PC Ecosystem..
Let's Talk about Graphics.... :
Textures are great, and the gameplay is locked at the sweet sweet 60FPS, and with the power of the Unreal Engine 4, there's no doubt that the graphics on this one is Top Notch(but not in the level of Crysis tho, thats on a completely different level) for a fighting game. Stutter rarely happen during gameplay[heppens when a controller gets disconnected multiple times], but in my case[I turned V-Sync On] whenever a Cutscene occurs, it then plays in 30FPS and sometimes with a very bad monitor/TV tearing will be very much noticable but take in note, this only happens on Cut scenes, the game play stays locked at 60 FPS. The game will remain visually pleasing, no matter how long you've played it, the visuals will still impress and please the eye, and the game truly have utilized the power of the Unreal Engine 4..
Let's Talk about Graphics settings..[for a bit]:
The game pretty much have a simplified list of changable settings, unlike GTA 5's expansive and detailed list of tweakable settings, Tekken 7 stays down in a conservative approach, but the offerings is kind of enough to make you try and tweak it out a bit.
Let's Talk about the Gameplay..:
As someone who played this series since Tekken 3, it still have the old feeling of what the game series truly stand out among the other entries in this specific genre. Be it a Series Veteran or a New Comer or a Series Casual, you'd get the chance to feel at home and how the mechanics work. Reflex and Player Response is key to the game's mechanics. Press a hit too early and you'll be screwed, hit it too late, you're screwed as well. Difficulty of the game is set to 4 modes, 1 star[easy] 3 stars[medium] 6 stars[hard] 10 stars[very hard(unlocked after completing story mode)] and to take note, the AI Scaling on the game is Fair enough, Beginners to - 1st Kyu A.I.'s are easy, 1st Dan - Initiate gets harder, and this continues to the highest possible rank..
Let's Talk about the Story/Plot...:
[MAIN STORY]
If you're like me, who hated Heihachi since the first time you played the game, then you're in a trip. The main story only revolves around these fighters: Heihachi, Lee, Alisa Bosconovitch, Lars, Kazuya, Akuma, Kazumi, Jin, & Nina
The conclusion of the Mishima Saga is pretty much going to give you a feels trip after knowing Heihachi's Purpose/Perspective. He may sound like an crude and rough person due to his attitude but he's forced into who he is today. The story pretty much is predicatble but the emotional scar it leaves after completing the Main Story makes you cry and have feels while facing the Main Menu... *cries as the Main Menu Music plays* and Kazuya will serve your♥♥♥♥♥ A LOT!
[SIDE STORY]
The other characters in the roster tho, they don't really have any close interactions between the characters mentioned above[main story], if you're used to the old formula that every character's desire got fulfilled after winning the tournament and it takes a total of 9 - 10 rounds, then you're out of luck cause the other characters only have 1 round to play as and against with, and a cutscene will then play, so just don't expect too much from it. but if you're to cross reference it to the Main Story, it could be understandable because Heihachi hosted the 7th King of Iron Fist Tournament as a distraction, which then a couple chapters of the story goes, then closed off, which is why most of the characters only have 1 interaction between each other[a kind of acceptable reason for me]. but if you really loved the old formula, you'll definitely ask for more side character battles, and interactions..
Let's Talk about DLC..:
I know almost everyone hates DLC's, but don't worry, Katsuhiro Harada[The creator/director of Project Tekken] says that they'll be adding 2 guest characters as Paid DLC for the first year, but if the Characters that was in previous Tekken Games, and isn't a guest character of the previous games, the said character will be released for free. But these added characters will not affect the main storyline of the game, and will not change any of the events prior to the main story. Game modes will be added too as DLC(as I could recall) but you're better off doing some research from Tekken Youtubers about this discussion, since my memory isn't that clear about it.
Lets Talk about Game Modes..:
As of the moment the playable game modes are the following:
Arcade
Treasure Battle
2 player VS
Practice
if you're a fan of Ghost Mode, then you're kind of out of Luck since that mode didn't exist yet(I hope they'll add this mode). The closest experience of Ghost Mode will be the Treasure Battle. Treasure Battle will be where you'll be spending most of your time if you love customising your characters. and Treasure battle will also have some random match settings like Heist Mode(you battle an opponent, and unlock a certain item specific to your character) Turbo Mode(which sets the game's speed in a fast manner) Double Damage Mode(which doubles each damage dealt)..
but after a couple hours of grinding it in, the game modes do tend to get boring..
I do hope that they'll add more modes, or even allow the player to make their own Custom [offline] Game Modes, just like in Overwatch's Custom Arcade Game Modes, which would give the user the ability to change Damage Modifiers, Health Size, Game Speed, and all those details that can make or break a game, since I believe this will give the game a fresh and fun appeal to people who are bored or just looking to play in Turbo Mode all the time..
Let's Talk about Character Customization:
If you've enjoyed Tekken 6's Customization system, then you might be disappointed a little bit cause Tekken 7's Customization System isn't that robust and detailed, Upper and Lower Body outfits to be specific, most of them are just T-Shirts, being re-fit to the Character's Body, and straight out of the bat if you wanted to customize your characters straight from starting the game, then you're kind of out of luck again, cause most of the GOOD and Awesome Customization items are still needed to be unlocked from Treasure Battle, think of it as a Chest/Loot Box which randomly unlocks the item, but the good part is that once you got that item unlocked, you get it for FREE, So technically there's a Grind aspect if you really wanted to get the Aura's. and the awesome thing is, once you unlocked an Aura, anything equipped will not be removed(sweet right?) but the Character Customization didn't lose out from the Color Variants though, you can choose any color in the color spectrum, which is nice, cause if you really wanted to have that certain shade of green or grey or blue, then you could finally get it.
Let's Talk about the Over-all Experience[conclusion]:
My Game Rating: 9.0/10.0
Recommend this game?: YES!
PRO's:
If you're a Tekken Fan then this will definitely a must buy/play, Characters of the series do still have the Quirky and Fun Nature, the Story is Great(just expect to get feels) the gameplay is fun, graphics are stunning, PC Optimization is Great. You can set multiple Character Customization Loadout when picking the characters.
CON's:
The game modes are quite limited, and customization isn't as expansive as Tekken 6's system, and the A.I. in the Final Battle of Kazuya and Heihachi really do kicks your♥♥♥♥♥a lot, which requires to to really learn the mechanics or just simply suck it up and play on the easiest difficulty cause you got rekt a lot of times already, but even tho you're playing on the easiest mode it would still serve your♥♥♥♥♥to you..

Spelunky: Don’t Mess Up
Spelunky… Boy, this game. If you don’t know what it is, then buckle up! In many ways Spelunky is one of a kind. Many games are similar, but no game is just like Spelunky. It’s controls are tight, responsive, and precise. It’s difficulty is unforgiving, but not insurmountable. It rewards creativity with success, and punishes laziness with brutal and embarrassing failure. This game can be rage inducing. It is one of the few games that can really just crush me and rile me up. There is nothing worse, than having everything go perfectly, only to watch your entire run crumble in an instant when something unpredictable happens and you’re helplessly caught in the crossfire. As an example, I was in the Ice Caves, the games third area, and I was doing quite well. I had plenty of health, and all the items I could ask for to make my run easier. Unfortunately a certain type of enemy in the Ice Caves explodes upon death, and the debris from this explosion can actually hurt you. I knew this, but had no reason to assume an enemy off screen would land on a land-mine, die, and be jettisoned across the level. And then explode sending debris into me, causing me to fly back and slide across the ice, off of a platform, and then fall to my doom.
My entire run, destroyed. It took me thirty minutes to get where I was. And it crumbled in a 600th of the time. I didn’t play for awhile after that…
But don’t let this deter you. Spelunky might be hard, and… honestly there is no ‘might’ - it is hard. and does not apologize for it. But that’s the allure of this game.
It’s hard, and mean. But damnit, you’re a badass if you can beat it.
The nerve wrackingly high stakes are what make it so great. Really. If you want to get your adrenaline pumping, get to the later sections of a Spelunky run, and start dealing with the traps, enemies, and obstacles this game throws at you. I have been playing video games for nineteen years. This game is up there as one of the most heart pounding.
Spelunky is one of the many games that falls into the Rogue-like genre.  It has a procedurally generated world - meaning it is random every time. You start off with the bare minimum needed to succeed, and are thrust into a world hell bent on murdering you and laughing at your corpse.
Sounds fun, right?
Right...?
It shouldn’t be difficult to tell that I love hard games. I have put hundreds of hours into the Monster Hunter and Souls games, Ninja Gaiden, Dragon’s Dogma and many others. So it should be no surprise that I love games like Spelunky. Games that present steep challenges to overcome using their particular rule sets.
And that defines Spelunky perfectly. It’s a game of rules. Once you learn it’s rules, you can excel. Everything acts and reacts in a particular way. That eventually can be easier to predict and react to. Although there will always be those strange outliers where the stars align and you shoot an alien with your shotgun, it explodes and one of the chunks hits a landmine. Causing it to explode sending a rock flying at you, hitting you in the chest, sending you careening backward off of a platform. Falling onto a yeti who then throws you into a wall causing you to bounce off said wall back towards the yeti who then throws you into the same wall locking you into an eternity of pain and suffering, crushing your spirit and ending your life.
But hey, it makes for a hilarious story.
The game also has a great amount of depth, with a shockingly large amount of random “event” and hidden levels for you to find. As well as a very hard to unlock “secret” end boss that requires you to play through the game perfectly in order to attempt to beat him. I have made it to him once or twice in probably 500+ attempts. But, once you make it there. You can do it again. Spelunky is one of those games that, once you understand how it works, it seeps into your bones. You might be out of practice, but the game has conditioned you to play in a particular style that will reap success even if you’re not on your A game.
as an example of the depth and difficulty, here is what is needed in order to get to the ‘secret boss’:
-Be warned! If you don’t want to know specifics, skip the next few paragraphs.-
In the Mines (the games first area) you must find two items, a key and a chest. Inside the chest is the Ujad Eye, needed to find a hidden level in the Jungle (area two). These two items are in one of the Mine’s four levels. If you miss it you can still progress towards the secret area, but it becomes significantly more difficult.
In the Jungle you use the Eye to locate the entrance to Black Market, which is filled with items. In the black market there is the Ankh. This item is necessary for your advancement. Without it the secret area is locked out. Period. It costs 50k gold, a very large sum of money. Or... If you don’t possess the money, you can always kill the NPCs in the area and steal it (at your own risk!). But make sure you don’t die, as the Ankh will break and Revive you. But, this stops your progress because you need the Ankh for later!
Now in the third area, the Ice Caves, there is a large Moai Head, with which you cannot normally interact. However, if you have the Ankh, and die on the level it is present in, it will revive you within the Head. Giving you the Hedjet. One of the most important items in the process.
Now with the Hedjet, you need to get to the Temple. The games fourth area. In the Temple, you need to find Anubis (always on level 4-1) and kill him, and take his Scepter. NOW, with the Scepter, you need to get to the City of Gold, an optional area only available if you have the Hedjet, and the Scepter.
Once in the City of Gold, you have to kill Anubis again, and steal the Necronomicon.
NOW, you then have to beat Olmec, the game’s ‘Final Boss’... and make sure you kill him in the right spot, because you then use him as a platform to enter Hell.
The games ‘secret’ and true final area. Only accessible with the Necronomicon. Which is only available with the Scepter and Hedjet.. which can only be gotten if you use the Ankh in the right level… Yeah…
Now that you’ve made it to Hell, you have to ACTUALLY MAKE IT to the Final level, 5-4, and fight Yama, the king of the underworld.
As if getting to him wasn’t hard enough, now you actually have to kill him.
I haven’t been able to pull it off myself… But damn if it isn’t a rush when you get there.
-Spoilers over!-
I know it sounds like a lot, BUT what I laid out in the last few paragraphs is really more of an endgame objective. But it truly is very fun to try and strive for. Each time seeing yourself improve, getting just a little further with every attempt. Until finally you routinely make it to hell and kill Yama on the Daily Challenge without breaking a sweat…
I can understand why games like spelunky are intimidating. However, if you go into it with the right attitude I think that anyone can enjoy it.
This game is amazing, and I recommend it to anyone who enjoys a good challenge.
Yeah it might sound impossible, but it really isn’t. It’s one of those games that every time you die “One more run!” plays in your head. And then two hours go by and you didn’t even realize it.
Spelunky is well worth the effort it requires you put into it!

South Park's sequel to the previous game, the Stick of Truth is a phenomenal successor and an amazing experience through and through. As a long time fan of the previous game, I was overfilled and overjoyed with expectations for this one, and the expectations have been met brilliantly.
Much like the 1st game, the turn based combat is really enjoyable with the addition of 3 companions as well as a tileset mechanic, ultimates as well as a multi class functionality allowing you to pick your own moveset.
It's great, it's funny, it's fun.  South Park humor is subjective to people who might enjoy the direction of the show itself, however as a game it is remarkably well made, and it is really enjoyable.  It's really worth noting that much like the 1st game, the game plays like an actual 20 hour long episode of South Park, flawlessly executed.
Story wise the game takes a more Marvel VS DC theme rather than Stick of Truth's Dungeons and Dragons/Game of Thrones theme. It's quite amazing to see how a game about kids roleplaying can be so captivating and astonishing.  Matt Stone and Trey Parker nailed this one exceptionally much like the 1st one.
The game CAN suffer from occasional glitches revolving around the camera itself, as well as a startup screen being blacked out which can easily be fixed with Alt+Enter.
If you enjoyed the Stick of truth, or like South Park, even if just remotely, I highly encourage you to play this and Stick of Truth if you haven't.

Traps, monsters and environmental hazards block your way through a bunch of different worlds, as you descend deeper into randomly generated areas. The game is extremely difficult. Super Crate Box is a 2D platformer arcade game. Your objective is to collect as many crates as possible, while using any and every gun you have to kill the enemies falling from the ceiling. Everytime you grab a crate, you gain one more point and receive a new random weapon that you have unlocked. Each weapon is unique, fun and has its own reasons for use. Guns have unlimited ammo and deal different amounts of damage to the enemies. For example. Pistols take about 2 or 3 shots to kill the standard enemy of Super Crate Box, but an explosion from the rocket launcher is a one hit kill.
The way enemies move in this game is in a simple left and right motion. They continue to walk in the same direction until they come across a wall, then they will turn and move in the opposite direction as they make their way down the map towards a fire pit at the bottom. If an enemy makes its way to the pit of fire, they won't die, they will just fall throught the ceiling again. However, they will be angry allowing them to move twice as fast making for a adrenaline pumping challenge as you continue to collect crates and receive weapons.
There are three different enemies in this game. one you may already know is the small green guy, but there are larger green enemies that take two times the damage to kill. Finally there are floating skulls that fly around and also make their way down to the bottom of the map. The effects that fire has on enemies is the same for all three.
The game itself is addicting due to the fact that you must collect a number of crates to unlock new weapons, new characters, and new maps. You start with a fair weapon arsenal and will gain more guns as you play and develope your skills. Every game you start, you will have a random character picked for you, and every time you die you will have a new player modle. With this fact alone you will almost want to die just so you can see the new silly modles the game has in store for you. You start on a simple map with nothing much to see, but as you unlock more maps (three in total) you will find there to be more platforms to jump on and die on. The unlockible content is great, but if you find yourself playing with friends, you will be more worried about getting that amazing high score just to rub it in their face.
Super Crate Box is almost like flappy bird. Fun, addicting, and will make even the most calm and collected people burst into anger.

There's contrived puzzles (why would someone build a bridge like that), but for the most part that's easy to ignore -- especially since the game is short and doesn't repeat puzzles endlessly.
You are frequently holding both triggers and moving the sticks, so this game could trigger your RSI. I took a bunch of breaks and was okay.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is an inventive unique game, not to mention a work of art. The most difficult thing about this game is controlling 2 characters at the same time, which you
need a controller to play as. But once you get used to the mindtwisting that is required the game is rather easy. That was my main problem with the game, it simply was too easy (for me). Brothers also goes for the heartstrings
. I personally felt the tug of the emotions because I have a little brother, in fact when I refered to the characters in my head I used mine and my brother's names. The one detractor to this is the unintelligible dialogue, which is intentional.
But that is all the bashing I can do about the game. The in-game music  is brilliant and compliments the visuals and the emotional scenes perfectly. And the visuals, holy mackerel. This game is an artistic jewel, if anything just buy the game to watch it. The style and the presentation will stun you, some of the shots belong in a frame at an art display.
While I may have been able to quickly overcome the difficulty of controlling two characters at once, that fact in of itself is reason enough to buy the game on sale. But compound the emotionality, the music, and the visuals on top of that, and buying this 4 hour game at full price is worth it.

Tekken 7 made me a believer in the series. I grew up playing Virtua Fighter. Back in the day for 3d arcade fighters there was Virtua Fighter 1 first then Tekken. I played Virtua Fighter only, I brought a Sega Saturn to have Virtua Fighter. I never gave Tekken that much of a try. When I did...I disliked it because it felt different than VF. The last Tekken I played was Tekken 3 on PSX. I brought into the hype, got a PSX and Tekken 3 and found myself wishing that I didn't. Wishing that I saved all of that money to play VF3 at the arcades.
I didn't play Tekken 4, 5, 6, TT or TT2. When I seen Tekken 7 was going to come out on pc, I thought should I give it another try? Nah.....I was never a fan of the series. But then again....it does look awesome. A fighting game buddy convinced me to just give it a try so I took the plunge again. This time around I found myself loving it. The controls, the movement, how fluid the game just feels. I began to think....was I wrong all of these years? Just maybe!
The game is unbelievable, I'm still getting into it. VF and Doa (since it plays a lot like VF) were the games I would play. So I'm still adjusting to converting to Tekken. Its going to be a long road, but I'm enjoying the game so much that getting bodied never felt so good and rewarding.
The game is filled with content for those who care for that thing. Since I'm not into single player content much but the competitive experience that stuff doesn't really concern me. But none the less its great to have for those who do. The only real flaw that I have run into is with the game lobbies. There is no way to adjust the amount of sets you play nor is there a rematch option. So after a match you return to the lobby over and over again. Its a time waster and quite annoying. Hopefully they implement a rematch for lobbies or at the very least allow the player to adjust the amount of sets that are played.
The netcode is also super smooth, it feels like I'm playing offline. Its absolutely amazing.
With no Virtua Fighter 6 in sight, I will say with out a doubt that Tekken 7 is king of 3D fighters with no competition to that title. Is it worth the price? Hell yeah it is. Namco did a outstanding job bringing the series to pc for the first time. I say with confidence now that I'm a believer in the series and wish I would of put more time into it long ago.

Tekken 7 Fated Retribution heavily falls short on the plotline elements and its cliché writing. But remarkably overshadows it with a rock solid roster and gameplay mechanics that is polished to the core. It is a must own fighting game of this generation.

The difficulty of two people working together without a shared is enforced by the camera, which will always rotate to have the left-hand controlled brother on the left side of the screen. The right eye provides the visual information. The two halves of the brain are forced to work apart from each other instead of controlling a single entity. This is an incredible solution, adding depth and character to an engaging game and story.

So, I had previously made a rather negative review of Grand Theft Auto V made in the midst of all of the OpenIV drama. I was not best pleased, so I decided to rewrite it - the review is still negative because any critism I gave Take Two Interactive back then still applies now.
Let me explain, I have no issue with Rockstar Games - infact, they seem to be rather supportive of modding their games, and have in the past featured mods on their Newswire site. The issue is with T2, and their ideology of sales over what the consumer desires. In Grand Theft Auto V, this is apparent through the ludicrious Shark Card scheme - which by this point has become a requirement for anyone wanting to have anything nice on GTA Online. It is also apparent with the OpenIV resolution, T2 took a big L and decided that their decision was going to hurt them.
See how I've been able to get by without mentioning that OpenIV didn't even support what T2 suggested (allowing for online modifications) so far? That really is a shocking indicator of how T2 acts. But to suggest that this was any suprise is utter nonsense - T2 having sent cease and decist letters to the authors of alternate online modifications for GTAV a few years back.
---
As far as the actual game goes, its pretty good - okay story, very nice graphics. Online has become pretty awful has time has gone by, requiring either hundreds of hours game time to get money to have fun - or hundreds of pounds spent to have fun. It certaintly started off nice, I was one playing online as they released the X360 update.
Note that I said the story was only 'okay' - I say this as the story is nice, but doesn't really feel like a classic GTA title. For the money, and the story - Grand Theft Auto San Andreas is a much more viable option IMO. Considering the two share the same fictional (although different in interpretation) worlds, there are things that don't really add up for me - such as how the Ballas took over Grove Street, in the continued existance of 'The Families' - or even how 'The Families' could become a thing, CJ having really turned on every gang in Los Santos at some point for territory. All of these unanswered questions ontop the ♥♥♥♥♥ier map, I find that San Andreas is a more enjoyable game - try doing a master save if you've got some spare time :p.
In closing, I will note that I may have some inaccuracies regarding the 'The Families' and Grove Street, as its been a while since I last played through the GTAV story - which is steadily becoming the better half of GTAV. Frankly, T2 have put me off purchasing any of their new games - I won't be getting RDR2 - I'll stick to their just-as-good or even-better older titles, when they actually put the consumer first (or atleast not as close to last as they do now).

Fair enough the engine might not be made for intense gore like others but when I completely annihilate the skull of a rather happy fellow I expect his face to at least fall off or be changed in some way but nope, he still has his happy face.
The "stealth" was...questionable. When playing on Sniper Elite, I expect to be spotted when literally in front of someone but for some reason I was able to walk right past. Overall, I disliked the game but it was fun to shoot something.

Look, it's Mortal Kombat.  It plays like MK, it looks like MK, if you liked the previous MK, you will probably like this one because it's more of the same.  All in all, there is a lot of fun to be had in here.  Read on for details.
This is a console port, a rather crude one at that.  There aren't many graphics settings to tweak, so you may need to adjust things from your NVidia or AMD Catalyst control panel to get it running 100% smoothly.  I had no issues, but I do have a very high-end system so YMMV.  I did not experience any framerate issues in the game.  The only crash I do still get, is if I try to remap controls from the main menu, which crashes to the desktop.  If I start a match, hit pause and remap from that screen, it works fine.  I have not had any other crashes.
The graphics are a bit sharper and more detailed during fights, but the cut-scenes look like mush because they were carried over from the console version (PS4/XB1).  They would look a thousand times better if they were done in real-time on our modern GPUs, but meh...  They still get the story across, and while I have not yet completed the story mode, they flesh out a lot of the characters' history, so longtime fans of the franchise will enjoy playing through it.  Playing the single player mode also unlocks a bunch of stuff for each character, so it's well worth playing at least once.
Like previous games, you earn "koins" to spend in the "krypt", unlocking concept art, videos/music and other bonus content.  They also brought back the concept of challenge towers (like in MK3), and the good ol' "Test Your Might" button-mash bonus round.  There is a LOT of content packed in here, with heaps of unlockables.
Extra bonus: If you have an NVidia Shield, this game runs flawlessly on it!  Mortal Kombat on the go ?  Why the hell not :)
So in recap, it's not without flaws, but it is most certainly playable and they have already resolved many issues in the first week.  If you're an MK fan, I highly recommend it.

Both S.T.A.L.K.E.R Shadow of Chernobyl and Call of Pripyat (which I purchased on disc upon release) were great gaming experiences. While not quite on par with Fallout 3's more detailed open world that is rich with quests, however, the STALKER franchise nevertheless offers a dark, gritty alternative for dystopian dreamers. By now, it has achieved something of a cult status amongst gamer circles.
Clear Sky is a bold yet flawed attempt at portraying a prequel to Shadow of Chernobyl's storyline. This time, the player takes the role of Scar - a mercenary currently employed by the titular Clear Sky faction. During the adventure, it's possible for Scar to form allegiances with a few other factions such as Duty and Freedom. But Clear Sky was the only new offering thrown into an all-too familiar mix, the rest was old ground previously covered in SOC. It's possible to complete side missions on behalf of friendly/netural factions, yet sadly these often had glitchy and absurd times in which to complete, such as defending a camp against mutants or bandits. Often I'd barely received such a request before the annoying 'Task Failed' popped up ten seconds later!
The combat aspect of STALKER is commendable, yet in Clear Sky I felt that the developers had raised the difficulty bar that bit too high. COS was challenging, yet this I found just too damn frustrating. I'm a seasoned shooter but really struggled all the way to the bitter end. If it's a mistake I've made then fair enough, but when enemies are deadly accurate, magically shoot through objects, survive bullets at point blank, and can 'sense' when I'm trying to heal then it's no longer enjoyable. Word of warning: stock up on med-kits and bandages! The final battle in pursuit of my target could only be described as a brutal experience. The AI can be a cruel companion in Clear Sky. What's worse, there's no way to lower difficulty to a more tolerable level.
As in SOC, Clear Sky boasted some fantastic firearms which worked well enough, yet it would have been nice to introduce a few extra goodies to play with - and there's whole arsenal of real world machine guns and pistols around to draw inspiration from. Again, Clear Sky fell flat by refusing to explore fresh ground in the armanents section. Perhaps even different types of grenade would have been fun?  As before, weapons deteriorate and jam over time, so it's wise to visit a technician to repair or even upgrade weapons and armour. Technicians were introduced in Clear Sky and, providing they have the money, players are now able to improve and/or modifiy equipment to their own preference. This welcome gem of gameplay was brought over to the more successful Call of Pripyat. Certain missions involve retrieving upgrade plans which can be implented later.
STALKER: Clear Sky boasts some superb maps detailing varied terrain: swamps, forest, grassland, deserted villages. For a certain amount money Scar can employ the services of a guide (a sort of fast-travel option) to save on gameplay time. I can't remember if there were any new anomalies, but overall certainly not so frequent as in SOC, and therefore resulting artifacts are few and far between. In SOC I enjoyed artifact hunting and selling them for huge amounts of cash, so I keenly felt their lacking during Clear Sky. In one sense, I understand the developers were attempting to cap repetitive ease of investment and have the player keep their money in reserve for repairs and such. But I'm sure purchases in Clear Sky were much more expensive than in SOC.  Having said that, the 'food' aspect was never once observed (rarely so in SOC) and merely rendered pointless. Something that Fallout: New Vegas hardcore mode harshly yet satisfyingly implemented. It's a shame STALKER didn't take the hunger element seriously.
Overall, I consider this a very average FPS lacking the character and charm of SOC or COP (the latter was released sometime later). STALKER Clear Sky is often regarded as a flawed part of the franchise without anything much new to contribute. The main storyline is not as engaging when compared to its bigger brothers, and what's annoying it really should have been an excitable sibling.

Tekken 7 made me a believer in the series. I grew up playing Virtua Fighter. Back in the day for 3d arcade fighters there was Virtua Fighter 1 first then Tekken. I played Virtua Fighter only, I brought a Sega Saturn to have Virtua Fighter. I never gave Tekken that much of a try. When I did...I disliked it because it felt different than VF. The last Tekken I played was Tekken 3 on PSX. I brought into the hype, got a PSX and Tekken 3 and found myself wishing that I didn't. Wishing that I saved all of that money to play VF3 at the arcades.
I didn't play Tekken 4, 5, 6, TT or TT2. When I seen Tekken 7 was going to come out on pc, I thought should I give it another try? Nah.....I was never a fan of the series. But then again....it does look awesome. A fighting game buddy convinced me to just give it a try so I took the plunge again. This time around I found myself loving it. The controls, the movement, how fluid the game just feels. I began to think....was I wrong all of these years? Just maybe!
The game is unbelievable, I'm still getting into it. VF and Doa (since it plays a lot like VF) were the games I would play. So I'm still adjusting to converting to Tekken. Its going to be a long road, but I'm enjoying the game so much that getting bodied never felt so good and rewarding.
The game is filled with content for those who care for that thing. Since I'm not into single player content much but the competitive experience that stuff doesn't really concern me. But none the less its great to have for those who do. The only real flaw that I have run into is with the game lobbies. There is no way to adjust the amount of sets you play nor is there a rematch option. So after a match you return to the lobby over and over again. Its a time waster and quite annoying. Hopefully they implement a rematch for lobbies or at the very least allow the player to adjust the amount of sets that are played.
The netcode is also super smooth, it feels like I'm playing offline. Its absolutely amazing.
With no Virtua Fighter 6 in sight, I will say with out a doubt that Tekken 7 is king of 3D fighters with no competition to that title. Is it worth the price? Hell yeah it is. Namco did a outstanding job bringing the series to pc for the first time. I say with confidence now that I'm a believer in the series and wish I would of put more time into it long ago.

Dead Rising 2: Off The Record is basically a spin-off of Dead Rising 2's story, but with some minor changes here and there on how it progresses.
And even though the story and cutscenes are basically unchanged from the original game, Off The Record has some new content to offer, such as:
- New weapons, new combo weapons, new clothes, new food items, new psychopaths, a new place to explore, a new ending and some rebalancing;
- All the DLC from Dead Rising 2 is already included;
- The re-addition of cameras so you can take pictures and share them with your co-op buddies;
- A checkpoint system to remove even further the necessity of loading old save files;
- Even more zombies on screen and some other minor graphical changes.
(These changes actually make this one a bit more demanding than the original game, so make sure you've got a good CPU to run it.);
- And last but not least, the "Sandbox Mode". This replaces the "Terror is Reality" game mode from Dead Rising 2.
Sandbox Mode has absolutely no time limits, so you can do whatever you feel like doing!
It also adds challenges for you to complete alone or with a friend, crazy survivors that attack you, and occasionally a psychopath will spawn just to keep things fresh.
You're also able to share your progress directly with Story Mode, so if you're having a hard time progressing through some missions, you can just level up in Sandbox Mode and then go back to the main game.
If you loved Dead Rising 2 and want more out of it or you just never even touched a game from the series, then this is certainly for you.
But if you're looking for a completely different experience, then you might just pass on this one.

I am confused about this game. The critical reviews are overwhelmingly positive, stating that it's superior to The Stick of Truth in every way, but I couldn't disagree more and that is very disappointing.
The story-line is largely dull and though there are a few laughs here and there, the writing is much weaker than the previous game. The cast of playable characters is much, much bigger, but the consequence of this is that each of them gets remarkably little time to say or do anything particularly memorable.
This is clearly a poor console port. The controls are odd in places to say the least, particularly the toilet challenges, to the point where your inputs are simply not registered - which cuts you off from successfully completing part of the content you paid for.
Crafting is good, but the downside of this is that it makes 70% of loot drops redundant and worthless as you will almost always have artifacts that are superior that you personally made than what you were rewarded with for defeating a boss or completing a challenge. This makes the achievement of success a bit lacklustre.
The battle system is better than The Stick of Truth, but frustrating in a few ways. You are only able to attack in one parallel axis with the vast majority of attacks. I'm not sure why we're not able to attack from the vertical axis given the vast amount of freedom we now enjoy in combat.
The music is weaker than the previous game and is not memorable. I would imagine that most people can recall without having to think terribly hard what the battle tunes were in The Stick of Truth - I can't do that with clarity for this game.
The game has quite a few bugs that absolutely should not be present given how long the game was in production and for how long the delays were before release. The most common example of this is that the game has a tendency in places to soft-lock during combat or following a loading screen. I also experienced a black screen at one point, where the game continued to run in the background, but I could not see where by characters were navigating to - forcing me to hard reset the game without being able to save. Mount and Blade Warband is one of my all time favorite games. I have more than 500 hours on record with this game (my third highest on Steam after Rust and Civilization V).
Players take control of an adventurer just arrived in the world of Caladria. On the battlefield, you directly control and fight with this character. You're also the leader of a warband, and so you can hire other soldiers to fight for you as well.
In the game, you move your warband around a strategic map of Caladria. Whenever a battle starts or you enter a location, that scene loads and you take direct command of your character and issue orders to your soldiers.
There's no set objective in the game. You begin with nothing and have the option to work your way up and become a king (if you want to know how to be king, check out my video).
The game is fun and addicting. The storyline of the lone adventurer becoming king of all Caladria feels immersive and compelling. Battles are very fun, though the actual tactics of commanding your troops is very light (certainly nothing like Total War). In most battles, you will simply move your troops together up to the enemy, order them to attack all at once, and then not issue any further orders. Since you do need to control and fight with your own character, this level of tactics is probably appropriate.
The biggest downside to the game is that it can get grindy. You'll fight a lot of the same battles over and over just to level up your character and troops and earn money. The game is fun enough and the story line you create yourself is immersive enough that you probably won't really care right away.
There are wonderful mods for this game as well, many of which can reduce the grind. As someone who normally doesn't like mods, I really don't think there's much point playing this game unmodded. In my video review, I have my mod recommendations.
If you haven't picked up this game yet, you should. It's a classic.

You like Minecraft's building system?
You like the combat system of Zelda with a touch of Dark Souls in it?
Then GET.THIS.GAME!
Portal Knights is- as you might've guessed- a game with an open world sandbox that has a very nice action combat coming with little RPG elements here and there.
You start out on a rather peaceful island that gives you a checklist of stuff to do to teach you the very basics of the game,
which works very well if I may mention that!
But once you advance from that point, you're greeted with a set of numerous islands which all represent different biomes.
Different biomes meaning different enemies and different resources- both for building and fighting.
So you're bound to explore more to discover and achieve more.
It's very nicely balanced on the resource factor, while the combat part is still very easy- to me at least.
The further you progress, the harder it gets.
And on every 10th-ish island you visit, you may stumble upon a boss fight.
The bosses feel very Zelda like, all having their own mechanics on how to beat them.
The bosses themselves aren't really hard, but it's nice to see how well the combat system is working along.
But don't think you can just stand there and defend from whatever the game throws at you!
Instead of giving you a shield, the game gives you a quick dodgeroll, which you can and have to use to avoid incoming attacks.
It keeps you own your toes and if you don't pay attention, you will get mauled by multiple enemies at once.
Now, from the combat and exploration part, down to the building!
I'm honestly surprised by the options the game gives you in this very early state.
Speaking of an early beta range, Portal Knights offers you lots of room for building and decoration.
Those who are unexperienced get greeted with some ruins of older buildings here and there, which they can either restore and make themselves at home, or take inspiration (and building material) to make your very own creation.
For those who are experienced architects on block basis (like me), there's still quite some stuff to play around with.
I for one, have built myself some cottages here and there, some castles, and even own dungeons, putting lots of detail in every single one of them.
And that's not even the start.
But wait- Multiplayer?
NEVER been easier.
Upon starting your game, either loading one up or starting new, you can set your game to private, friends only, or invitations only.
Meaning, when you start your game, you're given the choice to play by yourself, or host a game for free, for which you can adjust the settings for your friends to be able to join whenever they'd like, or you being the bouncer of your game by having the power to invite people to it, for them to be able to join.
Quick, handy, just what I want from a Multiplayer in this kind of game.
It's true, the game isn't very big yet, and it is really easy, but the developers are always happy to receive suggestions and they are always working on it.
You can feel the love that is put into the game with every single update you witness, if you have played it already.
For newcomers, the same goes to you.
Kudos to 505 games on this point.
They put the right people on the right game to make it evergrowing, while including the community to a reasonable, well weighed out extent.
This game gets a 8/10 from me, because what it does, it does damn good.
And room for improvement is always on it's way to getting used to every last bit.
Grab this game, guys.
Damn sure worth it.

BOSS战，大战蜘蛛精…. 通过弟弟把蜘蛛撞翻，然后哥哥把蜘蛛的腿一根一根掰断的合作方式（还觉得这是卡通么 :D），他们杀死了蜘蛛。但是哥哥被弥留的蜘蛛最后一击击穿了腹部，失血过多。。。尼玛要不要这么狗血。。。哥哥你别死啊T T
打败了蜘蛛之后，弟弟搀扶着哥哥来到了一个人间仙境的地方，于是这里就是生命之树了_(:з」∠)_ 弟弟去取了救命的水..但是下来的时候哥哥还是因为失血过多死了… 一口老血
你以为哥哥挂了就是最虐的地方了？图样，这个游戏丧心病狂的地方开始了…. 这才是我真正被surprise到的地方…
在弟弟伏在哥哥身上哭的时候，天上很应景的下起了瓢泼大雨(the-sky-is-crying-cliche)，但是镜头一转，哥哥活了？
但镜头又一转，哥哥还是面色苍白地躺着，抱着自己的哥哥只是弟弟的幻想。
我不会告诉你，刚才老奸巨猾的我居然相信了！！哎还是被这个卡通的画风给欺骗了，也是看过太多假死了所以想着”怎么可能死嘛他们可是兄弟这个作品就叫双子传说你让他们死一个这爬山都爬不上去还怎么愉快地当跑酷少年了你这是在逗我？“。
这还没完，接下来，你需要操作痛不欲生的弟弟亲手埋葬哥哥，当你拖着弟弟小小的缓慢的身躯一点点用土把哥哥的尸体盖上的时候。。。。尼玛你还能再虐一点？
然后弟弟带着能救老爸命的水回到了故乡，原以为三段式中的第二段已经结束的我，又一次被证明了图样。之前在开篇的时候提到，很多操作需要两个人共同完成。其中一个很重要的梗我没有提：弟弟不敢游泳。因为目睹了母亲溺水而亡，所以弟弟对水能避则避。全作中俩人不曾分开，如果需要游泳都是哥哥在游，弟弟都是用手搂住哥哥的脖子挂在他身后，如果松开弟弟的操作键他就只会在水里不停地挣扎然后喊”Naia, Naia..”
弟弟回到家的晚上暴雨交加，为了在父亲挂掉之前、把哥哥以命换来的救命药水按时给父亲喝下去，他必须要自己走完剩下的路。其中就包括了：自己一个人游泳，开以前只有哥哥能开得动的机关，自己跳上以前有哥哥在下面当人肉垫子的高墙…..
玩到需要弟弟一个人游泳的时候我觉得有点不可思议，因为我用右手操作弟弟行动的时候他还是一个人在河里挣扎然后大声喊哥哥的名字。后来，机智如我，我就加上了左手哥哥的操作（虽然我以为左手的操作在哥哥挂掉之后就相当于无用了，这又一次被打脸），结果！！！弟弟就非常勇猛地一个人刷刷刷地游过去了，也可以跳上高墙和搬动机关了！！！
这是何等巧妙而又虐心的操作设计！！！期间音效和音乐还不忘补刀，音乐催泪也就罢了，音效是哥哥的声音不停地回荡、回荡、回荡…. 一直在鼓励着弟弟走完最后的路，救回他们的老爸。
最后弟弟在内心中感受到哥哥的鼓励下小宇宙爆发的这一段，又虐又燃。标准三段式的第二段，哥哥没能回来，弟弟在怀念哥哥的过程中，完成了自己的成长和独立。
最后不枉兄弟俩的辛苦，老爸成功康复。标准剧情三段式的最后一段，本该是一家人其乐融融的HE，却因为缺了哥哥而不能称之为HE。（其实这种挂了一个的结局大部分人都认为是BE了..）

I bought Deponia during a Steam Sale because it looked like a cute game and I haven't played a point-and-click styled game since I was a kid.  Boy, I was in for it when I started playing Deponia.
This game is really tricky.  "Tricky" meaning that it's difficult to know exactly what to do all the time.  Some tasks are easy to figure out while others are extremely random.  Often, I was stuck wondering how anyone could have figured out what to do without exhausting every possible option beforehand.  However, I liked this aspect of the game because if it was too easy, you would be able to finish it pretty quickly.  If you are an achievement hunter, this game is pretty easy to 100% with some help from gamesaves and/or backtracking.
Another thing I liked about this game was the art.  I really liked the different areas and animations of the game.  I enjoyed discovering new areas and going into all the rooms, ect.
The story line was alright, I was curious enough to keep playing it but not curious enough to purchase the sequel.  What really killed this game was the characters.  Although Rufus changed a bit towards the end, his personality in the beginning really put me off.  I almost found the game unplayable with his ever constant nagging about literally everything, and the way he talked about and viewed women.  There were likable characters in the game, but Rufus took a dump on all of them and made some pretty mean jokes.  Maybe his character in the sequel improves and this is all just about his ~*~character development~*~, but I wouldn't purchase the sequel at full price after listening to him for one game.

I enjoyed this game tremendously even though it's obviously got some lacking elements. I love stealth and sniping, and this game has plenty of both. It does surprise me that after 2 years, the DLC has a) not really been reduced in price, and b) apparently has hardly ever been seen based on the number of reviews of it. I'd pick them up just to have more fun with the game, but until the trio of mission-based DLC come down to maybe the price of one of them, that's off my list.
Now: the good stuff!
I enjoy the variety of fighting though I almost always find myself defaulting to my 'stealth, snipe, whoops - kill everything in sight, wait for enemies to relax, repeat' mode. I don't mind that at all, though I suspect some find it too repetitive. The locations are really nice and I would love to have a way to remove the UI and get first person in there, just for screenshot purposes.
Killing fascists is always - ALWAYS - on my list of things to do. ALWAYS. There's a kind of satisfaction that comes from it that is kind of ... a guilty(?) pleasure.
I found myself more and more liking the little bit of actual story we have - nice touches to the character even though he's mostly a blank slate (I didn't even know that his name was Karl... lol, because they don't actually SAY it anywhere). Plus his voice. mmm. His voice.
Good musical cues, though at times the music overshadows any other sounds.
Overall very easy and intuitive to play, though I still hate third person motion quite a bit, but that's on me not the game.
The less good:
I really want to be able to jump and explore. Unfortunately that just doesn't happen. However on the plus side of this is that the numerous ways you CAN explore the areas to complete your goals are a lot of fun.
The sound editing is crappy, in that there's zero stereo sound cues, and that means in trying to hear directionally it's impossible to determine any locations of enemies. The chat that occasionally shows up is also weirdly triggered, because I'd already killed a number of enemies and then went through their chat trigger... so... a room full of dead guys and they're talking. O.o
Virtually no story. Now, I'll give this one a pass because I didn't really get the game to have a story, I got it so I could shoot bad guys with a sniper rifle. :)
Way too short. However also this gets a pass from me because the replay value is very strong, and the challenges pad the mission length. I don't play multiplayer so I probably won't get any of the other achievements or see any maps that might be mp exclusive, which is a bit of a shame.
I'd love to be able to interact with the environment much more than I do. I'd like to pick things up, climb, shimmy under things, etc, and explore to my hearts' content, but that's not why the character is where he is.
The .... bad?
Well I suppose the one thing I might say is that it's still too expensive and the DLC should be folded into one lower price point to actually sell it.
If you enjoy sniping and a variety of potential methods for doing the same 8 missions and challenge maps, highly recommend. Pick it up on sale, imo.

I loved Stalker SoC and CoP and finished both several times. But Clear Sky has just too many flaws. First the difficulty is quite high, what I usually like. But it`s not high because the enemies are very clever. They are not dumb either and gun fights can be really fun, when you are not pushed in the line of fire by a NPC or because even simple bandits see you in the dark while you can`t even see the weapon in your hand. They will shoot you from far far away with their rusty pistols. The problem is you can`t skip the night, so you have to wait for an hour realtime(!) or so untill it becomes day or you will die even more often than you already do during daytime. And then the controls: Awful! Who ever came up with the idea that you actually have two kinds of crouching from which one is such a small change to your standing position, that it`s more or less useless and the other one is only possible to execute, when you are crouched in the first postion beforehand. Who ever invented this should be banned from making videos games for ever. So you die most often because of the crappy controls and poor design choices and not because of the smart enemies. Two examples for how bad the level design can be: The beginning of the game in the swamps. 1st. The Water is radioactive and will kill you, but because of the high grass, you can`t see it most of the time. So you just stare at the map ignoring 98% of the screen to make your way and try to follow the totaly random and confusing mission messeges which are popping up every few seconds. One second a mission starts "defend x" a second later (you had no chance to get there in time) " mission defedning x canceled" and you don`t even know why. So You run in the opposite direction (staring at the map) to do another mission like the first one. But then again the first mission popps up again: "defend x". And a few more seconds later these missions can be canceled again or fail without any chance to accomplish them.  At another point the game leads you to a spot out of a canal where you are supposed to start a mission in a new area, but there is no way to pass the MG-nest which lies between you and the area where you need to go. You are literary sitting in a trap , sourrounded by barbwire, while on the only open side the machinegun awaits to kill you in a split second. This is by far the worst level design I have seen in a game for a long time. For the whole game F5 and F9 will be your most used keys. You will look at the loading screen like alot. And that`s the reason why there is never a constant flow of gaming. There is no chance that Clear Sky developes an atmosphere like the one the other stalker games are known for. Post Apocalyptic Mayhem is one of those games where everything sounds good on paper, but the execution is lacking.
I guess this is supposed to be a racing game, but the arcade & challenge modes revolve around blowing up as many rivals as possible. This is accomplished by grabbing weapons off the track. Players can equip weapons for the front, sides, and rear. There's also a boost for catching up to the...mayhem. With a multitude of tracks and a variety of cars to drive, this game gets a pass in terms of content.
In practice though...ehhh...hmmm..oh uh well shoot. There's really no incentive for actually trying to race. The winner is determined solely by # of kills. At this point, why not just have a big arena? Make it a car combat game like the Twisted Metal series. Actually that wouldn't work because most of the weapons are designed for a racing game. It's a head-scratcher of the a design-decision, since it applies to the entirety of the single-player. There is a multiplayer mode for racing, but everyone is going to destroy each other anyway(or at least they would if anyone played this game online).
All that said, it isn't really a big deal. I'm just annoyed as hell because while playing the game I got hit with a nasty bug. At one point the game gets stuck on a loading screen. It stinks but it happens. I bring up the task manager, but the game pops right back up with its infinite loading. I try to bring up task manager again, and the loading screen comes right back. This freakin' game was trying to hold my computer hostage! I had to restart the PC just to get out of that mess. That little experience soured me on the entire game. As soon as everything was back to normal, I uninstalled this piece of crap with the quickness. I'm not saying it could happen to you, but what if it did?
I wasn't feelin' it anyway. The game isn't even compelling enough to grind out a few achievements for. The loading-screen bug was the 2x4 that broke the camel's back.

Look, it's Mortal Kombat.  It plays like MK, it looks like MK, if you liked the previous MK, you will probably like this one because it's more of the same.  All in all, there is a lot of fun to be had in here.  Read on for details.
This is a console port, a rather crude one at that.  There aren't many graphics settings to tweak, so you may need to adjust things from your NVidia or AMD Catalyst control panel to get it running 100% smoothly.  I had no issues, but I do have a very high-end system so YMMV.  I did not experience any framerate issues in the game.  The only crash I do still get, is if I try to remap controls from the main menu, which crashes to the desktop.  If I start a match, hit pause and remap from that screen, it works fine.  I have not had any other crashes.
The graphics are a bit sharper and more detailed during fights, but the cut-scenes look like mush because they were carried over from the console version (PS4/XB1).  They would look a thousand times better if they were done in real-time on our modern GPUs, but meh...  They still get the story across, and while I have not yet completed the story mode, they flesh out a lot of the characters' history, so longtime fans of the franchise will enjoy playing through it.  Playing the single player mode also unlocks a bunch of stuff for each character, so it's well worth playing at least once.
Like previous games, you earn "koins" to spend in the "krypt", unlocking concept art, videos/music and other bonus content.  They also brought back the concept of challenge towers (like in MK3), and the good ol' "Test Your Might" button-mash bonus round.  There is a LOT of content packed in here, with heaps of unlockables.
Extra bonus: If you have an NVidia Shield, this game runs flawlessly on it!  Mortal Kombat on the go ?  Why the hell not :)
So in recap, it's not without flaws, but it is most certainly playable and they have already resolved many issues in the first week.  If you're an MK fan, I highly recommend it.

Second, I have a high end PC, i5-2500k OC at 3.6 GHz and a GTX 970, so running this thing should be a breeze right? It did have its dips at Dying Light and GTA V but those are really graphic intensive and open world games so that shouldn't matter. In this case, this game is a fighting game. It should stay at 60 constant. Why am I hiccupping? I shouldn't even have performance issues at all. Not to mention frequent crashes.
Do yourself a favor. Do not buy this game until it is fixed. I gaurantee Streetfighter V and Tekken 7 will probably be a better port than this garbage.

Most of this game's infamous "challenge" derives simply from atrocious hit detection and controls (ESPECIALLY with the wall cling and picking up objects consistently and quickly), not to mention that your standard melee attack is laggier than ROBLOX running on an old Windows XP. Certainly doesn't help that the first area of the game is the most infuriating and nonsensical according to what I've heard fans of the game say, and I can't say I disagree based on my own experiences. You'll be flung into a bed of spikes by an arrow trap before you even know what happened, gunned down by a 12-gauge-wielding insane shopkeeper because a boulder happened to roll into his shop, killed by a
projectile, and blown to bits by nonchalantly nudging a box with a seemingly innocuous bit of rock debris all within the first few hours of the game. Lovely, that's
how I want to be introduced to this "gem." It's because of incidents like the aforementioned that I've uttered more expletives at Spelunky than any other Steam game in my library. But it's okay, the game
you to make these mistakes... yet there's virtually no room for error because you only have so much health throughout the whole game. Your whip's pis
s-poor range and slow attack speed will cause you to trade hits with enemies very often, which is something you simply can't afford to do in Spelunky. The minute you step into that cave, you're only 2 or 3 arrows traps or long falls away from GAME OVER. Oh, did I mention? There's fall damage in a 2-D platforming game! What a
conglomeration of design choices we have here.
It takes a very specific kind of person to get your money's worth out of, or even tolerate Spelunky. Maybe it's just me, but I can't play the game for more than an hour or so without promptly ragequitting and interrogating myself as to why I even booted up the game in the first place. Even if you're a fan of other rogue-likes (I use that term
loosely, considering this game can hardly even be considered a rogue-like as much as those devious Steam tags will try to convince you otherwise), there's no guarantee that you'll actually enjoy Spelunky. It's a crying shame, really, because if the controls just meshed with the mechanics better (see: wall-cling), Spelunky would probably be a pretty addicting and overall fantastic game, but it's because of the control that I simply can't recommend it to anyone. If you only take away one thing from this wall of text, then let it be this: If you're as morbidly curious as I was and want to know what the hype surrounding Spelunky is all about, then please, make sure you pick it up while it's on sale and you
just end up breaking even. Hell, don't even do that, just get the original freeware version. Sure, there's marginally less content to "enjoy," but you won't have that burning hole left in your wallet after you've put it down in exasperation. Otherwise, there are dozens of better examples of challenging 2-D platformers on Steam (Super Meat Boy - which, funnily enough, runs for the exact same price as Spelunky - springs to mind due to its tight controls and cogent gameplay), and if you're just looking for a fun rogue-like to keep you busy, you're much more likely get more enjoyment out of something like The Binding of Isaac and its remake, to which my 1,000+ hours of gameplay across both titles can attest (and I'm not even close to unlocking all the items in Rebirth, which also is up for the same price as Spelunky).

What can I say about Spelunky?
I bought this game a while ago, played it for a short amount of time and put it away again.  I kept dying, it seemed like they made the difficulty way too hard for a casual looking game.
I picked it up again a few days ago with the determination to get through the first world, to have a proper idea of what the game is about.  Now I understand!!
Spelunky
easy.  If you've played it, you'll know it isn't.  The great thing is though, there are no cheap deaths.  Death comes from player error.  There are WTF!?  moments, but these are shortly proceeded by newfound knowledge and understanding of a new tactic or strategy.  The amount of ways to die in Spelunky, I don't even try to imagine!
This maybe what makes it such a special platformer.  With procedural generated levels and the multitude of ways our hero can meet his end, each playthrough feels quite unique.  It never feels mundane or like a grind.  Any frustration from dying is short-lived and usually accompanied with laughter.
The graphics are lovely and colourful, with a plethora of cute characters to unlock.  There's a whole host of tough achievements and a nice variety of catchy soundtracks that compliment it all really well.

For a game that is about 4 hours, this game really exceeded all of my expectations. I didn't really know what to expect, honestly. From the beautiful lighting, sweeping mountain vistas, evening icy lakes with jumping whales and the northern lights, or a frozen landscape screwn with the bodies of fighting giants, this game, while linear like all platformers, still manages to feel vast, raw, and gave me the same sense of awe and emotional high that I got from exploring Skyrim. The fact that the world feels so epic and tied together speaks volumes about the talents of the game designers and the strength of the game mechanics. There is an emotional integrity and intensity to everything.
There were two spots where moving a platform via a crank took fooooorever. It was really annoying, and I kept picturing the Monty Python "Get on with it!" scene, but it only happens twice and it's not that big of a deal in the grand scheme of things. Maybe it was just the way I was turning it, but I tried all kinds of possible key strokes and just couldn't figure out a faster way. :) There are also points where navigating both brothers can be really wierd when moving them at the same time and they tend to zig zag occasionally, which eventually leads them to cross sides of the screen and damn is that confusing! This is to be expected, though, since you do have to control both characters 100% of the time. Luckily, some patience and just stopping and taking some time to admire the beautiful environments while you move each brother to the area that makes the most sense for you is all it takes to move forward. Thankfully, jumping over chasms is easy as the game does that for you as long as you just keep moving forward.
The world is exceptionally dangerous. There are massive scenes of death, hints of death (rivers of blood in one area), and other dangers all over the place. The environment is as beautiful as it is subtly violent. As a platformer, this game really shows how much the genre has progressed and matured over the years. Every puzzle fits perfectly within the context of the storyline and the environment. Because of this, the game feels longer and much more vast than it actually is. The Unreal Engine really shines here, as does the skill of the narration. Even though the game is not in English, the character's mannerisms, the music, and animations all come together to help you understand the story.
There are plenty of moments where you have to have the two characters work together, and that leads to moments where you discover something truly special and the game rewards for that via achievements. The two person mechanic is especially powerful near the end, almost brutal. Characters and other objects will react differently depending on if you use the older brother or the younger brother, with the younger brother generally being more mischevious and playful. Some characters respect well to that, others do not. This is a subtle but very important touch that really ties the concept of "two brothers" together, on par with the various puzzles.
The game does recommend playing with a gamepad. I used my keyboard, which strained my hands a few times while I played around with various angles for my hands, but you cannot create your own layouts as the game gives you pretty much nothing in terms of graphic and control customizations. Despite that, this is definitely a game I will play again and again, keyboard be damned! :D Just note that you do have you use your head a bit--there are no real hints about what to do but the environment is so strong that I felt everything was more or less self-explanatory, though still challenging.
Final summary: this is a game I will keep installed for a long while and play at least a few times over here and there.

They're in-engine, but I assume that prerenders reduce the testing required since they function the same on every system. It's awfully jarring if you're playing the game on a modern system, because they look worse than actual gameplay. Frank's character lacks the innocent charm that he had in the first game; he's now a cynical, self-aware middle-aged man who says one-liners rather than the cartoon paparazzi sociopath of the first game.
The mall itself is based around its casinos. Let's be honest, casinos aren't fun and they aren't relatable for most of us. Even if you've never been to a massive mall you can understand that finding survival items in shops - or just cool clothes or ineffectual weapons - is fun. Fortune City is approximately one-third casino.
There's a crafting system now. You mix different bits and make weapons from them. I can SORT OF understand the appeal of finding stuff in a shopping mall and finding ways to turn them into weapons, but it feels like a crazy extravagence and a complete waste of time when you have an exacting time limit to obey. Besides, finding the stuff that combines on an arbitrary basis isn't inherently interesting in the way that exploring the environment for items is.
If you want to play more Dead Rising and you've played the first game to completion, this is the best that you'll get. It retains the appeal of the first to some extent. I wonder how much influence the rich-dad beard-men at Capcom Vancouver had over this. It's infinitely better than 3 or 4, at least.

Deponia is the first game in the trilogy. I have yet to finish the other two games so I won't be comparing them to each other. I will however, compare this game to other games in the genre. Deponia is a great example of a rightful successor of much older games in the genre. It has great hand drawn art style, witty characters, fun events and mind boggling puzzles. It will truly be a challenge to finish this game without looking for help on google but if you manage to do it, you'll feel really great.
It's interesting to see these kinds of games in these times where point and click games have just turned into interactive stories with little to no failure state. Telltale games have "evolved" the genre in a way that is catered to a more casual audience who wants to experience the story without having to stop and think for a couple of hours in order to proceed with it. I'm not saying it's necessarily a bad thing, I'm just saying that it's sometimes nice to see a game that reminds us of older classics like "Tales of the Monkey island", "Sam and Max", "Grim Fandango", "Broken Sword" and so on..
Deponia also grants us with a wonderful story set in a very interesting junk-filled environment. I recommend this game to everyone who wants to experience said story in an old-school way where you will have to think and often get frustrated by the sheer silliness of the puzzles which you will have to complete in order to finish the adventure.

Guess I'll throw in my two cents as to why I can't play this game any more
1. It has just become an absolute grind fest, for anyone without hours of free time per day it's quite excessive, I don't necessarily hate the online aspect of it with a bit of grinding, however, I have played the ps3 version up till PC release and I can safely say I have noticed a couple changes that are definitely a massive negative.

1A. They've decreased money per mission, I remember doing rooftop rumble and getting 20K+ pretty decently every time, although it was grindy, it was a quicker method of getting money as opposed to long set up heists they added later or other missions that require much more time for not that much money in the long run. It's just essentially been done to make the grind that bit more tedious to encourage payments for in-game currency. I do not condone paying for in-game currency myself, at least not for a game like this where it'll disappear in a matter of seconds with how ridiculous their prices are.  If you want to use your money on it, you're an adult and me or no one else really has the right to tell you what to do with it, I would just say that 8mil for about £80-90 of real life money is absolutely insane and more than what people earn in days of work, I can't understand how they imagined the scaling of these cards would work either.
1B. They subtly punish you for completing missions efficiently and quickly, deteriorating the fun another notch. I have become quite decent at speed running missions from when I started on ps3 and again, I have noticed that as I have come back to the game from time to time, when I speed run missions now, there is no static payout for reward for actually being good at the game, I literally farmed maximum money from easy missions by sitting there for 10 minutes then killing everyone really quickly and just ending it. You get rewarded to be slow, cumbersome and generally it just wants you to play the more tedious aspects of the game which take hours, such as heists. Now, I do like heists, do not take me the wrong way, however forcing me to go into games with a lot of random strangers who often mess the heists up, have no real cohesion with one another really drains me personally.
I have also come to the conclusion, even with all of those methods of making arcade style quick missions more useless to make money, I can still often make more money than I can in the time it takes to do a heist, just by sitting there, repeating and doing the same boring stuff, which in itself is easier for me and many others due to time constraints.
2. Public only missions and features, while I get the point of it, it honestly just becomes extremely tedious due to modders (chill out, I like modding and often it's hilarious, but in this case, it's a bit annoying) often just flying around, breaking everything, being invincible and generally just a pain. This is more of a gripe of my own, I loved playing public before but with all the stuff going on, it's just not the most fun thing to do for me and my friends now.
3. Co-op in a private game is just as tedious due to the same issues in point 1, you and your friends just want to play around, have some fun, etc. I loved doing missions with all the new vehicles we got, but as we became more efficient, even with the biker missions, it just became a grind fest of going back and forth, doing the same few missions over and over again and just not having any fun. The heists are fun when you have enough people and enough time, but they can take a while and often the payout really isn't that big, leading back to the cash card thing.
4. The absolute hatred of modders take-two has, rockstar itself actually likes modding and has often showcased mods in official feeds, however take-two has completely held that under the water for it to drown a slow death, gradually making it more and more difficult to create good content for what would be a great game if not for these issues (at least for me). I can already feel the kneejerk of "but you said you hated modders for public games, etc, etc", I do not hate modders, however forcing me into games with people who abuse them is not ideal or fun, however, removing modded content that specifically caters to the neglected aspect of the game, being single player, is absolutely ridiculous. Single player could be a modders playground but instead it is now being scorned for reasons unknown to me, take-two have just outright targeted single player modding, which has actively taken steps towards not affecting multiplayer games and basically stamped out a lot of work for seemingly no genuine reason. Modding has, and will always be part of the PC gaming platform, whether I have had annoyances or fun at the end of it doesn't matter, it's part of PC gaming, and should be embraced.
I remember when GTA was satirical of these shark like business practices, they were always a company trying to make money, yes, but GTA V has just become a parody of itself at this point, wanting you to pay real money for relatively small amounts of in-game currency as they bump up the prices of vehicles further and further, effectively asking you to pay upwards of £90 for about 8mil of in-game currency, just look at how insane that is and take a minute to look at it, paying twice the amount of the video games initial price (almost) for what is effectively enough money to waste in 5 minutes due to vehicle and upgrade prices in-game. I would again say, I don't condone it, you're an adult, do what you want, but I do not feel any pity for those who let themselves get ripped off in this manner, I hope it's a lesson learned to them because i'm sure £90 of their money, time and sweat in real life should be worth much more than a little bit of game currency, it's an insult to the consumer and gamers intelligence alike, we are better than this, we should be better than this.
TL;DR: I would like to say for the issues the game has, it's a great game, great vehicles and features, it's great fun when you do mess around but you won't make progress and it'll effectively become stale in the long run, it'll punish you for doing missions quickly and effectively while lowering the cash per mission bar gradually over time to encourage the purchase of what is now relatively small in-game currency for large amounts of real money. I'm sad to say that whatever has happened, I cannot recommend this game, as a long time player. I don't regret playing it, but I'm sad to see it turn itself inside out.
Edit: I've turned this to public just because, some of the things I have written may or may not have changed, in regards to modding and other features, I still can't recommend it due to the sheer amount of grinding you need for a game that's generally been about dumb fun.

Clear Sky is an entertaining game that expands on Shadow of Chernobyl (SoC).
The story, atmosphere, and sounds are still on point. I found it strange that you end up fighting humans a lot more than dungeon crawling and fighting mind-controlling mutants in this game. This game also introduces a faction war system, which is pretty cool. It gives me more people to shoot at with my ultra-high accuracy rifle.
If you're bothered by the wacky, inaccurate aiming system, I suggest you use the hunting rifle until you get a more accurate weapon. You can steal an AC-96 from the military people (South Cordon) and upgrade it (with scope and silencer). Then, use that until you get an F-200M and upgrade that. Also, always aim for the head. 1-3 hits will always kill.
If you need money, sell medical gear, weapons, and artifacts. Artifacts are hard to come by so keep the great ones for yourself. Always be on the lookout for anomalies, pull out your detector (press O) and look for them.
This game is hard as hell. You'll be pressing F5 and F9 a lot. But, if you stick with it, you'll be able to get the best equipment in the game and end up... pressing F5/ F9 less often.
Also, that incessant buzzing noise from using Night Vision for hours on end is stuck in my brain. It's like a brain scorcher.
End game Gear:
Weapon: FT200 (upgraded for accuracy) with some worthless pistol
Armor: CS-1 (Upgraded for armor and night vision)
Detector: Veles
Artifacts: Bubble, and the artifacts that give you more endurance and less weight.
Faction: Freedom
