This game will either claims hundreds to thousands of hours of your life, or it will claim none. And there's no way to tell without buying.
You play as a lone ranger riding throughout the mystical lands of Calradia, set in medieval Europe. Calradia is split up into many factions all fighting over sole control of the lands. You fight bandits, do tasks for lords, and recruit villagers from the towns, and soon you have an army of men fighting under your command. You can choose your walk of life from here, but be careful - one wrong move can put you back to square one. You can choose to become a mercenary for a realm. You can fight more bandits and upgrade your men to higher levels. You can join a tournament, and make a fortune with your masterful fighting. Or you can play with politics and sneak your way into become a vassal of a realm.
From there you can fight for your liege and make your realm the strongest in the land. Or you could try to sneak your way into overthrowing the king, putting in a puppet king under your control. Or you could even rebel against your own realm, and claim lands for your own, making a new realm in Calradia. But be careful because all of the other Kings and Counts can do everything that you can do, and you don't know which ones will strike at you first.
All of these choices are up to you in this incredibly diverse grand-strategy RPG.
I'll start with the good parts:
The game is extremely unique, there is nothing similar to it at all. It's like a mix of Rome: Total War and Europa Univeralis 4, except it plays completely differently from those. This "uniqueness" can make you come back to the game a countless number of times just due to the fact that there is no other way to have this wonderful experience.
I think the thing that attracted me to this game the most was how beautifully dynamic the world was. All the different characters in the game will talk to you differently based off of what realm you're in, how much prestige you have, and a number of other factors. This makes the game feel alive and you feel like whenever you do something, the characters in the game will actually
.
Another thing this game does very well is combat. The way the fighting works is very fun, and there is no 'one right way' to do it. You could be a foot soldier, a lancer on horseback, a horsearcher, or a crossbowman. They are all good in their own ways.
Similar to the previous point is that this game for the most part gets balance right. Even though each realm has completely unique soldiers and completely unique weapons in completely unique terrain, none of the realms are too powerful. Every time you play, a different realm will become the "super power".
Ok so let's move on to the negatives:
The graphics are outdated and quite honestly a pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥ Do not get this game expecting a beautiful Skyrim-like world. Expect a game with 2001-level-graphics.
The game is full of bugs. Unfortunately, due to how free the game is, it is stacked with bugs. Not game breaking bugs, but small bugs in the dialogue or graphics or collisions. This causes the game to lose a lot of the immersion that it is based upon.
The multiplayer in this game is bad. The incredible fighting mechanics in the game would work so well in multiplayer if it was executed properly. Unfortunately, it wasn't. There are usually only 2-3 servers with enough people to play a game. The games have unpolished and gross maps, and the UI seems like it was built in 5 minutes. The community can be fairly toxic too, at times.
This is one of my favorite games of all time, but I accept the fact that it is incredibly flawed and not for everyone. If this review even SLIGHTLY interests you in the game - totally buy it. If not, and it happens to be a turn off, maybe this game isn't for you.

Had a blast playing this game! If you've played the first game of the series, Shadows of Chernobyl (SoC)—this second installation is a prequal—you'll find lots of similarities, but a few distinct differences. Gone are the moments of terror and tension of "stalking" through radiation- and anomaly-infested facilities wondering in fear of what may be around the corner. You still do a lot of it—the game world is near identical to the original SoC; however, this time the pace is much more action-oriented.
A new "faction" mode compels you to spend a lot of your time fending off other humans (bandtis, renegades, military, etc...) in a "capture-the-flag" type game mode, so a lot of time is spent fending off enemies in weapon-to-weapon situations. If you're a fan of the horror motif of SoC, it's been toned down quite a bit, but if you enjoy working with very intelligent AI to take control of key positions, then you'll find that aspect of the game very engaging.
The upgrade mechanic is also a welcomed mechanic; however, it was frustrating at first using low-end base weapons and watching them miss their mark more often than not. Cost of upgrades were also a little pricey, forcing you to choose very carefully or run the risk of spending additional hours grinding to make enough money to craft a new weapon to your liking.
Overall, definitely worthy of the series, albeit a slightly differenty type of game than the original, but the differences were definitely more of a positive than a negative. Would definitely recommend this game, even if you've never played SoC (but I would recommend playing SoC first, as their are some major spoilers right away that reference aspects of that first game).
Now I'm looking forward to finishing off the trilogy with Call of Pripyat!

If I'd need to describe Portal Knights in few words, I would say "casual Minecraft-like action", "casual" being the main word here.This review describes v0.3.0, Early Access. If you're looking at the "not recommend" flag: I'm not saying the game's horrible, mind you. It's more... "not for everyone". For me it gets boring rather quick. If I would be given a 1 to 5 scale, I'd rate it 3. Interested in details? I got them for you.
Pros:
+ Coherent cartoonish graphic style
Something PK excels at, graphic style is kept at professional level and is arguably the best among all sandboxes. Diversity of blocks (and props) is something the game improved in recently and I think it won't be the last time devs do it.
+ Overall stability
Something you don't see often in Early Access games, PK is quite stable. It rarely crashes and even more rarely throws bugs your way.
+ Easy to grasp, forgiving gameplay
While some can say it's a drawback, this game doesn't make you shake in horror being afraid to lose everything you've got so far. Resurrection is instant and causes no penalties (aside from the fact you're always resurrecting in the same place). You don't drop any items upon death.
+ Quick resource regeneration, no resource destruction
While all the blocks can be mined, most can be acquired without mining through farming mobs, the exception being simple dirt (and any world mostly consists of it so there are lots). Trees and crops grow (relatively) fast. As I've said, it's a casual game. Bombs and exploding monsters don't destroy blocks but "mine" them (you can pick them up later). Few ways to destroy blocks completely include dropping them into the Abyss surrounding each island or waiting for the mined blocks to despawn.
Cons:
- No goal in the game
While "lack of a goal" may sound strange for a sandbox, there is actually not much you can do here. Monsters and "bosses" aren't much of a challenge. Currently the basic principle of gameplay can be described as "beat mobs, activate portal, jump into hext island". Repeat. There are no NPCs, little lore and no story. There are no quests, no pets to tame or rare things to collect. The latest updates brought random events though, so there finally is something you can look for.
- Lacking and mandatory crafting
"Lacking" doesn't mean it's downright bad. But most props and gear can be built straight away if you have the right crafting stations and resources, few recipes dropping from monsters (and even these can be skipped). You'll skip most early weapons and armors as you get new resources much faster than use them (especially copper).
Resource requirements for crafting are unbalanced, especially late-game. While you can easily craft your first forge, gathering high-tier stone/metal for the upgrades quickly turns into a digfest (or grindfest). Conversion rates for late game metals (ore to bars) is ridiculous (was even more so before the devs halved it, and it's still high).
Early recipes are fine, with the exception of a torch which requires cotton (growing and dropping only in first biomes) and 3 Wood (which is what roughly one tree drops). If you're going for torches (and you'll need lots of them for exploration) it's much easier to get to the desert island, wait for the night and kill Fire Knights - every knight drops one.
Last, but not least, crafting is mandatory and is the only way of obtaining better equipment. Monsters, including bosses, and treasure boxes don't drop armor, weapons or props and drop few recipes.
- "Classes" have little difference
All stats are raised during level-up simultaneously. Skill tree doesn't give many cool things, if any. Every class has spells but weapons are generally more efficient, so a mage doesn't usually do magic. Armor and weapons aren't bound to a class (which is good) and are of little usefullness beyond protection/damage and HP/MP increase (which is bad). Thus, little to no specialization. Playing every class is basically the same.
- No treasure hunting
"Treasure" boxes, urns and chests don't contain actual treasure. It's mostly blocks, potions, crafting ingredients and healing hearts (and rarely, recipes). All gear and most props are crafted. The game has no traders and no currency so crawling dungeons has sense only in search of portals.
- Fragmented game world, static biomes
There is actually no "game world", just small islands flying in the Abyss and connected by portals. Big enough to explore, small enough to not get tired of distances.
The size, however, has its drawbacks. Abyss means no water or lava (or any other liquid whatsoever).
"Biomes" are bound to islands, don't depend on soil or any other factors and are mostly decorative. Monsters and crops are also bound to islands so you can't bring your favourite mobs/crops to the world you like.
- Static spawn system
Spawn system is extremely predictable. Mid-game you'll know how many mosters are there in a room before entering it. There is no way to prevent spawning. In most sandbox games light sources or player-placed artificial blocks prevent monster spawning. In PK there is no such (or any other) system. You can find lots of half-destroyed castles and rebuild them but there will always be skeletons inside if you reenter the island, same number, in the same places.
- Most props are purely decorative
And when I say "most", what I mean is "everything except torches, doors, chests and crafting stations". Beds, tables, chairs, windows etc have no function.
If you're looking for a quick relaxing game after work, that might be your thing. If you're looking for something more deep and serious I would recommend looking somewhere else.

PAM is a surprisingly great and funny game built on a principle of Destruction Derbys. That means your goal is to race and destroy as many vehicles as you can. You have a lot of ways how to do it - you can use your driving skills (for example push the opponent from track or into other vehicle), front weapon you load when you collect a yellow barrel, side weapon loaded with blue barrel and rear weapon loaded with red barrel. So we all get what´s this game about, so I´ll write what I like and what I dislike about it so far:
+ Lots fo vehicles you can choose from. They differ not only in the boring statistics like speed, acceleration and other, but they are really funny and they all have custom weapon animations. For example little pink car, that has an unicorn horn as its front weapon or other car is thwrowing nuclear waste as ammo.
+ The maps and tracks are well built. There are numerous ways where you can go, you can jump, trick or lay traps.
+ It´s a real fun to play
+ I haven´t played the multiplayer, but I think things could go really crazy when you play it together with your friends. I wish my friends have this game too!
+ You could get it really cheap, there are lot of sales and you can buy a 3-pack for your friends too. This game could be often found in random steam keys too.
- The game does not offer a lot of hours of playtime. The game goal does not change and in spite of the fact, that there are a lot of vehicles and tracks, there is no advancement as in other games. You can play all the cars from the beginning, you can ride all the maps. Everything is open. You don´t see any point of playing it sometimes (except it´s fun). So it´s great fun to play as a pause-filler but not as an full-time game.
- The physics of the game are sometimes unrealistic. There is a bus and a little something, that looks like VW Beetle and the tiny Beetle could push the bus easy from the cliff. It seems like all the vehicles have the same power, the same weight in collisions. But when it comes to speed, handling, acceleration and breaking, everything seems to be ok and appropriate.

The endless whininess and negative reviews based solely on the cost of DLC is ridiculous. I've put 90+ hours into TS2017 and its predecessors, and I've almost invariably thoroughly enjoyed the experience. It's stable, it runs well, and it executes incredibly well on the core fantasy. Routes such as the Liverpool-Manchester, South Wales, Clapham, North London and South London lines are fantastic.
Is the DLC expensive? Sure, but it's still a lot less that DCS World's single aircraft (and even their prices are totally reasonable, IMHO). People are entitled to their opinions, and "reasonable value" is a very subjective concept that means different things to different people. From my perspective, though, I just wait until the sales and I feel as though I've had huge value for money out the core game and the hundreds of dollars of DLC that I've bought.
Your mileage may vary, but my personal opinion is that "mixed" reviews casts TS2017 in a very unfair light given that it's one of the most satisfying and endlessly engaging games I've played in 35+ years of wide-ranging hardcore gaming.

- Monty Python pretty much summed up what living on Deponia is like. So it's no wonder protagonist Rufus wants to escape the literal pile of trash. Too bad he's an obnoxious, egocentric idiot who can barely do anything right, other than perhaps make various things blow up in various faces...
A not-entirely-likeable definitely-not-hero for a protagonist is a classic ingredient for adventure gold, and Daedalic followed other parts of time-honored recipes, too. Puzzles from trivial to head-scratchers (the way some of them don't really have good hints for them may be the game's one Achilles heel), a graphics style that fits the comedic tone of the game and is executed well, plus some nifty little tricks that make playing eassier (like quick-warping to sscreen exits).
If you think you live in a dump and have it rough, you ain't seen nothing yet and totally need to treat yourself to the
experience. Ideally, look for a package deal that includes the sequels - even though this is a full-length adventure, it's really rather open-ended.

Being a fan of the other 2 games in the series I bought this one expecting another great FPS but what a steaming pile of crap I stepped in. I could only get through about 6 hours of playing it before I felt like I was totally wasting my time. The combat is probably the worst I've ever experienced. I've tried a variety of weapons, upgraded damage and accuracy on some, and still the enemies just seem unaffected by me unloading all my ammo into them while they kill me with ease. The armor they start you with is totally worthless as are the guns. I thought I just needed to explore a little to get better equipment and upgrade things but even that didn't help.
Because the combat system is totally broken that makes it near impossible to accomplish anything since most of the quests are about attacking or defending something which is hard to do when your equipment is totally ineffective. To make it worse, the trade system sucks too. Find a gun worth 1000? You'll probably be able to sell it for 50. Good luck saving up to mod your weapons and armor at that rate. Then again, the upgrades don't help so why bother.
With the combat and trade systems being total garbage, I just don't see any reason to continue playing this game. There are much better games out there that are more worthwhile. I've heard certain aspects of the game can be fixed with mods but you know what works better than hunting down mods to fix a crappy game? Installing a better game that works right from the start. Skip this one and spend your money elsewhere.

Second Stalker was improved compared with first under many aspects, everything seems to works very well here and much better, but you'll face again an high difficulty, altough a bit lower compared with the first chapter (and this is a positive note for me).
Now, you CAN repair your gears, weapons and armors, this was much more than a simple change, this was awesome, believe me :)
Altough in the first game thre was the chance to upgrade some gears, in this game this feature is taken to high levels, allowing you to improve a lot your armaments, making you almost invincible, money and schematics allowing, yes, because you'll have first find the proper schematic and take them to the right technician who will be able then to upgrade your stuff....
I said above you ned a lot of money to upgrade your gears, so farming money will be very important in this game and will recquire a lot of time and here comes a very negative aspect of this game, because there will be a point in the game, where you'll lose all your money, and no, there is nothing you can do to avoid it, it's part of main story, so my suggestion id to store all your found gears in a stash and sell to vendors only AFTER this disgraceful event will happens.
I really hated this feature invented by devs cause there is nothing that advice you before, i spent hours farming and lost all, lucikly a previous savegame fixed in part the problem but made me losea lot of time and patience...
And again, another very bad new feature in this game will be the EMISSIONS, a sort of radiation explosion that will happens suddenly while you'll play, no matter where you are and what are you doing (and how much heavy you'll be in that moment, so you'll not be able to run :(  ) so to avoid to be instant killed you'll have to take cover, but, you think that will be enough enter in ahoude or inside a solid tunnel ? Nope, you''ll have to run in specific marked in the map zones (yellow color) where you'll be immune, even if is a n open place, no matter, you'll survive, while you'll die in any other place....
So, this could have been a nice feature, if was implemented a little better, but when this random event will happens, you'll be often, ( specially the first time, when you'll die a dozen of times before you'll realize what is happening to you ^^) too damn much far away from the suggested cover point and could happens that you'll not do in time to reeach the safe spot, or because you carry too much stuff that will deny you to run or because in the cover point there are enemies that will kill you while you try to enter, so, with time, you'll learn few tricks that will save your life but, overall, this is very very annoying mini event :(
A nice tip, since to make money you'll have to sell weapons dropped by dead soldiers, you'll most of the time be unable to carry more than a few of them cause of the weight limit, making the process difficult cause of the distance to the vendors, i've discovered this after i was already playing and i was very happy of that, dead bodies, of both soldiers and mutants, can be dragged keeping pushed together your USE button + Left SHIFT, this way you can use the corpses like a bag where you can put anyhing you want , altough dragging these corpses for miles could be tricky cause they will fall down from your hands often in the process, you'll have some benefit from this.
A new feature of this game is the Factions War, you'll be free if to help some of them and exterminate another or remain neutral with all, you'll receive some serious benefits (in gears) if you'll decide to join some of them, specially The Duty and The Freedom.
The search of manufacts, items that will improve some of your stas, incresed of importance here and became a little more funny and pleasant the system to find them.
In conclusion, i could recommend this game even to non hardcore players, but the difficulty remain at high levels altough more reasonable compared with the first game.

A flawed but fantastic game and a brilliant evolution for the series.
The story mode is a great start, it's a little lacking compared the Netherrealm games but hopefully with the next one they can ramp it up. I say the next one because although touted as "the final chapter in the Mishima saga" it clearly isn't. I won't spoil anything and it is more conclusive than anything before it it still isn't the end.
The biggest flaw with the story mode is a single voice actor, a narrator journalist man who talks through a lot of it between major cutscenes and his voice is dead. It's almost as if they were going for a noirish approach but not only does it not mesh with the rest of the game but it's a very fine line between dull as♥♥♥♥♥♥and intense as ♥♥♥♥. They missed the mark with that. That's even if they were going for that, it might just be a truly awful voice actor. Outside of that it's still a great story mode, although a bit short. It goes through from the beginning of the saga to the current point so newcomers should be able to understand what's happening.
The other modes include a practice mode, an arcade mode and a treasure mode where you can unlock customization items. I have to give them credit for not going with any kind of microtransactions in this given the game has an in-game currency. It's all set out like a proper old school game where everything can be unlocked just by playing at a reasonable pace. Also some of the items you can put on your character are usable, guns and melee weapons as well as some bizarre clothing items that react being hit and stuff. It's all stupid but kinda cool nonetheless.
The arcade mode is five fights which is a bit short too but it doesn't really matter when all the characters are already unlocked from the get-go. I was a little dissapointed in that because that used to be the meat of the singleplayer but I guess there's a story mode now so it's not too bad The endings for each character are gone from arcade mode but not missing altogether. For whatever reason they decided to put them in the story mode in a section called "Character Chapters". Here you can pick one of 30 characters and play a single match against whoever their enemy might be and get a short cutscene. This also feels a bit lacking as you don't get to play as that character for very long so it doesn't feel rewarding. Still, they are there though.
I've yet to touch the online but I've only heard good things about it's functionality so that's nice.
The soundtrack is easily my second favourite OST for any Tekken game, second only to Tekken 3. It's the first one since that where I just like it as music and not only in the context of a Tekken game. It's very electronic heavy and some people may not like that but I dig the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of it.
Where this game impressed me the most though is in it's optimization. To put into perspective I have a GTX 670, a 3.20GHz i-5 processor and 16Gb of RAM and with the exception of AA, which is all the way off, I can max this game out at 1080p with a solid 60fps during gameplay, unless I'm playing as or fighting against Panda or Kuma as they have a lot of fur. They look damn good though. I do get a lot of drops to around 40 during cutscenes and the Rage Arts things but whenever I'm actually playing, solid 60. Obviously I don't play the game that way but I had to test it out. The load times are quite lengthy, I have this installed on an SSD and the load times are what I would expect to be normal but it's not painstakingly bad. It might be a test of patience on a normal hard drive though.
Overall I think this is an excellent game and a truly excellent addition to the Tekken series. Goddamn I've missed these games since moving to PC gaming.

My friend and I got this together on sale. We're both fans of games like Minecraft, but Portal Knights takes the concept a step further with a more in-depth RPG aspect.
PROS -
Unlike Minecrack, there are several worlds to travel to a fro. Although they're much smaller than a single server in MC, they're still plenty big enough to encourage exploration, and I believe the worlds' smaller sizes makes the game run smoother (whereas MC takes a beast of a PC to run smoothly).
You can build whatever you want! I've built a modest home where I farm resources, while my friend make his wizard tower up the hill from me where he makes spells and bombs.
The graphics are a bit cartoony and childish, but they're VERY pretty and leagues better to look at than MC. There are many different looking enemies and tilesets between worlds, making no place feel the same as you leap between portals.
Although there is a bit of an RPG feel to MC, Portal Knights takes it much further by making far more types of weapons and armors that add varying bonuses to suit your play style. Combat is simple, but it's more complex than MC.
There are classes! I started off as the Warrior while my friend picked the Wizard. He heals and does elemental damage from a distance while I charge in and agro. You can't do that in MC!
The game starts up very quickly and the loads screens between worlds are brief. I'm never tapping my fingers waiting to play.
CONS -
We're unsure of why it happens, but when my friend in connected to my world he crashes out of the game from time to time. While I continue playing just fine, he has to restart the game (which isn't that bad, more of a mild annoyance considering how fast the game starts up).
MC has a survival feel to it, having to cook and eat food - I wish this game implented something like that down the line. It'd be interesting to travel between worlds and eventually need to set up camp with your friend to eat some grub.
Water. There are no bodies of water, which means there are no boats, underwater creatures, or swimming. Unless there is a level down the line I've yet to see, I'd like some form of seafaring adventure.
OVERALL -
This game is awesome and I'll be playing it for a long, long time. I can't wait to see where the devs take this title and it's totally worth the asking the price. Aside from my friend crashing sometimes while we play together, I have come across ZERO bugs. For an early access game, I am very surprised and pleased with my purchase and play time.
Very good blend of Terraria and Minecraft feel of play. Like the crafting syste, Also like the travelling from place to place for new items. Looking forward to what comes next with this title.

-RNG gear drops

-Harder bosses

24 hours in, and I'm ready to pull the trigger on this one. Portal Knights is a quality product. Since launch, it has been updated a million times, and improved SO much. 505 is killing it with this game.
Let's get this out of the way:
It's NOT a Minecraft style game
It's NOT a 3D Terraria
If you go in, expecting either, be prepared to be confused. It's an Action game, with crafting and building elements. Crafting is mostly for POTIONS, CLOTHING, WEOPONS, TOOLS, MAGIC, and other assorted items to help you kill the baddies. Crafting or building other stuff, can be skipped entirely.
It's HARD playing solo. Take your time, and don't just plow through the portals, you will get to a point where you suck HARD.  Best with friends, especially the bosses. Take your time, level up, and upgrade your gear as much as possible.
Portal Nights doesn't WOW me like other favorites of mine, but it keeps pulling me back, to try my hand at progressing... I feel like I'm just getting going, and I've got 24hrs, at $15. That's a WIN....

So heres my basic thoughts about the game. I will address the most obvious pros and cons that I experienced about the game.
PROS :
- ww2
- upgradable weapon system
- plethera of weapons and vehicles
- good map design
This is a game that most peopler who like ww2 should try out. I have personally had good time running through a village with my M1 Garand, shooting krauts. I have also had bad times though.
CONs :
-still pay 2 win, although its much less than it used to be.
-paratroopers can drop themselves anywhere on the map, with any weapon.
-poor graphics
-poor physics engine
-sounds are wonky
-♥♥♥♥♥♥ ranking, xp and money system
Its still a pay to win. Even though the devs sort of fixed the ranking system, it still sucks, it still takes you forever to get enough credits with out paying for them to actually improve things. For example, a skin for your M1 that makes a darker shade of brown costs 79k. Imagine what an actual trigger or barrel or god forbid, even a sight mod would cost. Now consider that your default salary as a soldier starts at 8k per hour. PER HOUR. Yes, you heard it. You earn cash based on how long you play the game, not how well you do in it. No matter how many points you cap or people you take out or games you win, you literally need to play for hours and hours and hours on end to even see a visible improvement. Now, about the whole wonky sounds and graphics. The graphics are bad. They are, and there is no excuse. War Thunder, another free to play game, has beautiful graphics, so H&G cant hide behind that. Now, lets put this into perspective. There is a sniper in the hills hiding in foliage. He can see you through his scope perfectly fine. You can't even see his gunfire because even on max graphics the games render distance is horrible. Unsuitable for the large, strategic maps thats you find in assault and war gamemodes. The sounds are even annoying. Planes dropping bombs are some of the most annoying sounds, and the gunfire sounds are poorly done. Literally firing .22s in person sounds cooler than the rinky dink sound the M1 makes. Its really just a poorly done game. It has great potential, but would honestly need a different ownership and a complete revamp to make what I would consider a "good" game

Deponia is a very challenging point-and-click game about a loaner trying to escape his junk-filled home planet. As a disclaimer I should say that I haven't finished this game and probably won't come back. The fact of the matter is, the game is just too difficult for me to finish. However, other than that, I actually really like what I've seen of the game, and I don't think a high difficulty alone should be enough to not recommend it. Just know that it's only for "hardcore" point-and-click players.
+Decent humor that made me chuckle
+Nice art, if you like the cartoony style
+Even though it looks like a game for kids, it's actually targeting older players (hence the difficulty)
+Lots of quirky characters and dialogue
+Interesting story
+/-Difficulty wise, this is the Dark Souls of point-and-click games.
-I had a bug where the game was too zoomed in and didn't fit the screen. Googling this revealed I could fix this by editing a config file, but occasionally the game would auto-edit the config file back and I would have to change it again. I was playing the Linux version of the game.
In a way, I'm not qualified to write this review, since I haven't finished the game and therefore haven't seen the end of the story. I also can't speak for the length of the game, although I do already have 10 hours in it, and it feels like I'm not even halfway. Bottom line, I definitely like this game, but it's hard as balls, and you are going to end up tearing your hair out. It got so bad that I ended up trying to brute force solutions by making every single humanly possible combination of inventory items. But I'm sure there are people who are either better at this type of game than me or just like the challenge. For those people, this is the game for you.

I'll start off with something basic before my opinion on the game: If you do not like challenging games that test your ability to learn and adapt to situations then don't buy this game. 99% of negative reviews are just complaining that it is a difficult game or that there is a timer for each level, often times these people have less than 2 hours in game, which is what I believe is the time needed to really start to feel comfortable and progress.
On to my own opinion of the game: Spelunky is easily one of the most challenging game I've played, you will die random deaths from very small mistakes and rage constantly at the beginning. But if you like the challenge of mastering character mechanics and learning how to survive in tough situations then this game is perfect for you. I'll break down the very basics of each "category" to games.
Visual/hearing: You'll probably know if you'll like the graphics based on the pictures above but what suprised me was the games fluidity. It never lags and everything just runs smoothly into itself. The music is fun and adventurous which fits the game perfectly.
Controls: I use an x-box controller which I recommend highly. The controls are easy to learn but hard to master. Their are small quirks and tricks that you figure out for yourself as you progress.
Gameplay: There are many different paths you can use to be succesfull in this game. There are plenty of items to choose from and with the randomization you'll never have the same experience. The game is extremely hard so unless you want to spend at least 2 hours or so getting good enough to relax a bit this might not be for you.
Overall this game is amazing. People's only turn off is the difficulty and timer but thats the point of the game. Plus the payoff is great once you reach new levels, just like beating a boss in dark souls haha.

I rate the game Surgeon Simulator 2013 2.5/5. Not very good but not total garbage either.
This first-person-perspective game causes you to play as an incompetent, possibly drung surgeon's completely numb left hand (with one keyboard button controlling each finger) and has you trying to complete simple "operations" with nothing but the use of that left hand. The "operations" consist entirely of breaking through bone and ripping out cartoon-styled internal organs before dropping in replacement organs in a fairly imprecise manner. Essentially, this game, which is not very well made but has not major bugs either, is just for laughs (both yours and those who you relate your game experiences to) and for getting bizarre and disgusting steam achievements. This game fulfills its essential comedic purposes but doesn't really do much else.
+Cartoon styled graphics which strike a fine balance between grossness and humor.
+Excellent sound effects add to the humor.
+Fun (though extremely unrealistic) physics simulation.
+Fun steam achievements.
+Fairly inexpensive (though short) game.
+/- Poor and difficult controls which, while very frustrating, add greatly to the game's humor.
-Very few "operations" (6 or 7 in all) very few modes, too few options, too much secret stuff which cannot be accessed via a menu, most of the game must be unlocked causing you to end up getting stuck on an extremely hard kidney transplant (for example) before being allowed to continue on to other, often easier "operations."
-This game has a downloadable pack including more operations dubbed "anniversary edition content" for 3 more dollars which contains stuff that should have been included in the original game.
-This game can easily become frustrating and has a very difficult learning curve.
-There's a general feeling about this game that much, much more could have been done had the game's designers been more ambitious and that the game could have been a whole lot more fun than it is.

Surgeon Simulator puts the player in the place of a surgeon, performing various surgeries with a rather defunct hand eye coordiration. Your keyboard will serve as your hands for this comedic simulator, each key bound to a finger. Best of luck actually having any kind of skill at this game, I've played it quite a bit and am yet to accomplish any level of skill for any of the surgeries within the game. Also, if you're expecting a realistic simulator, move on.
The gameplay does its job of being a wacky comedic style. You will miss injections, accidentally break bones, and probably rip out a few vital organs that really didn't need much attention given to them; it all adds to the comedy though. Surgeon Simulator manages to do what its supposed to do really well, and provide a fun experience for however long you can put up with these nonsensical controls.
The graphics are nothing amazing, but they do the job. The sounds are far too serious for a title this comedic, but I think that's all part of the charm. The graphics and sounds within Surgeon Simulator 2013 will make you think like you're doing your job properly, but I really wouldn't count on it.
There's no real storyline to this game, just a medical file full of many missions (and extras!) for you to get the most out of this title. There's enough content in this game to keep you going for a few hours, if you wanna' finish the whole game in one sitting. Otherwise, this is well worth the price.
Honestly, I can't find myself wanting to go through the pain over never being able to complete a level in my many days of gameplay, but I'm sure you will! The sense of completion Ican only imagine is one of the most satisfying feelings in gaming history, so I can't see you wanting to go through that pain again.

I bought M&B Warband long ago, first on a physical CD.  That got lost but I got it again on Steam.  That said, M&B Warband is worth every penny and then some.
The main idea of this game is a "sandbox" of sorts that the player can make a character, plop into the game world, and just GO.  For questing, there is nothing special as every other RPG does questing way better than M&B WB.  The graphics are horrible even for this game's release years ago.  It doesn't hold up even today.  You can find action games, combat / action RPGs with better combat systems.  What M&B did do that most RPGs struggle with is mounted combat.  The joy and freedom of having a horse, a lance, was exhilirating when the game released and it's still fun now, something I'm surprised other RPGs still are worse off at.
Individual systems other games do better than M&B WB.  The game however brings lots of things together to give you the freedom to do what you want in the game world.
Do you want to start off a lowly soldier in some lord's army, rise in power?  You can do that.
Do you want to be completely independent adventuring, fighting on your own, preying on whatever, whoever you want?  You can do that.
Do you want to ignore serving someone and gain power, prestige on your own that you can build your own big army and conquer your own kindom?  You can do that.
There's more than one way to play.  You can build up as a very combat oriented character, like a knight, warrior.  Or you build up as a ranges specialist for bows, crossbows, even javelins.  There's even horse archery.  Do you want to specialize as a highly charistmatic, intelligent leader built on getting a lot of people to follow you (and do your fighting) while also being great in tactics and engineering skills for benefits ingame?  That's a possibility also.  Again, the idea is the game gives you the freedom.
The graphics are ugly.  That needs to be stressed.  But it has never held this game back from years of continued support by the fans and has considerable mods.  Mods that simply expand, tweak the base game.  There are mods to convert M&B WB into Warhammer Fantasy style, Middle Earth.  There's even mods to turn this game into a Napoleonic era game.  There's even a Star Wars mod for this.  There are even Game of Throne mods for it.  Hop onto ModDB and see in the popular mods how much support this game has received from fans.

My recorded playtime is not reflective of actual playtime. I've bought Clear Sky twice now, and I play a modded version now.
So first, I'll give a review of the game by itself, then add a little something for the vets.
This is a great tactical fps and rpg game. The gun mechanics feel so good in this game. It's not like most games where bullet spread and accuracy is just enough enough of a factor to notice it in game. Here you you really have to have good aim, and you have to stabilize your gun before you fire. Getting into a battle with a couple bandits with a shotgun in this game feels more epic and real than anything you'll see in a COD or Battlefield or just about any other shooter. The AI is just awesome. Taking cover, blind fire, flanking, retreating, grenades, camping, even sneaking on a rare occasion. The combat mechanics are my favorite part of this game; every gun feels different and realistic, and every encounter gets the adrenalin going.
The art is another thing, some people find the game ugly, but I think it's got the best sun rays and dynamic effects I've ever seen. They had volumetric fog in this around the same time as the AAA games started getting it. There is nothing like the zone though, I find myself screenshotting a lot in this game. Seeing water stream down walls and the sunrays through trees or windows... it's just a beautiful game.
The story is great too, but it is mostly an addition to the story of Call of Chernobyl. That game had a bit of a better story with the whole "Kill Strelok" mission, but this one simply adds to that. What this story does better than the other STALKER games, and heres where I start talking to the vets, is it takes you through the areas of the zone at a much more balanced and compelling pace. It kinda funnels you through these scenarios that slowly feel more and more epic, because of the gameplay challenges presented.
Now with all that said, I think this is the best of the STALKER games, and I think it's worthy to note that it is cheaper than the others last I saw. Of course they all have their own merits and flaws but I like the mechanics the best in this one, and the challenge. I also believe that it has the best mods available for it, there's a few that combine it with the first stalker which is just perfect I think.
Get Arsenal Overhaul and The Factions War Mod and the game is awesome, without mods its frustratingly unrealistic with gunplay and the nades. Play on master or GTFO

Awesome game. Playstyle is quite different from other fighting games since it's 3D, but it's without a doubt one of the best fighting games right now.
As soon as you understand that it's 3D and that every button (ABXY) is a limb, you're good to go. Even if you're new to fighting games you can pull awesome stuff just by remembering those facts.
Pros:
-Highly optimized, runs perfectly.
-Graphics are pretty cool.
-Customization is extensive.
-Online runs flawless, even on 1/2 bar games.
-Treasure battles are really nice for those that don't like online.
-Online tournament mode is awesome, I love it.
-Has Eliza and Katarina. Period.
-Has a lot of content for a fighting game.
-The HUD and menus are really good.
Cons:
-After a while some of the music tracks make you wanna bang your head to the wall (Training room for example).
-No online training room.
-Story feels a bit rushed towards the end.
-Achievements are too easy.
TL;DR: If you like fighting games, get it. If you're new to fighting games, this is one is most likely one of the best to start with.

South Park: The Fractured But Whole is a great sequel to Stick of Truth, but it is not great in every way. All of the things I will be going through are going to be based on my personal opinion. hate it, question it, love it, do what you want but do not take my words as truth and fact. Keep in mind, I have just finished the main story and plan on completing the side quests then getting the Season Pass.
Let's first talk about the biggest change, combat. Admittedly, I enjoy this combat a lot, I think it's a big step up from SoT's combat which was a lot simpler, true, but also a lot easier. This one has an XCOM-ish/Chess-ish mix into it. Does it get repetitive and boring? Yes, a little, but I always come back to it and like it even more. That's the gameplay, I enjoy it. What I have mixed reaction about was the skills/powers. If you enjoyed SoT's fun and humorous attacks that are just South Park-silly, then you'd find yourself disappointed while playing this game, because it's lacking. Now it's not completely gone, it's just... less... But overall, the combat is great.
Because this is South Park, my next point will not be about elements like graphics or story. Instead, I'll be touching on the humor. Honestly, I loved it, it is definitely less like the "old" South Park and more like the "new" South Park, but I find that it is a good mix of both. I personally like both the "old" and "new" South Park humor, so it was all "Gucci" for me.
Now let's talk story, I'll refrain myself from spouting out any spoilers. I think it's clear to everyone that the game starts out from where SoT ended (kinda), then the games every kid is playing switched from Fantasy-LOTR themed to Superhero themed. I can't go any further from here but I will say that the story starts off slow, and it eventually gets better. Not better like serious-better but more South Park-better. I do not have the same standards of story for games like, let's say, Witcher 3 compared to South Park games, clearly. I just hope that there will be a third game, based on my interpretation of the last cutscene.
The collectibles... well... let's just say I need some cure for eye cancer now. But I love it. Not in the weird way, but in like, the humorous way.
A quick talk about the soundtrack, just like SoT, it definitely has the Fantasy-LOTR/Superhero theme to it. Always a win.
Now, the cons, or supposed cons. Uplay, now, I have nothing against Uplay aside from the fact that I think Ubisoft should have a "Steam" version of their games so that players won't have to install Uplay to play the game. I know people hate Uplay a lot and I see why. I understand and respect that, but I never had any issues with Uplay or have ever really thought that Uplay was a waste of time and space, maybe I did the first time I got Uplay, but I might've slowly adapted and have gotten used to it. So I don't see Uplay as a con.
I feel the same with Denuvo, which this game also have. I never had any issues with it, I know why people dislike it, but it didn't affect me in any way. So I also don't see it as a con.
Day 1 DLCs. I understand the hate, if it was just the costume pack, I think people wouldn't hate it as much because SoT had costume packs IIRC. But it was the Season Pass that included the costume packs and extra stories, items, characters, etc. I do agree that this practice is disgustingly bad for video game companies. That is all I can say right now, I do plan on getting the Season Pass to see for myself, so an edit of this review is imminent. Edit: Well, it seems that the extra story and characters are due for the future, so right now the only Day 1 DLC is the costume pack which... SoT also have but people... nevermind...
This next one however is sort of like a collection of things that I really didn't like about this game, some I tend to ignore after the first hour or so, but still. I guess this can be categorized as Optimization, because let me explain why I said it's better to get the game on consoles, this game has been delayed countless times and the optimization is just disappointing. The first time I booted the game, I got to the character creation screen with no problem, but for some reason, the game decides to lag every time I customize my character, whether it's in the first character creation screen or whenever I go on to the costumes app while playing the game. Luckily, my time with those screens were minimized because I wore the same outfit throughout the whole game. The lag did not stop there, oh no. In some cutscenes, more specifically the Origin cutscenes, it lags everytime without fail. Sometimes, I would say maybe 1% of the time, while playing the game, traversing around the town or in combat, it would lag sometimes. Okay, so that's the lag rant. Let's talk about the things that bothered me less, dialogues that never finish in time. Here's an example that is in the game: After using Kyle as a buddy in the town, Kyle will say "Damn, my whole outfit reeks now, thanks a lot." but  right before he ends that sentence, he says "Time to fly!", so the two dialogues overlap a little. But that's just a small example, it happens with other dialogues with other characters as well. But again, it didn't bother me a lot. One last thing, sometimes when combat starts or during combat, it freezes for a second before it continues.
That being said, I did enjoy this game, a lot. It was what I expected and a little more but it was brought down by the delays that were supposed to optimize the game. Do I think it's better than SoT? Ehhh, I would say not as good all things considered. So at the moment, I recommend getting the game on console rather than PC.

I am torn about this game. I liked the new grid based combat system, but I disliked that your character only had 4 powers to use at a time, which you could not customise (except for stat boosting your character with artifacts, which makes certain moves more/less powerful). It would have been fun to make this game more RPGish, so maybe an upgrade system for the powers, which improves AoE, damage, status effects, etc. In the stick of truth one could upgrade his weapon, which added a little more depth.
Speaking of RPGish, the RPG elements in this game are a bare minimum. You get to chose your whole character sheet, from gender to sexual orientation to race and ethnicity. However, as far as I know this does not do anything. I can't  know for sure however, because numerous information pop-up texts were bugged, and there was no actual text in them.
The game keeps the 'new kid' (the player) a silent protagonist, just like in the first game. In the first game you got to chose sides later in the game, but here there are no choices to be made.
Side quests are all either fetch quests, or collection quests, and not very interesting (except for one involving a gay fish).
The main quest I liked very much, up until a certain point. It is a very simple story in search of a missing cat, to get the $100 reward, but after finding said cat it quickly blows up to something much bigger, which I found sad, because I think South Park really shines when it is just kids doing kids stuff. I did not enjoy the final third of the game, because it felt quite rushed.
All in all, I'd say the game is not worth the full price. I'd say wait for a sale.

Firstly, I'd like to preface this review saying I am the oldest in my family. I only have one sibling and she is my sister. Now on to the review:
A Tale of Two Sons follows two sons (who'd have guess'd) as they attempt an epic quest to save their sick father. This game is very interesting in it's control scheme. You actually control both bothers at the same time with both analog sticks. There is a bit of two sides of the brain working at the same time thing going. It's a little weird, very innovative, and slightly awkward. Everytime I thought I have the ability to control them both with no worries I'd run into a curve in the road or some other obsticle that would have me sending both brothers in opposing directions.  That said, there is not a lot of times when you have to control each bother in independant direction; so it works out fairly well.
The game is super short. Took me 2hrs to beat and another hour to get all the achievments. However the game is made very well, and the graphics and puzzles are nicely done. I do think some more variety of puzzles or longer story would have definately helped, but I would rather have 2 hours of a great game vs 16 hours of a mediocre one.
Now on the the emotional aspects of this game. SLIGHT SPOILERS: I never felt emotionally invested in this journey. This game seems to spawn from the idea that the player's will feel deep emotions. I actually did not. Perhaps because of my relationship in my own family tree? I think if you are a younger brother this game may induce more emotion, but then again I can't say for certain. What I can say for certain is that the emotional tie-in felt overly pushed at times, disjointed others, and campy the next
All in all, this is a good game and worth a play through. It won't inspire tears like Papo and Yo did. The puzzles won't leave you feeling stupid like Limbo did. However, it's enough of what's good to recommend a purchase.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons.... wow.. just.. wow. Such feels.
Now THAT'S how you tell a story.
Amazingly beautiful game, yet so sad..
It's a very short game, but I'm glad they didn't feel the need to drag things out unnecessarily for the sake of length. I don't feel cheated by it only being 3 hours long - it's very cinematic, and the gameplay is quite simplistic platform puzzle solving with an interesting twist (that being that you control both brothers simultaneously via each thumbstick on a gamepad).
It's possible this game could easily have been an animation rather than an interactive game, but there were many nice touches that felt more personal when performing them yourself.. and the ending, well.. without saying too much, the mechanics work to increase the impact.
Sound design and music was also awesome, definitely a new favourite. Interestingly, Simon Viklund (composer of the PAYDAY 1 & 2 soundtracks, also favourites of mine) contributed to the score. It's strange, because all of his other work is intensely electronic and quite heavy stuff.. talk about having a wide range!
Also interesting is that, though the characters barely talk (and what few words are exchanged are in a language I can't identify.. possibly a made up one, but you generally get the gist of what they are saying), the story is conveyed very well - there's never any confusion as to what people are feeling or what they are trying to tell you/each other. You know that's some good storytelling when all the information you need can be communicated without words.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons, is very possibly one of the best games I've played purely from the point of it's complete self-integration. The gameplay, the narrative, the atmosphere and scenery all add to the overall experience. Whilst not completely original in idea, it is original in execution.
The gameplay done via a controller is nothing short of superb. Both characters are controlled via both directional sticks of a single controller. Whilst it's awkward to get used to at first, I had both brothers running in completely opposite directions on numerous occasions, it adds a co-operative feel to what is essentially a single player game. The mechanics creating and emphasising the co-operation and relationship between the Brothers themselves, as independently controlled but still reliant on the gamer's ambidexterity.
The narrative is subtle yet no less emotional for being so. This is achieved by the importance of showing the audience rather than telling, so the distinct choice to remove dialogue and "tell" the story through visual aids (read body language) and integrated cut-scenes of events is nothing short of brilliant. Each interaction and challenge that the two boys overcome leads to greater involvement in their supportive relationship, and even as just a witness to the relationship the player feels involved as the instrumental force behind their achievements.
Other characters within the world offset the two brothers, from incidents of being bullied and bullying themselves to acts of compassion and friendship, each additional interaction adds to and assists our understanding of the two boys. Their development as characters and the imaginative world-building adds up to an immersive experience that is thoroughly enjoyable.
The fairytale like world itself is fascinating, whilst we witness stereotypes, there are enough non-cliched characters to offset the tale as a whole, and overall the story of loss and grief gains a veneer of the beauty of life for being presented in this format.
The world itself is gorgeously rendered, the style adopts a medium between realism and a more cartoonist-storybook style. While the graphics will date, it has enough artistic leeway in not adopting a purely realistic stance that it will still be pleasant if not beautiful to look at in years to come.
The game is unfortunately very short. It runs about twice the duration of a movie, and there is little replayability value, as the narrative is self-contained. The only reason to replay would be similar to the reason why we return to a good book again and again. To experience the message and overall story again because it has become a beloved addition to our personal experience.

I bought this quite early on with some friends as we really liked the idea behind it. At first it was a bit awkward and there were a fair few bugs (it's early access so that's expected), but it's certainly fun and has even more potential. We played for about 18 hours before we kind of got bored of its problems and wanted to wait for an update to fix them. And here it is! We're going to play it again now, and I thought it'd only be fair to recommend it now while it's on sale. It's worth sticking with this game, especially if the developers are going to stick with it too; this update has certainly addressed a lot of the problems that we were having at the start, and I'm looking forward to seeing where it goes in the future.
EDIT: after playing it for some time with the newest update, I think that it has improved massively. It feels more like an RPG, with better loot and harder enemies (the ghost island gives you the opportunity to fight hard enemies and earn some loot way ahead of your level), and it's still beautiful as a sandbox. There are still some bugs, being early access (but the auto-save seems to work well, as it's crashed a few times and I've never lost anything), but it's less buggy than it was.
At this point, there are good points and bad points, which I think it's only fair to list, if only to put forward my opinions on the early access:
PROS:
+Beautiful game, great design and lighting.
+Fun fighting mechanics and great variety within classes (although Melee still seems at a bit of a disadvantage).
+Fun to farm for resources and loot. Incorporating more random drops in the last update, having to search for certain recipes and armour sets, has made playing much more rewarding.
+Good progression. You always feel like you're going somewhere, making your way towards something, a new weapon, or a boss, or some rare armor.
+Events in the latest update completely changed the feel of the game. It's a chance to test yourself against harder enemies and get worthwhile rewards. This update came with better loot drops as well, so certain enemies will randomly give you great stuff.
+Island size. I'm putting this in here because some people say (or used to say) that the islands are too small. I don't think they're too small. Some of them are very large. I think that they're the perfect size (and depth) for this type of game - you need to explore them and move on, not get stuck on one island for too long wondering if you've missed anything.
=Variety. This is a pro and a con. The variety of islands is really good, overall - there are several islands types in each section of the game (between bosses). Finding a new type of island is exciting, and exploring the first couple of that type is good because they do have slightly different resources. But there are too many of some types in each section, and eventually, you portal into a new island, realise that it's got the same resources and enemies as the last two, and don't bother to explore it. This is usually only for the last few islands before the boss, after you've already got all the resources you can get in that section of the game, but I'm sure that as the game develops the variety will, inevitably, improve.
CONS:
-Some bugs, getting stuck in chests, crashes, but it's to be expected in early access (and nothing gamebreaking).
-Repeated islands, as aforementioned.
-Dungeons aren't great; the first time you do a type of dungeon, it's fine, but there isn't much variety (much like the islands they're on), and the loot isn't really good enough to make it worth going through one.
-Sandbox controls. Block placement and breaking isn't always smooth, and items have a tendency to bounce around into odd places; it needs some tweaking. But variety is good so far and you can build some cool stuff.
-Poor wiki. I know that this isn't anything to do with the game, but as the game becomes more like an rpg, with things like random drops, it's harder to know what to look for without a decent wikipedia or forum to help you out (think: Terraria). I suppose it depends how much random drops come into it, but to develop as an RPG it's probably going to get more complicated, and looking things up to do is part of the fun.
TL;DR: before the update this game was ok, neither a great RPG, nor a great sandbox. Now it's really showing us what it's capable of, and it's pretty good at both. I hope it continues to get better, but it's worth playing NOW.

In short: Post Apocalyptic Mayhem (PAM) is a combat racing game where the players race ad-hoc battle machines through various sandblasted locales, with the ultimate goal being to rack up as many kills as possible within five minutes.
Since this is a driving game, lets talk about the vehicles first. Generally speaking, the smaller the vehicle, the more "zippy" and easier-to-control it feels. Larger vehicles trade in control for weapon power and the ability to take a beating. Not exactly the most original concept, but it's reliable and makes perfect sense within the apocalyptic setting.
The driving mechanics themselves do not do a good job of conveying a sense of speed. Even when using Nitrous, you're never going to feel like you're breaching 50 MPH - as a result, when you manage to catch some big air in a race, it's going to feel like your vehicle has very "floaty" physics. As a veteran player of
,
,
and
, this
irritates me.
On the plus side, there is very little overlap between each vehicle's unique weapons. There are four types of weapon pickups you can collect, each color reponding to either extra fuel for your boost meter, or front-facing, side-facing, and rear-facing weapons. Though most side-weapons tend to be "a bunch of miniature bombs", the front and rear weapons are almost always totally unique for each vehicle. As a result of each vehicle requiring a different playstyle, there is actually a huge amount of strategy in picking which vehicle you'll use during a race. I've become rather fond of the Nucloid vehicle myself.
The overall level design is very, very good. There are six unique tracks, and a seventh Christmas-themed reskin of the first track.  Each level contains wide-open spaces, chokepoints, and multiple routes. Very rarely will there be a part of the track where you can't come up with a plan on-the-fly.
My one complaint track-wise is that three of the game's tracks - Wasteland, Cold War Beach, and Airplane Cemetary - all have very bland aesthetics. The latter two have
interesting architecture, but Winter Wasteland is about ten times more interesting than regular Wasteland despite being little more than a reskin. The other tracks - Urban Jungle, Death Area 8, Abandoned Sawmill, and (again) Winter Wasteland have far more interesting aesthetics and are generally more fun to race on as a result.
The soundtrack is... generic. Though the genre of each background song varies, they really don't add anything to the overall feel of the game. Once again, the exception being Winter Wasteland's background music, which is actually pretty damn epic for a
remix.
The A.I. in this game can actually be surprisingly skilled, though there is just a touch of rubberbanding involved in their programming. Playing on hard difficulty can result in most players earning an average score of around eight kills (which is a hell of a lot). Though you'll find virtually no online games being hosted, going a few rounds with friends is when this game shines at it's brightest.
If this game happens to go on sale for a decent price, I urge you to give it a shot. It's not
, but it is a fun romp nonetheless.

Oh well. One last thing we agree on: This was merely an overture, the real adventure is just getting started. But personally, I’m very excited about that.

A short review of South park: The Fractured But Whole. This is a sequel to Stick of Truth but it's not necessary to have played Stick beforehand. But it really helps if you're a fan of the TV show. I would not recommend this game to people who don't know wtf South Park is. At the time of this review the game has 2 DRM measures separate from Steam. It has Denuvo (anti-piracy) and requires Uplay (Ubisoft client). Xbox or PS4 Controller is highly recommended for play, especially for the mini-games and QTEs. Still playable with keyboard but wasn't as enjoyable for me so I switched back to my xbox controller.
Fractured But Whole plays like a semi-open world RPG. That world being the town of South Park Colorado. The Comedy in it is subjective but personally I didn't find it as well written or as funny as Stick of truth and that's most likely becaue Obsidian wasn't involved in this one. The combat is strategy based. Battles are initiated through Touch encounters and play out on a grid much like a final fantasy tactics game or Disgaea. But much more simple and streamlined. In fact the combat was the highlight of the game for me and I liked it much more than the combat in Stick of Truth. I would recommend playing it on Mastermind difficulty if you want any challenge. There are also ways to augment your battle strength in way of Artifacts you can craft, buy or find from enemy loot drops. As you level up you unlock more artifact slots which will increase your overall Might ranking.
There are plenty of sidequests to be completed, collectibles to be found and mini-games to be played. All the characters you love and hate are in this game, Fractured contains the largest cast of characters in any South park game to date. My completion time was around 35 hours and Stick of Truth was around 17 hours and that included the DLCs too.
So the question is would I recommend it? 100% recommendation to South Park fans, don't pass on this game. Even if a lot of people including myself may agree that Stick of Truth is still better, that by no means makes Fractured a BAD game. It's still better than most of the triple A titles that are out right now.

I haven't played the first one, as it was until last month an xbox exclusive, nor Dead Rising 2 because from what i had been told, Off the Record was the exact same game but improved on a few points. That is why I won't compare it to the previous installments.
As an entry to the series, and even though I knew what to expect, I had a really good time playing through. Lots of weapons, bosses, and a story that brings up some funny situations for a game that never takes itself seriously.
Add to that a few vehicles, some of which can be modified with weapons to plow through zombies even more easily or just travel the map faster.
The time limit means you probably won't be able to save everyone (at least your first playthrough) as each survivor requires some conditions to be fulfilled or specific items to agree to follow you, and those often take you far away, too far sometimes to come back in time.
The AI is alright, they will get stuck here and there and you will have to wait for them before each loading zone but overall they don't ruin the experience and provide a sense of life in a map infested by the dead.
For those who want to play without time limitations, there is now the "sandbox mode" which allows you to play on the same map, as Frank and with the same level of experience you have in the story and lets you do what you want, even level up to make the story easier or gather more cash without wasting the precious time of the story mode.
Finally, you can also play in co-op and join a random person online to help them or just mess about as you both kill zombies by the dozen.
A great experience, fun, entertaining, and something you can always come back to for a few hours.

With every 16-bit type rpg one of the most important elements is the story ---- the fundamental narrative to maintain interest, the pacing to avoid boredom, and the character development to add some fun are all very important, and all of these aspects are nicely tied together in "Ashes of Immortality".
The game is quick to start and the first dungeon of many is at hand, and the adventure begins as Simona (a hunter) travels throughout a large world inhabited by vampires of all types, werewolves, ghouls, and a host of other supernatural creatures. She will recruit allies along the way each of whom has their own story to explore as bonds are formed and personalities develop.
There are many battles along the way, but they never overpower the actual story, and the game does a good job of keeping your interest in what is going to happen next ---- and there are, indeed, lots of surprises.
Each area is nicely presented ---- towns, dungeons, woods, etc. ---- and all need to be carefully explored for the treasures to be found.
Music is nicely done, stays in the background yet adds to the structure of the game.
In addition to the main story, there are many side quests to do, all of which offer good rewards for completion.
All of the characters, including the npcs, are interesting, entertaining, and are easy to like ---- even the somewhat eccentric ones.
There are a great many things to like here, and I think anyone that enjoys the 16-bit type rpgs will have a great time with  this well told tale.

Early Access Watcher Reviews Portal Knights
Update Version: 0.2.2
Disclosure: This game copy was bought by the reviewer
The first time I heard about this game, I was skeptic. Anytime someone mentions "like Minecraft" to me I instantly turn off. I will admit, I am probably one of the few humans left that has yet to play Minecraft in one form or another, but when you had to endure the massive praise the game received over the past couple of years you don't really need too. I am not saying Minecraft is terrible by my lack of experience with it, but the idea of creating something from nothing can be a little daunting for some. Thankfully, as soon as I started playing Portal Knights, I discovered that the option is not possible with what is offered and managed to focus on the task of reaching the final island.
The one thing I can say right of the bat is how wonderful the visuals look. With a genre overburdened by a visual style of blocky low resolution fodder, it is refreshing to see characters and enemies at least look like something other than boxes and rectangles. The colorful atmosphere and cartoonish aesthetic gives each foe a charming sense of gleeful villainy while giving the player a character that can range from sourpuss to overexerted flower child. It is simple, but effective.
The world has enough detail to provide a distinct look while maintaining the needed box upon box construction. Trees at least look like trees, bushes like bushes, ore sticks out of dirt and it all works with the quirky music to emulate something you would find from a 90s era children's cartoon. The major downside, however, is the lack of variation in the biospheres. You get a few types (desert, snow, magma, forest, space) that repeats with new materials and the different skin variants of the same enemies you fought the last island. Diverse locations is crucial for a game stretched over several islands and when you have seen the same looking area on repeat, it gets old.
Combat suffers from this issue as well when you take the lack of monster diversity into account. Combat relies on a camera lock system that causes your character to stop moving when striking. For melee, this can be a major problem when you can find yourself mid strike and unable to roll out of the way of an attack. Rangers and Mages can simply find high ground and watch as the AI causes the enemy to simply hug a wall as you lay into it. Bosses are rather similar, with a add phase, hit weak spot to stun while you lay into phase and a retort phase. They would be a lot more fun if they didn't repeat the same two attacks in the same order constantly. The bottom line: combat becomes very dull, very fast. Considering this is half of what you do in this game, means you can get bored or the repetition fast.
Crafting and gathering is the second half of this uneven pizza with an overflowing portion of cheddar. Gathering consist of consumables, plants, ores, wood and gems that all (except wood) have tier variants as you progress further on the island map. Different types of crafting tables are used with each one requiring upgrades to unlock the better recipes. Monsters also drops parchment with recipes as well. The trouble comes in with the limited amount of resources available on each island and the amount needed to make ore into bars rises with each tier.
Base building is also an option with doors, fences and cosmetics such as book cases and beds. Dungeons also exist on each island with special chests and hidden portals. Each portal requires six of a special item that is crafted from fragments dropped by enemies or randomly when gathering. This one aspect can be extremely tedious and makes reaching the last few islands a pain. Max level is 30 right now and 44 islands. The downside, however, is once you kill the third boss there really is no incentive to keep exploring outside of achievements. It feels like a chore just reaching the third boss honestly with the amount of time spent collecting the shards for each portal. It is fun for a couple of hours, but right when you beat the second boss and see the first space looking environment, you have seen it all.
Now, mechanically the game is a seesaw. I have had a perfect experience half the time while the other few sessions have been a nonstop frame rate drop with crashes ranging from opening a chest to entering a new island. It is very inconsistent, which I guess could be a positive, but the fact it happens at all is grating on the nerves. Staying connected with friends can be an issue too with random disconnections, but whether this is the game or Steam is another question. The UI runs into some issues as well when transferring goods to chests, crafting or accessing inventory, but this is more a quality of life issue. Glitches can occur ranging from getting stuck between blocks (just destroy a block to free yourself) to bugs that make my character run non stop. The game client also has an issue where it opens up minimized and cannot be seen on screen unless I maximize it through Task Manager. It just gets really annoying.
Outside of the beautiful visuals (although redundant after awhile), I just couldn't get myself to play this after I finished the Ghost off at the end. It was hard enough pressing myself to push on once I finished my set of Iron equipment. I am not sure how much this game is similar to Minecraft, but it reminded me a lot of survival simulators and that is never a good thing. The lack of a purpose outside getting from A to B makes it hard to feel accomplishment or a sense of purpose; now that I think of it, there really is no story to this outside the introduction cutscenes. With it's technical problems, simple combat and tedious progression, I cannot recommend the game at this time.
Pros
- Charming aesthetic
- Music is delightful
Cons
- Crashing and Frame rate dips
- Simple, tedious combat
- Lack of diverse content
- No real incentive to keep playing once third boss is killed

Train Simulator 2017 is a very realistic and fun game to play. I enjoy playing it, but sometimes it freezes for no reason. I have almost 20 DLC's and I find them very fun to mess around with in the Scenario/World Builder.
PRO's:
1.) Very realistic
2.) Giant range of DLC's, for people with different tastes. (eg: Steam, Diesel, (Or For Me, Electric)
3.) Very smooth when it does work.
4.) Although some may say this is a CON, I think it is a PRO, that this game is a time consumer!!!!! :) (Look at my total hours gameplay for the game!!)
CON's:
1.) Sometimes freezes on OS's that so far exceed the games minimum reccomended requierments. (MRR)
2) The DLC's, (IN MY OPINION) are majorly OVER priced. (Don't get me wrong, it does take a while to 3D model all the trains and build all the routes and stuff, but we could do that ourselfs and I just think if they lowered the prices more people would buy DLC, meaning they would have EVEN more money.)
3.) No ability for 'Custom Content' (Station signs, trains (& Liverys) etc....)
4.) No ability for Multi-Player and walking around. If they added walking around like TSW/WOS3, and Multi-Player it would be more fun!!
OVERALL I rate this game: 9.2 / 10 :D

I've owned this game on my PS3 for two years, and despite a few breaks, have played the daily challenge almost every day ever since then. Spelunky is a masterpiece of puzzle design and exploration. This is a game that literally changes genre as you get better at it, making it so, so hard to get tired of. When you start its just an overly difficult puzzle platformer, but once you realise the world has extremely consistent rules and patterns, deeper the rabbit hole goes. Bats become moving bouncy platforms, giant horrifying spiders become sticky-web vendors and rats become the ultimate trap-triggering, arrow baning godscend. It's a VERY steep learning curve, and not everyone will get past the frustrating amount of platforming precision required.
Spelunky will break you many, many times. But each time you rebuild yourself, you realise you're evolving your playstyle and are becoming completely different erudite beast.
