If you were stuck on a planet filled with nothing but junk and surrounded by idiots you’d want to escape right? Well if so then this is the game for you.
Help poor Rufus make his dream a reality and escape the junk ridden world of Deponia and make it all the way to the lofty heights of Elysium a floating city high above. And along the way meet a few new friends and enemies to boot. The story is pretty good and full of jokes and gags. I loved the writing and thought it was very well done. The characters are great too, each adding to the overall zaniness.
Deponia is a point a click game and as such the gameplay is pretty standard for the genre. The puzzles are not overly challenging but you may well be stumped a few times on the journey but each and every time you figure it out you feel pretty darn good. Clicking on everything that seems interesting to find all the needed objects and combining items together to overcome every obstacle can be very satisfying.
The game looks great; the art style is very unique and cartoony. Every set piece, character and item all fits nicely into the decaying world in which the game takes place. I loved exploring people’s homes and seeing what was used to build such wacky places. The game runs great, but as mentioned it’s a cartoon so there isn’t much the computer needs to generate. The game sounds great too; the music is fun and catchy. The sound effects are pretty comical and fit well in the title and every character is very well acted. I thought they all worked well together.
Although not ground breaking or particularly long it is a thoroughly enjoyable title from start to finish. I had great fun with it. At full price it’s a little steep but that being said if you like point and click or love the way the game looks or the comedy then go ahead and dive in. For the rest of us I’d wait for a sale, but it’s worth a look and will give you a few laughs.
Have fun ^_^

Heard about this game from youtube. Did some research, and bought it on sale in steam. Before I played, I donned the traditional gopnik flat cap and slav squatted for the whole game. I played this game with NO fixes. NO mods. Master difficulty. You drop into the game with a little cinematic, and it looks... EEEEH. You spawn in and these random science gopniks tell you "you should be dead but you're not so get gun and go in swamp ♥♥♥♥♥."
At this point I had no idea what was going on, so I got my gun, and headed into swamp. Instantly, I noticed my main gun had 30 rounds of ammo, and this sets precedent for the entire game. You have NO AMMO. And, to make things worse, all the guns are peashooters that, even with a 1.6x scope, you can't hit a dinner plate from 10 yards.
So the thing that made this game unique was it's AI system and environment. The AI is so cool, fighting it out even when you aren't there. securing the swamp for the science gopniks was easy because they did all the work for me. But as soon as I thought AYYY this isn't as hard as people say, I made it out of the swamp and went to the cordon. This game does not hold your hand. it doesn't tell you "go north to avoid the gun" it says "FIGURE IT OUT YOURSELF ♥♥♥♥♥" as I went north, I encountered a squad of Renegades. All I had was a hunting rifle, which is GARBAGE at ranges, and one of them had a Viper 5. It took me 30 minutes to defeat them. this is where you get introduced to your good friends f5 and f9.
F5 quicksaves. You should do this A TON. The game never autosaves, and added onto the difficulty, this can be hell. But if you get past that one squad that you've been fighting after 15 minutes, the feeling is SO GREAT. Skipping ahead, I had arrived at Agroprom, and I joined duty and beat freedom. After that, I headed to the place that enters the Red Forest. that's where the atmosphere really hit me. It's so good looking and fits perfectly. For all this complaining I cannot reccomend this game enough. The game is hard, but it rarely is unfair.
EDIT: After thinking the review over, I am changing my review to an 8/10. This game has some flaws. I haven't tried SOC, but with this game, my hopes could not be higher.

It was a cold morning, we were on the truck heading to the base where i was stationed. We had stopped at a small outpost for supplies when it had happened. At first there was silence but then like magic enemies came pouring out of the woods. We held our ground refusing to give in. We fought and fought for almost and hour before the enemy ranks finally turned back and retreated into the woods. We knew there was little time before they struck again.  I sat down to catch my breath, that had been my first taste of real combat.
We all geared up and mantled a retalliation force. I hit the road early to scout so we weren't ambushed again, But that was my mistake. A small squad of the Nazi force jumped out and started shooting at me. I managed to dodge most of the bullets but i caught one in the left arm putting it out of commission just before diving into cover. I pulled out my pistol and fired blindly at the enemy to buy myself some time. I patched myself up as quickly as humanly possible and listened to see if they were waiting for me to appear, but all i heard was silence. I poked my head out only to see a pile of dead nazis where they ambushed me. As i stood in the road astonished with how I was alive my Squadron appeared from over the hill. I waved them down and hopped on the back of the truck at the convoy rear. the medic quickly looked at my arm and gave me a nod of approval. Clutching my gun tightly I mentally prepared myself for the fight to come.
The convoy stopped and the men beside me unloaded and headed into the woods to take positions around the enemy camp. I lagged behind slightly feeling a little unerved from the combat I had already faced. This isn't what i had signed up for, Pain, Death, Blood and Tears. This isn't anything I imagined it would be, This is Hell. I mustered up the courage to join my companions. We hid in the cover of the forest, observing the enemy encampment. The squad leader signalled us the order to take aim. With bated breath we all lay there waiting for the command to fire our sights trained on the nazis below. Finally, after what seemed to be an eternity, our squad leader gave us the order to fire. All hell broke loose as the thundering of a thousand shots being fired. We fought the enemy back and we were so close to driving them out. My hope surged there was no losing this battle. I stood on the road firing my pistol at the receding ranks of nazi soldiers when I heard a short shrill ringing. I turned to face the origin of the sound but it was too late. All I saw was the brief glimpse of a Nazi on a bicycle ram into my abdomen and knock me to the ground. He proceeded to run me over continuously until the lights started to go dim. As my vision started to fade, The nazi dismounted the bicycle and walked over to my frail broken body. He stood over me with a sinister smile on his face. he crouched up and down several times shoving his sweaty taint into my face over and over. I felt my body breathe it's last as his butt was pushed up against my face. I opened my eyes to see a black void and a message saying "You have been killed by xXxn0obSlayer69xXx, Respawning in 10 seconds."
10/10 would be killed by xXxn0obSlayer69xXx on a bicycle again.

The gameplay, while nothing spectacular, is still pretty fun and intuitive. There was one small part of the game that I found frustrating involving diving underwater that I failed at and had to retry 10+ times, but the rest of the game controlled well. Playing with an Xbox-style controller, my right thumb occasionally got sore or uncomfortable -- you are constantly using both thumbsticks in this game, so you really do notice the effect of having two sticks at different positions. The game's story is compelling enough, and is also good at subverting expectations, so even when you know what's coming, you aren't really sure until it happens. The game is long enough to last a few sittings, while staying short enough that it never feels like it's dragging on (according to Steam, I completed the game and all achivements in 3.7 hours). Overall, worth checking out if you want to adventure through some amazing environments.

This is a beautiful game. The key for me was that it's LIKE Minecraft, only....better. Certainly it's a cube world, but with much prettier people and monsters. I also am a really big fan of the local multiplayer feature, which has allowed my whole family to cooperatively play together in the same world. My boyfriend and I had been searching for just such a game.
While the main objectives are simple (find the portals, activate them, visit all the islands, beat up the bosses), there is room to self-initiate other quests. I myself have set goals to craft all the best armor and weapons in the game, and build houses in each biome (using as exclusilvely as possible resources from that biome alone).
All the boss fights are repeatable, which is excellent given the invaluable item drops. I never would have gotten the equipment I have without them.
Needless to say, I am breathlessly awaiting the day when more content is released.

If you like Terraria and/or Minecraft, you will most likely love this game. I don't have a lot of time invested, but so far I really like it.
HOW THE GAME WORKS:
1. You can choose from 3 different classes. Essentially a knight, archer and mage. You gain abilities, weapons and armor sets as you lvl up and progress through each world level.
2. There are 44 worlds to progress through. each have their own theme, enemies and resources. (There are also boss worlds.)
3. The idea is to explore an area, mine its resources then find and repair the portal to the next realm (Sometimes more than one portal.)
4.You can build homes, various workstations, tools, weapons, armor, spells and potions.
The only bad thing I can say, (And this is my opinion.) is that each realm is very small. It takes 15-20min to explore each one. That being said, there are 44 realms and you have to go back to previous realms for specific resources at times, so you get decent use out of most realms. And to be honest it is kind of exciting trying to hurry and get to the next area, because you have no idea what it is!
Also take into account this game is in testing. I personally think this game has a lot of potential.
PROS:
Nice visuals.
Good progression system.
Engaging gameplay.
Really fun co-op play.
CONS:
Some bugs and crashes. (To be expected.)
Small areas.

I was around when games like Space Quest, Kings Quest, Police Quest, Leisure Suit Larry, etc. were the popular games that basically popularized the "point and click" genre.  As such, I still enjoy these types of games and it's nice to see someone making them again.  That said.......
I like the art style in the game, I like the music, sound effects, and all of that.  I can deal with a slow moving character, as hair pulling as it may be sometimes.  My only real complaint with this game is, unfortunately, what it's about and that is solving puzzles.
I like solving puzzles and I like a challenging puzzle as much as the next person.  Where these games generally excelled in the past is that while challenging, you were still provided sufficient clues to figure out how to get through the games.  This was back in the days before the internet, walk through guides, Youtube videos, and all of that stuff.  Where this game has infuriated me is the puzzles - I do not think that I should have to consult walk through guides in order to complete a game and that is what I find myself doing time and time again.  Judging from other reviews, so have other people.  Again, there was a time where you could find clues in the environment or failing that, after a few failed attempts, your character might offer something helpful - not here.
You will need to backtrack to areas that you thought you were done with and generally don't get any prompting to go back to (or even know you can get back to).  You will sometimes need to go back to the same room multiple times in order to find items that should have all been available the first time you were there (unlockables or things of that nature notwithstanding).  You will be required to interact with certain things in the environment, that you thought you were done with, multiple times in order to proceed (I'm not giving examples so as not to ruin for those who haven't played it yet).  There are times where you may have to manipulate the same nonplayable character multiple times to achieve the desired result (with no prompting or hinting that this is necessary to ultimately elicit the required response/result).  The mini games present inside the main game give you no prompting, clues, or hints as to what you are supposed to do to get them to work or how to solve them in most cases.  There are times where you click on everything in the environment and try using everything in your inventory, just to find out none of it works because you didn't realize you have to backtrack to the beginning of the game or some other area you thought you were done with to proceed.  Of course there are other times where what you are supposed to do is blatantly obvious  - I just wish they could have found a middle ground someplace with this.
So for those reasons, I am not recommending this game.  If you don't mind having to cheat to get through the game by consulting walk through guides, then give it a shot if it's on sale or offered as a bundle.

What do you know.... WB and NetherRealm actually managed to get this port fixed. I uninstalled this so long ago due to bugs ruining the playability of this game even when I did manage to get the game to play just fine on my system (and it was below the recommended requirements- it is a laptop). It just kept going to slow motion and would never go back to normal speed. I wanted to forget about this game and move on. I wanted to leave Mortal Kombat and fighting games due to such a bad experience.
Then, once Injustice 2 was on the verge of release, I got curious about MKX again. I sold off a PS4 copy I had because of PTSD from this version. I played MKX on an Xbox One with some people that were around (it was a public place) and I started to remember how much fun the game was. The characters were great, the moves fun to use, and the fatalities are just as gory as you would expect from Ed Boon and his team. But that PC port? I didn't want to think of it.
It was when I decided to clean my computer up did I decide to reinstall MKX. It had received its XL patch and the reception for this version got better from what I noticed. How would my below recommended requirements PC handle the game with the XL update?
Well, the slow motion is still there, but it only happens on occasion, Even then, I could simply pause the game for a few seconds, maybe look at some moves and try to memorize their combinations, then go back to the game and the speed would be restored. After the Jason patch so long ago, that wouldn't happen. But now I could stop it.
When I booted it up, I was stunned by the quality of the port two years after release. The graphics are much better now, even on lower settings, and the gameplay runs fast and frantic. And I started to have fun again. I started to have fighting marathons again where I would just pick two characters and just fight. After that fight was done, I would pick two more and have them fight. Then another. Then another. It's non-stop fun.
I don't have Kombat Pack 2 on PC, but with seeing this version now? I think I have $20 burning a hole somewhere...
At least now, I can have some sort of closure with this game. FATALITY LIVES AGAIN!!!!

Disappointing compared to SoC. The upgrade system is a cool idea, but is implemented oddly. Your weapons flat out suck until you invest thousands of rubles in upgrades. You won't be able to headshot an enemy standing twenty yards away with many stock weapons. The pistols and shotguns you start out with seem to shoot weaponized cotton candy bullets.
There's no more magic to exploring and getting ambushed by an unseen enemy. As part of the faction wars system, pretty much every enemy shows up on the map, even mutants.
Faction wars itself is a huge disappointment. It's a cool idea implemented horribly. Forget Duty and Freedom, it seems that every faction is out for turf! They even turned Loners into a faction. Loners are not a faction, they're the absence of a faction! Beyond the lore issues, there's also gameplay issues.
I'll capture an outpost and use a bunch of ammo because my stock AR has like a three foot spread at twenty meters. The enemy faction will then constantly send squads to take back that position. Naturally, the men defending it get whittled away, and I'm likely in no position to help. I was taking over the main bandit base in Garbage, only to have all my work be for nothing because bandits captured the southwest entrance for the billionth time. It's a huge test of patience.
Did I mention the grenade spam? Because there's tons of it. Enemies throw a lot of grenades and have amazing accuracy with them. It reaches CoD: WaW levels of stupid with its grenade spam.
The story is nothing special. I looked it up out of frustration with the game. The most important thing it does is explain why Strelok ended up brainwashed at the start of ShOC, which I didn't care much about. The Clear Sky faction doesn't matter much in the larger lore.
At least I got this game in a sale. The way I look at it, I got Call of Pripyat for 50% off and Clear Sky for free. Speaking of which, I'm moving on to Call of Pripyat now, supposedly the series' magnum opus. Hopefully it's better than this.

If you enjoy any kind of backcountry skiing or exploring, this game is for you.
The jibbing/jumps in thte parks are serviceable, but for me this game shines when you pick a crazy line down some random steep peak and just bomb it.
The challenge modes give this game plenty of replay value and encourage you to pick better and better lines. The leaderboards are a good motivator for that as well.

Early on for me, it was obvious that I needed to just uninstall this game. I like (not love) snowboarding games, from 1080 on the N64, Cool boarders on PSX, SSX and Stoked on the 360 to Steep on the PS4. Each one with great elements that make them fun to play. Snow for me, on the other hand, feels bland and pointless but the weird thing is there's no obvious or single reason why. Graphically it's fine, the soundtrack is understated (in a good way) and re-wind is a great, useful feature. The controls are easily the worst aspect, but not exactly unbearable. I think it must be a combination of the overall feel and presentation, the lack of a soul. From the off, the clean yet bland menu system makes it feel more like an impressive Google home page game instead of the start of an epic snowboarding adventure.
Despite this, I still recommend it for any fans of the genre, because it's free and you just might like it. I hope the developers enhance everything from scenary to physics, as it is far from broken and has so much potential.

As a game, Mortal Kombat X has exceeded my expectations of an MK game.
The game itself looks wonderful, the music and sounds all very satisfying and intense, the gameplay is simple but stimulating. A returning MK fan from either the 90s anthology, the 2000s trilogy, or fresh off of MK9 will be in for a lot of fun.
The controls are good, whether you use a controller or the keyboard. Very responsive, but like any PC fighting game, you'll have an ideal time with it if you're running it at 60fps. Every character has three variations, each alters their moveset a tad but enough to where you need to develop a newer playstyle with all three. Fighting game fans may be reminded of Samurai Shodown games and the Slash/Bust system or the three moon style selection of Melty Blood Actress Again. It's well done and makes returning characters still feel fresh.
The character roster has been expanded a little, the game went Street Fighter III/Garou: Mark of the Wolves where some new generation fighters come into the mix. The characters are interesting, they feel fresh, gone are the palette swapped ninja with similar movesets for old school MK fans.
For people who were fans of Mortal Kombat 2011/MK9's story mode, Mortal Kombat X is a great improvement, if you're a fan, you'll immediately be able to tell this is supposed to be a retelling of Mortal Kombat 4, but the story itself is still its own and builds off the previous game and going in a completely new direction that is entertaining.
Now then... the bad.
The game has had a rocky launch on PC. When you get this game, via Steam or even going to your local game store and picking up a retail disc, you'll still have to download the game's full size. You'll be given a 3GB preload where you can play as you download. The downside is that because this is experimental, there's problems. You need to download packs 1-29 however it's not until pack 12 where you will get your first stage to play on. The only advantage of this is that you don't need to quit the game to install the updates you're downloading, the game is updated in realtime. After the 30GB download in total, you'll need to download a 15GB patch, hopefully this will be incorporated into the initial install in the future.
Your PC settings are limited, if you want the game to look high grade to most PC enthusiast's expectations and you have the hardware to do it, you'll have to force the features yourself. Also note this game is dependent on your CPU. As of this review, I sincerely hope High Voltage Studios is looking into their code to fix this as a fighting game has no business relying on the CPU more than the GPU. Make sure your hardware is up to snuff for this game. Even on Low settings, it doesn't mean you'll be steady with something from five years ago. The online mode is being worked on, it's not perfect but for a while you may be looking for local players and even those may not be perfect lag-free matches. Something minor, the intros before a match and finishing moves at the end are locked at 30fps
I recommend this game based on what the finished product is. It's a very well done, fast paced fighting game that will keep your attention and you'll enjoy it thoroughly. But please be aware that before you buy it, your computer can handle it.
My computer specs for reference, I can run the game perfectly fine at 60fps on the highest settings at 1920x1080.
OS: Windows 7 Ultimate 64-bit
CPU: AMD FX-6300 @4.4GHz
GPU: GTX 750 Ti Superclocked 2GB GDDR5 VRAM
8GB of RAM
Stored on a secondary 7200rpm 2TB HDD

I've been playing a lot of games that have grinding involved in them, and what I greatly respect from this game is that the only rng that may occur is where certain enemies pop up and what particular recipes drop from bosses. Otherwise all enemies have a set and guarunteed drop list; it's still a grind because resource costs get more expensive as you progress, but at least you have an idea of what progress you are making and have a variety of places to farm. This is what I would love to see in other games: a ittle less random chance and more assurance.
The gamplay is pretty simple, you have to walk around each world searching for a portal to get to the next one. Each potal needs six portal blocks to power them, and the shards to make them can be found from enemies and digging. It does get to be repetitive gameplay looking over the grand scale of things, but I actually didn't mind.
The classes are well balanced from each other; all it comes down to are if you like to get up close and personal (warrior), if you like to shoot from afar and dodge (ranger), or use a bit of both and have the ability to exploit elemental weaknesses (mage).
The music is very nice and fitting of the environments.
Speaking of that, the environments are beautiful. My only gripe is that they could use some other dungeon sets, because most portals end up there and you will find yourself crawling through the same dungeon a lot.
But, again, my high point is the sense of progression and grind/farming without rng getting in your way.

Not much I can say that hasn't been said before. I felt I got my money's worth, but just barely. I'm probably more neutral on the game.
Pros
- Early game is pretty fun.
- Graphics are very nice and most of the environments are amazing (space stuff didn't do much for me though).
- No penalty for dying, which I know is controversial, but I tend to play conservatively if there are penalties which make things even more of a grind and less fun.
- Moving between the different themes was a nice suprise.
Cons
- Inventory is limited. There are so many things you are forced to collect, but almost no room for them. Chests are small as well.
- Game is likely to go free to pay (ex. timers on crafting which have no real purpose and devs have said there will not be mod support), so just know that going in.
- No story, so no real reason to explore anything once you find just one of the portals (if not dead end). I assume they are trying to be vague like minecraft to let people create their own story, but there is so much potential for making things interesting with one (all those abandoned castles).
- Unlike an RPG, you never really find an item other than crafting materials, so you have to build pretty much everything.
- Monsters are interesting starting out, but by halfway through there is nothing new. Just recoloring and resizing of existing monters (except for the one that is nearly impossible to kill for good - so annoying).
- Monster respawn in locations that are cleared (which is generally a good thing), but it means they will respawn in a build you created or tried to turn into a home. That can get annoying and makes building things less desireable.
- As far as I know you can't "use" items like new recipes without getting out of the inventory so you have to go back in a rearrange again. The new recipes were really confusing to figure out what to do with until I tried to use them in the quickbar once.
- Can't see the upgrade requirements of the various forges, alter, etc without specifically clicking on them. So when I'm grinding for the blocks I have to remember how many of something I needed.
- Can't put things on the ground, just delete. Makes juggling with the limited inventory difficult.
- Combat camera is kind of annoying. Been many a time where I didn't notice I was locked in and couldn't jump to back away in time. I'm really not sure what the advantage of the roll is versus just moving out of the way.
- I'm not sure why the day and night monsters rotate. I guess it is to bring in the monsters with glow effects but just feels very wierd to me. Especially since the night monsters are pretty much all the same from the beginning of the game (colors are different is about it).
- Monster AI is pretty weak. Stand on a post 2 blocks high and almost nothing will hit you and they just stand right below you.

A very good turn-based dungeon crawler, that I'd be tempted to call great if it wasn't for the tiny issue that a following game in the series; Elminage Gothic, is imo better.
Everyone's mileage may vary though and E:O is certainly more forgiving than Gothic. With an auto-map right from the start and less enemies that can instantly kill you in the first few dungeons, this game is a better entry point into the series than Gothic. It can still be a bit obtuse, with little in the way of explanation in-game. Be prepared to look stuff up online, probably from the comprehensive Japanese Wiki, (thank you Google translate!)
Make a party of 6 characters in the training school, form a party in the bar and then go out and explore dungeons, solve puzzles and bash monsters, all in turn based combat that has suprising depth when you understand it.
Don't go in expecting AAA graphics, but it looks better than emulating it from PSP and the translation is better. The key thing is that the gameplay is great. You get one save file, although you can save anywhere, and trying to get all the dungeons mapped out can be a tense and exciting affair. Later dungeons have all the staples you'd expect of the genre- anti-magic zones, dark zones, teleporters and more. Manage your spells, HP and items and get back alive from the depths! Levelling comes pretty fast, especially straight away, and the stat increases on levelling seem more generous than in Gothic.
There's precious few of these games being made outside of Japan, so English language versions of crawlers of this depth are few and far between. Buy it and see what all of us crawler fans find so enjoyable!

This review isn't "waaaah DRM" or "Waaaaah optional DLC that has no impact on the game at all!" I'll be going over three elements of the game for those who are interested in playing it. I won't spoil so expect a lot of details to be left out, best to find out on your own!
Story: In terms of what you'd expect from South Park this was spot on. Characters act like themselves and each are involved with the plot in great ways. While it fell off towards the end it was still very funny. What I liked the most is how the dialogue changed based on the background choices you make for your character and in some parts even changes the story with your parents.
But....
Even if it checks off as a South Park game I felt less interested than I did with Stick of Truth. It felt stale when compared to its previous installment. The magic that made the last game wasn't nearly the same as it was in this game. Not a bad story, but I felt like it gave up too much for the combat and enviremental exploration. Speaking of combat...
Combat: Off the bat I will say it is vastly superior than its previous game. How you can customize complex teams based on each encounter. The way the battle grid works while fighting something. The boss battles were kickass if i'm to put it bluntly. Great improvement and improvision from the previous game. A+
Exploration: While the combat was fantastic the exploration part... well lets say it's easily forgettable. I was sorely disappointed when I found there was no real hidden stuff when exploring. Sure you can go into other peoples hmes, but it felt more like a chore to get materials rather than a cool adventure. While the previous game did have exploration it wasn't the main focus of the game. Because it wasn't the main part of the game they were able to concentrate on the main story and side quests. That's where this game falls short immensely. While side quests exist they weren't really all that great or memorable. It was cool how they incorperated the side quests in the dialogue for the main story, but has no real meaning once that dialogue was over. I didn't feel stronger and all the extra items really didn't do much. Cool they added more things to find, but when the meaning is gone it just feels empty.
Overall: 7/10
It passes its mark on what it wanted to achieve and is worth playing. If you hate exploration then you'll probably want to avoid this game to be honest. Half the game is just exploring.

Haven't played much yet, but as a big fan of Elminage Gothic I can already see I'm going to love Elminage ORIGINAL.
A few quick impressions:
The translation is better than Gothic's so far, which is great to see (hope they continue to improve in this area for future ports.)
Some convenience features are really nice for a change of pace from Gothic's brutal dungeon-crawling (mini-map with icons makes navigating the dungeon easier, and using the map isn't tied to a consumable item, so you won't get lost as easily.)
Not a ton of settings to tweak in the settings menu but it gets the job done. Can configure a lot of small details in the UI, the speed of text in the game and more. I'm playing in 4K, which brings me to my next point.
Like Elminage Gothic, the artwork and overall aesthetic of the game is gorgeous. For a PSP port that costs less than $10, I'm impressed. The wall tiles and textures are not very high res, but the portraits and character art are really charming and beautiful even if they aren't ultra high res. It's surprising considering the port is coming from a PSP game. (Turn on Supersampling AA x8 and force on every graphical enhancement in the Nvidia Control Panel. It actually makes a difference in how the game looks, even on 4K resolution, and the game will still run great.)
The music is also lovely. Has a sort of classic JRPG vibe to it, very atmospheric as well. And there is a feature where you can change the music in-game and put your own music in each location, etc.. Cool! You can do the same for faces and character portraits, too.
As for the gameplay, it's classic Elminage. Create a party from a vast array of character choices, dive through deadly, labyrinthine dungeons collecting tons of loot, leveling up, fighting devlishly tricky monsters and groups of monsters while trying to survive and piecing together the story from NPC encounters you find and bits of mystery you pick up along the way. There are many unique pieces of gear to find and use, many different types of monsters to slay, from Giant creatures to Insect creatures and even God creatures. Lots of ways to express your creativity in how you design and outfit your characters from the large amount of races, classes and loot you can equip, and more.
One difference from Elminage Gothic is that it's a bit more open. As soon as you finish the first dungeon you are free to go all over the map to many different locations (most of which you'll die at.) You have to collect Fame by doing side quests you'll find in the various towns, which you then use to power your Compass to help find the legendary Rings of the gods and save the world. There is a lot to sink your teeth into here, and the dungeons are large with a good amount of challenge, interesting things to find, secrets and more.
I'd say if you're like me and a big fan of challenging dungeon-crawlers with turn-based combat, lots of party synergy and character development opportunities, fun exploration, looting, and survival/party management aspects in an RPG, definitely check this one out. And grab Elminage Gothic, too, if you haven't. ORIGINAL seems like a step under Elminage Gothic in challenge, so if you were put off by the somewhat brutal design of EG, this is an easier entry into the series, IMO.
Will update the review later, possibly. Thanks for reading!
P.S. Make sure to read the General FAQ and Starting Tips threads on the Steam forum! They are a must. Once you get deeper into the game you will learn it like any good RPG system, but you may also want to keep an eye on the wikipedia or look up information for the ruleset when needed.
And feel free to read my exciting antics in the very first dungeon (essentially the tutorial dungeon.) Was really something!
It's a very barebones port of the PSP version but the translation is better and the game itself is a really good dungeon crawler in the vein of the classic Wizardry games.

A story from when I had a non-Steam copy of the game, that I posted as a comment in a thread back in 2013:
"I do have one specific memory of Clear Sky being creepy.
I was wandering around in the Red Forest, minding my own business. I noticed it was getting close to night, so I made my way to the group of Duty guys at the edge of the forest. When I got there, there were 2 of them dead, and one bleeding out on the ground.
I heard dogs, and saw them dragging one of the dead bodies back into the forest. Then, I heard a bloodsucker woosh from behind, and immediately ran to the guy bleeding out, healed him, and we tried to fight together.
That didn't last long as he got killed by the bloodsucker just 5 seconds after I healed him. I ran to the building, went up the stairs, basically cornered myself to the wall, got out my shotgun, and waited until morning. Every now and then, I would think the bloodsucker was gone, try to leave, only to hear that grunting/snorting sound and a woosh again, reminding me to stay put.
Eventually, it was morning, a lone Duty guy came back to take the building over again and it was over.
Remember, this was all while it was pitch black out at night and before I even knew what a bloodsucker was."

This is going to be kind of a rambly review because... I... I... don't know. I don't know what to say about Deponia.
It's got some hilarious writing, especially for an adventure game, and I got through most of it without a walkthrough, so those are some good points.
The art in the game is spectacular. Like, really spectacular... until you get to the cutscenes, where they look like strewn-together flash animations. It still looks good enough that I can let it pass.
But... there's something about when the game says it's going to sit down, shut up, and be serious when it feels like something's amiss. The game just... can't be serious. Too much silly stuff is going on.
I really like the way the game presents itself, as sort of a set of 3 open-world-y "scenes" where you have to work out the puzzles throughout each scene, and get to see the place turn to chaos as you slowly manipulate everything for your personal gain. It also fits the protagonist very well. Hell, the protagonist is basically the epitome of adventure game protagonists. He's basically how an AGP would actually act. He's actually kind of annoying to play as sometimes for that reason, but it kind of delivers with him a message about the genre. It's silly, and really shows Daedalic's writing style.
I just feel like there's so much about the world we haven't been informed about though. I guess that's why Deponia is a trilogy, but it feels a tinge too short to make it worth being released in a trilogy.
The game is weird and silly and a whole lot of fun and hilarity, but it's just the ending that makes it fall flat, when you realize you've hit the ending and there's quite a few loose ends to tie up in the later sequels,
I
the setting in the game. It's beautiful, and I so badly want to explore it more. All the little eccentricities of the world really show itself off. Daedalic seems to be absolutely god-tier at worldbuilding, and if you really like a world that feels like it's full of life, you should check out this game. Heck, the stellar worldbuilding gets you so attached to the world that it makes a later twist in the game all that much more impactful. Too bad our protagonist doesn't share the same views.
I'll probably amend this if I ever get the other games in the series, but right now Deponia is standing as "a pretty good adventure game". I do recommend it, but be warned that what you're getting into is a little below par.

I played Deponia like I was watching a movie, beating it in the span of one day. I was so into it I even 100%ed the game too (that Droggeljug achievement though, XD). While this may not be the best way to play games, I still found it a fun enough experience to commit to completing it over the course of most of a day off (no regrets)!
Just a quick recommendation, don't be afraid to use a guide with this game. Some of the puzzles are pretty brutal and take place over a couple different areas. This isn't to say the game is unreasonable, all the puzzles are logical, but it's easy to make only a cursory look-over of an area and end up spending an unnecessary half-hour looking in other places for a small, yet important item. You can only have so much free time (cough, cough). Plus it's less satisfying to when you solve one of these "puzzles" making you think "What? That was the solution?" rather than "Yay, me and my smartness figured things out!".
Either way, this game is an engaging point-and-click adventure with a sense of prominent humor and an expansive story that goes through 2 more games. Its world and environments are very stylistic, well-contrasted and full of awesome characters (that I hope to be seeing again in the next couple installments).
Do yourself a huge favor and at least try the demo because Deponia is definitely worth a buy!

Deponia is set in a world completely over run by garbage, even being used as a junk heap for another world, Elysium. You play as Rufus, a self proclaimed 'inventor' whose only goal in life is to get off of Deponia and enter Elysium.
The world itself is gorgeous, the art style is great and the voice acting is fantastic (I was particularly in love with Captain Bozo).
However, it has it's problems. The main one being that Rufus is not a likeable character at all. At best he's an antihero. I actually found myself rooting for him to fail at times. The start of the game sees Rufus trying to create a rocket to launch himself onto one of the garbage trucks that tower overhead so he can get onto a transportation system to Elysium. He has to pack a bag first and you find lots of nagging messages around the house left by his roommate. Rufus apparently doesn't do his fair share of the housework. You later find out that his ex girlfriend is actually letting him live there for free, hoping that he'll get his act together, get a job and occasionally pick up after himself and Rufus still rolls his eyes at her and thinks she's a cow?
Anyway despite the unlikeable protagonist, the game is fun, the puzzles are interesting, if a little obscure, there are some funny parts in the game, and the rest of the characters are great

This is my first foray into the Dead Rising series, so I can't really compare it to the others. I am also writing this review as I nominated it for the "Villain most in need of a hug" award, because there are so many characters in this game that need to find Jesus (or equivalent) haha!
This particular game is a 3rd person adventure that takes place in Fortune City, a fictionalised place loosely based on Las Vegas with casinos, lights, and odd characters galore. Unfortunately however, a zombie outbreak occurs! Curiously, this is one of the few zombie games I've played where the zombies themselves are known about and already exist in the in-game world. So much so, that there is even a pharmaceutical drug called Zombrex that infected people in everyday life have to take to avoid becoming a zombie. However like I said, it gets a bit out of hand and the zombie situation spills beyond containable levels in the city. You being reporter Frank West, need to get to the bottom of this by getting out and about, leaving the sanctuary of your shelter.
The game itself is very fun, with a semi-cliche, but serviceable plot. The slighty cheesiness of the plot actually adds to the game, given it's one that clearly doesn't take itself too seriously. One of the trademarks of this game is that you can craft a huge variety of sometimes ridiculous weapons from materials found around the map. Your character will eventually collect new recipes as you progress, but you can also discover them by just experimenting. You can hit a zombie with a bucket, or use an electric powerdrill on it, or you can combine them to create a 'brain bucket' that minces any unfortunate zombie you make wear it. There's also a wide variety of different clothing combinations your character can pick up around the map.
There's also LOTS of zombies, but on the whole, they're quite docile. You, and more likely your NPC partners that follow you in parts of the game, can still get mobbed, but the massive hoard of zombies (at least initially) are fairly slow compared to some other games. At least initially anyway...
There's also quite a number of boss-like fights either as part of the main story or side-plots or events (known as Psychopaths). I found there to be a good variety between them, and some of the Psychopaths in particular are hilarious (my favourite being the Postman and Randy).
Unfortunately, the game isn't exactly without issues. It sometimes feels a bit clunky, and while technically open world, you actually get put under time pressure in the story mode if you want to do everything that comes up (and there's quite a few things). There is a sandbox mode to address this somewhat though which is nice, but not quite the same as a story mode with slightly more flexible timing in my opinion.
Also, apparently this game used to rely on GWFL, and when it was moved off that, all the DLC stopped working/appearing and this issue was never fixed. While the DLC doesn't seem to be a big deal, this kind of laziness doesn't really put the game in good light.
Overall though, I had fun with this game and would still recommend it. It usually falls to quite low prices, so be sure to get it on sale!

First off, this is the first fighting game I've play in maybe 15 years, and the first that I have ever purchased. I got inspired by watching the MK9 EVO 2014 tournaments on youtube and seeing RG SONIC FOX win MK9 and also win Injustice, then watched the Killer Instinct EVO 2014 tournament. I saw the fans watching and thought, 'yeah, that community could be something I would like to be a part of'.
Last time I played MK was MK3 PS, so that's what my exceptations were. This game is more than just a tournament against CPU enemies. It has a Krypt mini game that allows you to explore a world and unlock its secrets, there's a story mode that is flows like a book, and it has depth to it, which takes around 10 hours to complete. Maybe that's just because I'm terrible, and it will take you longer, but oh well.
Lastly, there are faction wars, where you choose a faction and gain points via different types of victories, which flow to your faction, and the faction at the end of the week (I think(?)) wins, where some type of prize goes to that faction's members. You also get faction points by defeating online players belonging to different factions.
Well, that's about it. I haven't had this much fun playing a 'new release' game in a long time, and I highly recommend this one for anyone that is looking for a full, fleshed out experience.

I have played most of the other Mortal Kombat games and at the time of writing this review I had completed the story mode on Easy and taken part in most online and towers modes.
After a rocky first few days including a dodgy new install method, split in to 29 parts but it takes at least 13 before you can actually play a game? There have also been server issues, which are still intermittently occurring at the time of writing this review.
However, ignoring these issues it is a great game. It has the usual style of Mortal Kombat characters, fatalities and arenas but upgraded for the next gen. consoles. The online mode now adds five competing factions that you can choose to join. Your game progress will count towards how they perform within a week. This leads to comradery and competition. The towers are one of the most interesting elements with races against other players whilst random effects applied to each fight. You also have a king of the hill mode, to see how long you can stay on top.
The new characters are interesting including the four young 'uns to join the now aging veterans. There are DLC characters to be released, which you can get in a pack or as they come out. The story was fun to play through and allows you to try out some of the characters as you progress (about 24 without DLC). You also get the Krypt to explore, which is almost like a mini-adventure allowing you to unlock art, costumes and fatalities with the Koins you earn throughout the various modes.
This is the Mortal Kombat you know and love but with more emphasis on online competition and not just the standard versus modes.

Dear Mary,
I lost another one today. I don't understand why they brought me here. They needed a Surgeon, but they brought in me. My first patient was the old Surgeon, I was the only person left who had any knowledge of operations, but I was just his assistant! I never went to college, I never had years of training. But they needed him, people were dying and they needed a surgeon.
And I failed, Mary. I failed. He died during the operation. I was so distraught, a mans life in my hands, and I failed. That night I was reckless. That's why, Mary. That's why my arms broke. I felt they were not meant for this world. I broke them so that nobody would ever be lost to them again.
And, later that night, they brought in another one. And the next, another. I told them I was not fit for duty, but they didnt care. They dragged me to the operating table and had me do it again, and again. The one patient I actually saved became a vegetable.
Mary...Please help me. I'm so sorry to drag you into this, but I need a favor. My arms will not turn inward, so my actions to myself are limited. They wont let me near the medicinal cabinet after hours. Remember that vial of perscription medicine my mother used to use, the one for her condition? When you reply to this letter, please, empty all the remaining pills into it.
I'm sorry Mary. I can't lose another one. I just can't bear to see their eyes again.
Sincerely,

I've played some hard games in my day. This is not one of them. Trust me, this game is not hard: a game being hard implies that it keeps pushing you to defeat it. This game, on the other hand, doesn't care. It makes no effort. It's a pedestrian, woefully unappealing platformer that presents, as its one and only catch, randomly generated levels. Of course the roots of this practice go back to ASCII-based RPG games like Rogue, which used its randomly generated dungeons to create a sense of endless peril and menace. On this game, however, the levels feel like the result of a game designer who was too drunk to care. This must be why the play screen is so small and close to the character: it's so we can't see the catastrophic, unpleasant results of this level generating mechanism.
The gameplay consists of reaching the end of the level, getting to the next one, repeat. You can get some gold and gems along the way to buy some items whose purpose you won't care to know, and you can find a damsel in distress to take to the end of the level and recover some of your health (I only wish I were making this up), and you can also do some other things that add a flimsy, cheap sense of diversity to a fruitless gaming experience. You die, you start again from the top. You can reach some checkpoints along the way, and if you provide the tunnel man with enough items, and if you run enough miles and jump enough lakes of fire and watch enough Friedberg & Seltzer movies, you can maybe open up a shortcut to quickly reach those checkpoints. Your prize will be, of course, more of the same.
It's quite amazing, but the makers of this game have managed to suck out every last drop of enjoyability that could remain in this game. This means that if you think having fun is too mainstream, this game is for you. If you enjoy doing the same kind of task over and over again, with as little diversity as possible, then don't play this: play Euro Truck Simulator 2, which actually manages to create an experience that is alternatingly pleasant and exciting, and nearly therapeutic. Buy this game if you don't like money, and if you don't like fun; then you can brag around about how "hard" this game is and how hardcore it makes you. But if you want an actually hard game, play Battletoads.

Portal Knights is very impressive.  I've played some 'finished product' / release version games that weren't nearly as polished as Portal Knights is in Early Access.  The production design, artwork, UI elements, sound design and the scarcity of bugs or issues here are all better than you'd expect in any "Early Access" game.
And it's not just the polish - the concept is great, too.  The video here on Steam is an excellent representation of what the gameplay is actually like.  Imagine if someone took Minecraft, made it look twice as nice as it does, expanded on the combat systems (including adding character classes, magic spells, wands, etc.) and put it all to a really terriffic soundtrack.  If you could envision how cool the total package might potentially be, you'll have a pretty good idea of what to expect from Portal Knights.
Get some good speakers or a nice headset to fully appreciate the sound design, including excellent sound effects and a fantastic soundtrack that could stand on its own.
How they managed to package all this together neatly and cohesively for $15... it's damned impressive.

Unpopular opinion, but Clear Sky is the best STALKER-game imo. I really love the settings, the weather variations, the fractions makes sense. The fractionwars is also a really cool feature. Just make sure to choose the right faction. For example, I really hated the Red Forest as it scared the sh*t out of me so I sided with Duty to get the guides for fast travelling to guide me to the safe spot in Red Forest. That, on the other hand made me an enemy to Freedom, which controls most of the Military Warehouses, making that area even harder than it already is with mutants, Zombiefied and Monoliths. But the point is, the option to join factions and wage war is totally awesome.
One bad thing is that there is no 'cheatcommands' in the console for this game. You dont like cheating? Well neither do I, but lets make something very clear, Clear Sky is full of bugs. For instance, after I conquered Freedoms base with Duty, Freedom launched an assault on their old base, I was inside, and Duty locked the doors. So basically no-one could get in or out.
On the plus side, its really easy to install mods that allow you to ghost/noclip through doors and resolve the issue. Also you can get stuck in holes and betwewen rocks and cant get out. These mods helps with that.
The storyline is also really cool, but so are the storylines in the other STALKER games. I wont say anything about it to avoid spoiling it.
So to summarize it, a really cool game in a postapocalyptic Chernobyl/Ukrainian rural area full with mutated animals, monsters, Stalkers(humans) and filled with anomalies and artifacts, extremely dangerous weather and some cool East and West-based weapon that you can customize and modify to suit your needs.
The story itself isnt that long, you could easily get this game done in a couple of hours. But the sidequests, and of course the fraction wars, litterally eats your time up. And if that wasnt enough, there are tons of mods that adds new content.
For the small prize it costs nowadays, there is nothing to think about. Buy it.

With a unique world setting, and a well-drawn cartoon-style art direction, Deponia brings back a traditional style point-and-click game for the modern age.
This naturally means it will feel a bit slow compared to todays games, but it's about using the mind... even if some of the solutions to the problems seem a little far-fetched.
The story itself is actually not that long nor does much really happen. Most of your time is spent trying to figure out how to do the smallest of tasks. Regardless, it's still a decent story and worth a playthrough, especially if you like point-and-click adventures.
6/10 "Okay"

Deponia is set in a world completely over run by garbage, even being used as a junk heap for another world, Elysium. You play as Rufus, a self proclaimed 'inventor' whose only goal in life is to get off of Deponia and enter Elysium.
The world itself is gorgeous, the art style is great and the voice acting is fantastic (I was particularly in love with Captain Bozo).
However, it has it's problems. The main one being that Rufus is not a likeable character at all. At best he's an antihero. I actually found myself rooting for him to fail at times. The start of the game sees Rufus trying to create a rocket to launch himself onto one of the garbage trucks that tower overhead so he can get onto a transportation system to Elysium. He has to pack a bag first and you find lots of nagging messages around the house left by his roommate. Rufus apparently doesn't do his fair share of the housework. You later find out that his ex girlfriend is actually letting him live there for free, hoping that he'll get his act together, get a job and occasionally pick up after himself and Rufus still rolls his eyes at her and thinks she's a cow?
Anyway despite the unlikeable protagonist, the game is fun, the puzzles are interesting, if a little obscure, there are some funny parts in the game, and the rest of the characters are great

Set during World War II players take on the role of elite OSS sniper Karl Fairburne across a selection of missions. Despite some fairly poor enemy AI (enemies will quite often just run straight into your crosshairs) the gameplay is solid and enjoyable with a good variety of objectives and interesting settings. As an added bonus the whole campaign can be played co-op which makes the game even more tactical, although the lack of an option to save mid-mission is an oversight seeing as they generally last for well over an hour. There are also a selection of co-op only ‘overwatch’ missions that focus on teamwork by tasking one player with using their sniper rifle to protect the other whilst they complete evolving objectives.  It has its flaws, and some of the slow motion kills may be a bit to gruesome for some, but overall Sniper Elite 3 is a good game, particularly if played with a co-op partner.

Note: This review is for the vanilla Stalker Clear Sky.
Stalker Clear Sky is the prequel entry to the series, the game has you play as a Merc named Scar, who survives a large emission storm and is trying to find Strelok before he reaches the center of the zone. Stalker Clear Sky is a hit and miss for many fans of the series as it introduces some great ideas and makes some questionable decisions. While many consider the intro segment an example of the games flaws, I did not find myself dying that much but I can see why players dislike Clear Sky. The intro segment in the swamps is unlike any Stalker game as it has the player in a specific area, running errands, and doing very little exploring. Getting into gunfights more frequently and constantly finding myself against large enemy groups with a double barrel was kinda ridiculous. There are also a lot of questionable decisions which would leave new players to the series baffled as the first entry route to Cordon will have a player against an army base and the player was suppose to know to take a different path in. Minor decisions like that are what makes Clear Sky a fustrating experience. Another horrible decision was to make bandages rare as heck and needing mutiple amounts of them to plug up one injury. Clear Sky does however bring the faction system and uses it fairly well. Players are encouraged to join factions to gain access to better gear and is a core aspect of the game. The PDA is better in Clear Sky compared to SoC. Clear Sky however performs the worst of all Stalker games as I had constant crashes and error messages in my playthrough. Interesting to note is that Clear Sky looks the best of all vanilla Stalker games as it has some impressive dynamic lighting, great amount of vegetation on screen with an impressive draw distance.
Pros:
- The new faction system is a good idea and used well.
- Weapons can be upgraded and modified.
- Large amount of Hub worlds compared to the other Stalkers.
- Many factions exist to make the faction system useful.
- The FoV effect/motion blur when reloading and moving looks amazing.
- Visually impressive for a near decade old game.
- Great to revisit areas before the events of the first game.
- Gunplay is tight and requires players to play slow.
Cons:
- No hunger system, this makes food an alternative to medical kits which makes no sense whatsoever.
- Bandages and Anti rad became rare which can create very fustrating moments of dying slowly.
- The worst intro segment in any Stalker game and maybe difficult enough to make players quit out right.
- Auto save is poor so spam that F5 key.
- The akward natural difficulty curve of the game may throw off players.
- Crash city and error messages galore.
- Bugs.
- While the gunplay is tight, pistols cannot have aim down sights...
- Ai has the habit in the starting sequence of turning shotguns into sniper rifles while you cannot do the same (get some slugs).
- No tutorial so please new comers do not get this game first.
Clear Sky isn't the worst game I have played and is enjoyable at times. However, the many questionable decisions that Clear Sky made in its game can make it a test of patience and sometime push it a little too far. Clear Sky does get easier as the player progresses and while Clear sky does not differ to much from SoC, SoC executed its concepts/mechanics correctly. SoC may have a difficult beginning segment also, but the way SoC handled healing items and made the difficulty scale naturally was great. Certain areas in SoC were loaded with harder enemies so you came back when you had the gear to go toe to toe with them. Clear Sky throws military units armed with AKs or Akabans whIle you just managed to leave the beg inning hub world. Clear Sky has some idea of what SoC was trying to do but is recommended for the veteran Stalker player. If your new to the series, start with SoC or heck even CoP, but save Clear Sky for last cause it will smack you around.

I went into this game already knowing that it had gotten critical praise, so I decided to check it out - and I am glad I did. Brothers is basically a game about two brothers trying to find medicine for their dying father. You control both of them via the left stick and trigger and the right stick and trigger, if you're using a controller. Those are the only controls, but this simplicity is necessary so you can effectively control both at the same time. If I had to place a label on this game, I would call it an adventure/puzzle game. It does both of these aspects wonderfully. The puzzles feel fresh and unique enough that you will enjoy solving them since almost all of them require both brothers to work together and to their strengths, though I managed to solve most of them with relative ease. The adventure aspect is what this game was made for; the places you visit are beautiful and breathtaking and they frequently prompt the player to sit back and marvel at their beauty. In fact, the developers have placed benches throughout the game for that particular purpose. Now some people might see the 3-hour length as a downside, which is probably one of its few flaws, but this game is not meant to be rushed through. The experience and the story alone are worth the price of admission. I think the fact that the characters are all speaking a nonsense language is worth mentioning because it actually helps people to empathize with the emotional points of the story much better. Overall, it was a wonderful experience and I recommend this game to anyone looking for a light game, but with some good emotional impact.

You play as Rufus, who aspires to escape the junk world of Deponia to the utopia of Elysium. But his biggest obstacle? Himself. Rufus is an anti-hero. He is incompetent and somewhat of a scoundral (the latter becomes more apparent in the sequels). This differentiates Deponia from other adventure games. The player is not just overcoming external forces, but also rectifying Rufus's mishaps.
Deponia is a comedy. And it plays that part pretty well. As a puzzler, it does okay. Many of the puzzles are quite mathematical and would therefore force the player to seek brute force solutions. Other puzzles require the player to formulate outlandishly complicated solutions to simple problems. Hints are sparse and unhelpful.
There is a lot of love that went into this game. The artwork, music, voice acting and scripting are very well done. And for an adventure game, there is a lot of material. The game should last about 10 hours on average.

P.A.M belongs to the Vehicular Combat genre, a genre BEST represented by the Twisted Metal franchise and Death Rally.
In comparison to both, this is a bad game. But on its own merits, however it isn't a terrible game. Is it good? No. Not by a long shot.
The good:
* The graphics are great
* The vehicle designs are excellent
* The track designs are varied and interesting
* The attacks vary per vehicle and are pretty awesome at that.
* All vehicles and rtracks are unlocked from the start
The bad:
* The music is awful
* The sound effects are "OK" at best
* The controls feel wonky.
* The physics glitch out quite a bit
Over-all, if this goes on sale for a couple bucks, grab it. For a few bucks, it's a good game. For the full non-sale price? No.

When you start the game, you get put in what they call "Bronze Matchmaking" with all the low rank players, and you just basically wreck everyone, if you have any previous experience with any kind of FPS. People run around, they're easy targets, they have low tier weapons, just like you.
But then, as you rank up, you get into Silver, then Gold Matchmaking, and that's where the game truly shows its Pay 2 Win nature. You'll get rushed by guys having the best rifle in the game, and there's nothing you can do with your semi-auto rifle, except die. You'll get one shot by people camping in some bush, a mile away, because they have a fully upgraded sniper/bolt action rifle, while you have to grind your way through so many hours to make your rifle a little better.
People will also drive around in jeeps and run over you, when you're already trying to fight several opponents at a time. You know what this game lacks ? A freaking radar, and proper sound. When you hear a jeep quite close, especially when you're next to your spawn, you assume it's a friendly jeep, when in fact, it's a dude from the enemy team that has nothing better to do than getting car kills on people thinking they're relatively safe. So yeah, dodging airplane bombs, tank firing at you, snipers in bushes, and madmen driving around in their jeep kinda gets old when you just need to walk 10 minutes to get to an objective to try and capture it. Especially when half your team isn't aware of the objectives, and just sits somewhere to try and get frags.
Proper sound would be useful too, it happened so many times to me, that I'd be running around, and there would be a troll with a knife, chasing after me, for a good 10-15 seconds, and I couldn't hear anything. I feel like I can only hear him when I turn around, and realise he's actually chasing me. But before that, nothing. And I'm a CS:GO player, I'm used to enemy footsteps, and I focus to try and hear them, as sound is almost as important as visual in a good FPS, in my opinion. I have a Sennheiser headset, and good hearing, so the problem definitely doesn't come from my end.
As I said, a radar would be a good addition, even though I get it that the game should be immersive and all, and enemies hard to spot (which still makes it even easier to camp, encouraging p2w players to use their OP weapons to nail you, once again, devs thought about making the game easier for them too). But a radar showing where your friends are, and displaying red dots for spotted enemies would be nice.
Spotting enemies should be faster too, to encourage teamwork. It is SO ridiculous to have to sit there and aim at a target for 4-5 seconds for it to display on the radar. And if the target moves, the red dot is completely off. Battlefield has a system where you could spot the enemies by pressing "Q" (or A if you're on an AZERTY keyboard), which makes it easier to communicate threats to your teammates.
So yeah, if you have hundred of hours of patience, and wish to grind with low tier weapons, you could enjoy this game, after a few weeks/months of intense playing.
Definitely pass unless you have money to spend, or a lot, and I mean A LOT, of time to dedicate to this game.

Heroes and Generals is a WWII shooter, based around capturing key positions on the battlefield to push the enemy forces back.
In Heroes and Generals, you start off as a basic Infantry soldier. You have 3 factions with one of these soldiers in each. The goal is to advance through the ranks, unlocking new weapons and vehicles until you reach the rank of General. As you level up, you may branch off into different positions, such as a tank crewman or a pilot.
Pros:
-Rank system
-Multiple weapon and vehicle choices
-Large open-world battles
-Multiple gamemodes
Cons:
-When you advance into a different branch (a pilot, recon, ect), you must buy all weapons and gear for that branch. Nothing carries over
-Mostly a grind fest. You have to play many battles to get any sort of money, which all goes into weapon and vehicle maintenance. You will have very little spending money
-If you want anything, you have to devote a lot of time into battles, or you have to pay for expensive Gold Packs
Overall:
I rate this game 3/10. It has a great idea to it, but the devs are very greedy. The game forces you to spend hours on battles for money, which all goes into keeping your gear fixed and refilled. Very expensive Gold Packs will have you spending a lot of money for in-game money that will barely get you anything. The battles are long, sometimes taking an hour or two (Yes, I have played hour long battles), along with a penalty for leaving mid match. If you dont have good internet, you will get no where in battle. This game is a grind fest in all. In all honesty, this is a very top notch free game, but in the end, you will still have to pay money to get anywhere.

I've written about this game a couple times, and I've played it time and again just to refresh my memory on why I hate this game so much. I'm more than happy to express my "♥♥♥♥ you" attitude toward this game in as volatile a manner as possible, but it's not really satisfying until I can really challenge the acclaim this title gets and convince people not to buy this game. So, take three!
Spelunky is a roguelike, which means it's randomly generated. Levels have random layouts, random events can change the gimmicks you come across along the way, and you can get random items along the way that help you progress. Cool, right?
It also works off a bit of chaos theory; if something blows up, chunks of rock could trigger an explosive box; if you throw a rock, it can come back and hit you, and you could fall into a man-eating plant. The ensuing volatile results can sometimes be hilarious, and oftentimes they can be infuriating.
Here's the thing: because it's a roguelike, there are no savepoints, and if you die once, you're out. But another thing is that stunlocking is a prevalent mechanic in this game. Nearly anything in this game can render you immobile for two seconds so you can get hit by even more stuff. Also, a lot of stuff that doesn't stunlock you will just kill you outright, like falling into spikes, getting blown up, getting crushed, etc.
Basically, if you get hit by anything that isn't a bat or a frog or whatever, expect to die 80% of the time.
Now, this kind of brutal difficulty by itself isn't a bad thing, but there are a plethora of other factors that go in tandem with this to make for a mindnumblingly boring and painful experience. Stunlock deaths, random unforeseeable danger, permadeath, lack of difficulty scaling, and unintuitive or unexplained mechanics. Level 1 is hardly any different in difficulty from level 4; arrows deal harsh damage to you even if they're just rebounding off a wall, and explosive boxes can be triggered by mere shards of debris or blood, yet jumping on the box is evidently no problem. Things slam into you without warning or the shopkeeper gets angered because random map generation causes something to explode immediately.
Because of all this and a lot more, a lot of unfun ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t can suddenly end your journey and force to start all over again, and it happens ALL the time. The problem is that most of these deaths happen in level 1 or 2, so guess what level you get to see ~80% of the time? Level 1.
In a game that's actually well-designed, at least one of these factors would be missing, allowing you to feel some sense of progression, but unfortunately that tends to not be the case here. This problem becomes escalated once you try to go for the true ending, because not dying over and over again from angry shopkeepers means spending a third of your playtime in the mines farming to get the item you need to unlock the secret level and HOPEFULLY not die before then. And if you do die after doing all that, guess what? More mines playtime!
The only reason I think I even managed to get this far in playtime and beat the normal game is because of my fascination for game design and how many jimmies this game rustles for me. I really just don't understand the praise this game gets. While the production value is certainly there and it's a lot "prettier" than most 2d platformer games on Steam, still there are much more satisfying ball-hard games like Super Meat Boy or Risk of Rain that don't force you to repeat ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t over and over just because you made one mistake. The game could have been a lot of fun if they just got rid of stunlocking, added lives, or did any number of things; the combination as-is is just too much for casual playthroughs or worthwhile true completions.
To my understanding, the original Spelunky is a lot more balanced, though maybe a bit slower paced, so if you really wanted, you could try that instead. As for Spelunky HD? Not worth your time or money.

Nearly 20 hours in - this is a wonderful game to play with some beautiful and colourful graphics, lots of worlds to explore and one that I'll add is a BLAST to play with your kids!
I love how I can build houses and craft items, much like that other infamous sandbox game, and thus I can sit there with a bit of a battle here or there but otherwise build my home. Is it Alpha, sure, it is! I'm looking forward to beds and the furniture I craft having a greater purpose, but it's all done in such a wonderful colour palette, I can sit back and admire my home.
I can go out and choose to adventure, different difficulty levels depending on your character's gear and the world you visit when you portal to other lands. The combat is fun and the enemies have different techniques that you can use to take them out, you can go all tank, ranged or magic on them and the visual effects are great. Boss fights are fun and can be very challenging depending on your gear, and there are lots of other innovations here like drills, resource finding tools, that can remove the grind of resource gathering (ores, gems).
I am enjoying this in both single player and multi-player (with my kids) for ANY parents reading my review, just buy it and have fun with your kids, it's a real blast, I'd say completely fine for 8 years and up (just because crafting does require a bit of thinking of what resources to gather, etc.) Characters look great, not too gory, lots of replay value here (just keep creating new worlds).  You can spawn on each other's worlds as long as you are all connected via Steam.
I enjoy playing the game on my own as well, and can happily spend an hour or two adventuring and playing, just having fun.
Does it need anything / my wishlist?
Resource stack splitting - this is something that would be great to see in a future update.
Medium and Large worlds - performance is great on the current "small" worlds, I use quotes because once you start mining and exploring, some are quite a decent size, however, I'd love to see a large world being 10x the small size, as long as performance is the same.
Speaking of performance, the game runs flawlessly on my system (i7-3770K, GTX970, W10, 16GB RAM) but also runs flawlessly on the computers my kids run (Core 2 Quad Q6600 - GTX960 - W10 - 4GB RAM (yep 4gb old systems :o) ) and there are no issues whatsoever on their computers.
You will enjoy this game, and as you can tell, I certainly am having a blast... and this is ALPHA!

About the game: It is a cooperative game in which you control both brothers. You are sent on a journey to find a cure for your dying father. The brothers must work together to overcome obstacles along the way. I played with an Xbox controller and quite frankly don't know how the game would be played without it (didn't try, but don't recommend it). Steering both brothers simultaneously takes some getting used to but it is not as difficult as you might think. There are some benches along the journey that you have the option of sitting on. I recommend you do, as it reveals breathtaking landscapes and is one more reason this game is so special. To that end,  the time and thought the writers and developers put into this game is clear, and gamers should be grateful for it. I wouldn't be surprised if a slew of games trying to emulate Brothers come out over the next couple of years. Let's hope so.

It's Dead Rising 2 but with Frank West.
For those of you unfamiliar with the Dead Rising series, it goes a little something like this: You are trapped in a huge mall with more zombies than you thought could possibly be rendered on screen at one time. You have to survive 72 in-game hours while searching for the truth behind the zombie outbreak. Along the way, you will rescue survivors holed up in various parts of the mall as well as fight off psychopaths who see the zombie apocalypse as an opportunity to let their homicidal urges fly free.
Nearly every object in the game world can be picked up and used as a weapon, with varying degrees of effectiveness. Squirtguns, gumball machines, rakes, katanas, chainsaws - you name it, Dead Rising probably lets you swing it around. Many of the items can be combined to make combo weapons, which are absurdly over-the-top and insanely destructive. Stuff like taping a couple of chainsaws to each end of a kayak paddle, or using a car battery to turn a yard rake into an industrial sized taser.
The real challenge comes with the game's time limit: Basically, you have only so much time to complete the side missions before the next story event starts. Unless you meticulously plan your routes and the order you choose to rescue survivors, you are unlikely to finish them all in a single playthrough. At any point in the game (or upon dying), you can elect to restart the story from the beginning in a New Game+ type fashion, maintining your level, upgrades, and all of the combo weapons you've unlocked. The game is designed with multiple playthroughs in mind.
There are a couple of minor differences between "Off The Record" and the original Dead Rising 2. But apart from a different final boss, you probably won't notice most of them. I didn't. I picked this up because I wanted to replay DR2 and this was what was on sale. It's still every bit as fun as I remembered and it runs great on modern hardware (of course) but I do prefer the story of the original game. New to Off The Record is a sandbox mode mode which eschews the story, time limits, and missions. As it turns out, aimlessly wandering around the mall with no structure and nothing to do but kill as many zombies as you can gets old fast.
If you're playing Dead Rising 2 for the first time, I'd recommend you go with the vanilla game over this. If you don't care about the storyline and just want some off the wall zombie slaying fun, you won't be disappointed.
