After spending a little over 4000 hours in this simulation over the past several years, I decided to rate it.  As far as entertainment value, I can definitely say, it has kept my attention.  The variety if DLC allows one to chose and focus on what region and era of railroading strikes your interest.  The wealth of third party developers add to the choices in not only regions and rolling stock, but also in quality and depth of realism.
I must be made aware that this core of this simulation is over a decade old and it is a 32 bit program with memory limitations.  It can be frustrating at times especially when pushing the system to the limits of VAS and accessible memory.  Scenarios can be of various levels of quality dependent on the skills of the author.  I am not a scenario or route builder myself, but from the years I have been in the community, my understanding that the tools provide do have a learning curve.
All that being said, this simulation has kept my interest for many years and with new DLC still being produced both by DTG and third parties keeps it interesting.  I highly recommend this simulation for those of you that enjoy railroading and have the patience to work through the occasional problems that might occur.  There are several community forums were many helpful enthusiasts are more than willing to lend a hand without the drama so often found in the Steam forums.

I can feel a bit of a dissonance between quite serious topics covered in reading files and not-so-serious anime-VN-style elements (especially in *Hyun-ae route). Hate Plus might not be as deep as Analogue, but Christine Love's writing is still excellent and I've really enjoyed this sequel.

It is not for nothing that I consider *Mute one of my favorite characters of all time (*Hyun-ae is good, but not as much as *Mute). If the previous game focused on *Hyun-ae, this one, however, tells us a lot more about *Mute. And oh boy did I want to cry on this.
I may be considered too emotional - and serious - about this, but the events in this sequel are just too good for me. Be it the soundtrack that really focuses on *Mute's emotions and feelings, or the logs of the Mugunghwa that describes, again, events that are just revolting ... Maybe all of this, it just makes *Mute real.
She's an AI, just a program - literally -, and yet she sounds almost real, as if she was a human in flesh and blood. She's given substance, and can be relatable.
That's why she's awesome, and this VN as well. Some people may think that both of the Visual Novels aren't worth their while, since the price may be too high or the game too short. But it's quality over quantity : and even if it's short, not really developed and mostly relies on logs to read, in the end, it's what you learn from it that is worth the while.
And I learned a lot from it, that ... I can't hate it, in the slightest. Yeah.

Spelunky is a modern masterpiece. It's as close to perfect as it is possible for a game to be. Every element is deliberately designed to fit together into an intricate system in which each failure teaches you something and prepares you that little bit better for the next game.
Its genius is in applying the traditional "roguelike" elements - randomly generated areas, high cost of player death, and learnable systems - into the approachable form of the platformer. No single element of the game is terribly challenging. Each monster, trap, item, and weapon has a very simple behaviour and is easily mastered. Once you see how a bat moves, you know how to deal with the next one. However Spelunky rarely gives you a series of single challenges, but a mix of several all at once: so while a single bat is no problem, a bat, a spike trap and a spider is something else.
This is the heart of what makes Spelunky so great. Because the levels are randomly generated, you can't memorise them, and instead have to learn the underlying systems. You're constantly having to quickly eye up a situation, apply what you know about the world, and work out a way to get through it. Even though you can get very skilled at the first few levels you never cruise through on autopilot as the arrangements of obstacles always offers a challenge.
And no matter how good you get, there is always some way to test yourself even more. I recently defeated the game the easy way, so the next challenge is to find the secret areas and hidden levels and defeat them too. I know what is involved and some of it seems eye-wateringly difficult. But I'd have it no other way!

The first part of the Deponia trilogy isn’t exactly a bold game that tries to discover new territories in mechanics or storytelling; it’s just a well-constructed point ‘n’ click with proven character concepts, plot mechanics, and puzzles.
The Deponia series is arguably Daedelic Entertainment’s most famous point and click title. Yet the first instalment, for the most part, is just another good adventure game, nothing more.
The protagonist, Rufus, is a stereotypical egocentric jerk who just wants to achieve his one goal in life (leave his home for good), no matter how much grief it causes to everyone around him. When the other main character, Goal from the (literally) upper society drops into his life, he sees her only as a ticket out… but eventually gets entangled in a much larger plot, which– the game being the first part of a trilogy– naturally ends in a cliffhanger.
What makes this often seen story stereotype work is the writing. The dialogues are perfect from Rufus’ self-centric monologues to the sarcastic responses he gets from everyone else; the characters may be simple, but they have a good synergy.
The puzzles are what one expects from a point ‘n’ click: mostly inventory and map hotspot manipulation, with a few occasional (and skippable) minigames. The difficulty is moderate; if you know how adventure game logic works, you shouldn’t have problems– except for maybe the middle segment, which require some trial and error.
As a final word: the trilogy was re-released as a single game, making these individual titles somewhat obsolete… unless you want to play the famous drugglejug mode, which was never implemented in the Complete Edition.

Hate Plus... is arguably a visual novel. It's a visual novel in that you will be reading a story and it's actually a pretty good story. The story is presented through decrypted diary entries which is great as a narrative device. Even though you'll probably read the entries out of order, it's actually somewhat engaging. It actually feels like the diary entries are more fun to read out of order because then we can piece together the visual novel ourselves. The stories are short enough (there's one main story and a couple of sub-stories) that it's actually possible to use this narrative style. This method doesn't scale up well unless you're really good at tying threads together with skill on the order of George R. R. Martin. These stories are only tangentially related, in A Song of Ice and Fire I don't think there's a single unimportant set of details. Yes, even the food scenes.
The characters are all fairly interesting with realistic interactions. I like how the character design is really thought out. There's not so much on character development (the game is too short) but that's fine, that's not the point. These diary entries are just about... life. I guess it makes sense considering that the purpose of diaries is to write about life but I don't really know any other way to put it.
The biggest flaw in the game is execution. The core of the game's story is *Mute, the character depicted on the title art (seen at the top of this page). The *Mute of the past doesn't quite seem to be the *Mute of the present so you get to dig around figuring out what happened, ultimately uncovering the beginning of the totalitarian regime that died out from the first game.
This game has a lot of fluff. That's the be expected since it's a diary game; but the amount of fluff in this game seems exceedingly so. In the prequel it took you make one to three minutes to read each diary entry. This game takes around five minutes an entry and while that may not seem like much, that's an increase of close to 100%. The rule is not "Longer is better" but rather "Be as long as you need to be". Unfortunately, from my point of view, some of these entries are too long. Don't get me wrong, some of them are legitimately great reads, but they can drag on when you're in "get to the point" mode.
I think that by far, the worst addition to this game though, is the time restricted setup. Yes, you can change your computer clock to skip it. No, I don't care. Why was a mechanic like that put into the game in the first place? The rule is, you need to wait 12 hours after reading the day's worth of diary entries (usually 12-18 entries). Why was this unnecessary barrier to content added? I paid for the whole game today. I didn't pay for 1/3 of the game today, 1/3 tomorrow, and 1/3 the day after that. This is unreasonable and severely hurt my opinion of the game. There are also several sections of the game where you are literally forced to wait twenty minutes to an hour to proceed. This. Is. Frustrating. Design.
I'm actually going to sit on the fence here. It's not a game that you can recommend to anyone. I personally found it to be... acceptable. But you have to remember that I'm a little bit weird. I liked the fluff even if it dragged on a little longer than it should've. I found the way the totalitarian regime began to be interesting. I like the characters. So while the time delay execution style is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I tried to not let it get in my way. So my last word will be a conditional. If you enjoy fluff and reading about things entirely unrelated to the content at hand (even if only briefly) and you want to learn about the rise of a Confucian society, maybe catch this game on sale. If you need the linear path or even a mostly linear path to progress through your games, maybe give this one a pass.

Solving the mystery left behind in the first game wasn't worth it. It'd be more fun to just read the log files minus the rest of the game.
Pros:
The mystery  is solved! We get to read the events that lead up to Year 0 in the first game!
You can use your save file from the first game with snippets of information (like costume, some random decisions, route ending, and which gender you were)
The log files are massive. So much to read, so much story.
There's an index of character names (only most of them with pictures) and your AI's will have commentaries on who they are.
Even more invasive exploration of stuff
Some NSFW not-straight romantic tragedies if that's your thing.
Cons:
Waifus.
A plot twist you saw coming a mile away.
Power level is actually related to real-time days but not the way you think. The game decides to end the day when the power level reaches 1%. And THEN there's a 12 hour timer. I don't know about you, but if I had my own space ship I would never EVER want my power level to reach 1%, especially when it's going to take 12 hours to get it back up to 25% (if the first game taught me nothing, it's that life support and bulkheads altogether cost 2% of your power. so I'm pretty sure the MC is actually a robot).
Lot's of diary entries by pretty unrelated people (I couldn't finish the game after I read the death of Old Mute, fifth crash was enough for me).
Game crashes constantly.
UI was a major downgrade from the first game. The only way to go through a log file is to press a button and slowly reveal the log or to scroll. As a fast reader and someone who dislikes using the mouse, it was painful.
The AI will react to the log as you read it. However, it's never clear WHAT they're reacting to. Most of the time it's something I read two paragraphs ago, or it's something I haven't gotten to yet. It's actually really obnoxious.

I've invested many hours into the XBLA version of this game when it first came out, so I'd say I'm pretty experienced with Spelunky.  It's so deeply challenging and rewarding, with lots of secrets to uncover (assuming you don't just look up everything on the Wiki).  I'd say it's probably a bit more niche than most games; people tend to either love it or hate it.  The local coop is a ton of fun, though unfortunately the camera perspective cannot be shifted in coop, which puts everybody but Player 1 at a disadvantage.
The best part about Spelunky is that it's highly replayable.  Levels are procedurally generated to great effect, keeping a nice difficulty curve as levels go on.  The game is also mod-friendly, allowing players to create custom seeds, textures, sound effects, and music, all while maintaining the integrity of the leaderboards.  One particular mod, titled "Frozlunky", allows for the game's difficulty to be increased much further than it already is; so if you somehow become a god at the game (ha, right), you can still challenge yourself even further.
I fully recommend Spelunky.

La mejor parte de Spelunky es que es altamente rejugable.  Los niveles se procesal generada con gran efecto, bien manteniendo una curva de dificultad como los niveles avance.  También mods son de fácil manejo, permitiendo a los jugadores crear semillas personalizados, texturas, efectos de sonido y música, mientras manteniendo la integridad de las tablas de posiciones.  Uno mod en particular, titulado "Frozlunky", permite la dificultad del juego que aumentar mucho más allá de la dificultad orignal; Así, si de alguna manera te convierte en un experto en el juego (ja, claro), todavía puedes ponerse a prueba aún más.
Recomiendo totalmente Spelunky.

First Tekken ever released on PC platform with huge success and undoubtedly its debut deserves all medals.
Not only did it a great launch on Steam but it's also full of content.
To begin with, some of its offline features include: story mode (haven't finished it yet), arcade, practice, gallery, customizable chars/player mode, VS and species of survival where you can farm treasures and gold.
All of them are really fun however the treasure search is pretty addicting; once you start gathering the different objects it's hard to stop.
Being able to change the colours, hairstayle, clothes, also adding hilarious features such as wings, auras, or weapons (just aesthetic) makes you want more and more. You can save several customized chars to choose the one that suits best for the occasion. From Valentine and Halloween theme suits, to armors, sport clothes and many more. You combine whatever you want.
The roster is more than good, 37 characters and they are aiming for more. Personally I've just tried Shaheen and found a lot of fun with him. If you pre ordered you may have got Eliza too, otherwise you'll be able to get her within a month according to devs. Gouki/Akuma is a guest char and they already confirmed some other incoming guests.
The online mode works really well, I didn't have lag issues, perhaps on a pair or matches just a bit at the very beginning but then, everything was perfect and I played with ppl from several places of the AmericaS.
Online mode includes: Ranked, lobby/non ranked, tournament and rankings.
I hate comparisons, nontheless it's necessary here. Unlike poor content provided by sfv, a game that totally disappointed me, this one has much more and by now the only lacking thing is a replay mode which I expect to hopefully be added in a close future.
I'm a beginner in Tekken (universe) 7 thus, everything is new to me, combos are just different from what I am used to doing, nevertheless, with practice you can learn and adapt to this playstile if your are new too.
I used to love USF4 which I considered the best FG ever. Right now I believe Tekken7 will be the king of all fighting games from this generation.
Other details: it does not support crossplay, but just because console companies have their politics that avoid that.
On the Steam web page of Tk7 you may see a lot of ppl playing depending on the hour (at the moment this review is written 12k but an hour ago it was over 18k).
I'm playing with an xbx controller and no issues. Combos are not impossible with this gamepad. Fightsticks should be more suitable I guess.
If you are hesitating whether to buy this game or not, consider the game is utterly terrrific and exciting, and imo it deserves all support from playerbase, so don't even doubt it. Get it asap. A great point-and-click adventure game.  The writing is great paired with an odd style of humor and even stranger world.

Personally, I have never been a fan of point and click games, however, Deponia has entirely changed that.
I originally batted about the idea of purchasing Deponia because the art style really appealed to me, but I was put off by the play style and the price. However, when it came on sale for £0.79 I snapped it up without a second thought, as, even if I were only to use it for artistic reference, I knew I wouldn’t regret spending that on it. It is probably the best thing I’ve ever bought for under a pound. Immediately, I was hooked. It is fun and immersive, and, though it appears to have some childish tones, the dialogue and extremely well-developed characters provide many humorous moments and you start to see that it is rather adult in its comedic value.
Then there’s the difficulty. I never imagined that a point and click adventure would prove so taxing! The hidden objects, the combinations required, the little puzzles and the specific orders required for the completion of tasks often left me scratching my head and, I will admit, if I hadn’t had the opportunity to glance at a walk through on the odd occasion, I doubt I would be anywhere near completing it right now (though I avoided using the guide as much as possible, of course). I’ve still not unlocked all of the achievements!
I am not entirely sure whether it has a lot of replay value, but I know I will be coming back to it simply because I will miss the atmosphere and the quirky characters! And I will admit, though Rufus is an egocentric jerk and possibly one of the worst boyfriends in gaming history, he is very loveable and under it all, a real sweetheart.
The only thing I can complain about with Deponia is the fact that it is too short, and the prices on the series are a bit high for my liking, but the moment the sequels come on sale I will be snapping them up!
So yes, I whole-heartedly recommend this game. It is beautiful, the sound track is super funky, the characters are funny and unique and it does supply a good challenge to keep your mind occupied.
Plus, my toothbrush ran away and hid in a dark corner, mocking me from the shadows, and I made coffee out of battery acid and gave it to a cat who licked stamps… What’s not to love?
10/10

A good read about polemic and complicated issues that actually makes them feel "human".

I had a ton of fun with this game. It's the perfect successor to The Stick of Truth, with a main story line taking about
hours to beat.
The reason I say
hours is because I did all of the side missions (except
). But to be fair, the side missions line up very well with the main story line and are usually on the way to the next main story quest. So basically, why wouldn't you do the side quests?
The gameplay is a lot more involving than it was in The Stick of Truth. The combat system is a LOT better (not surprising, since that was the worst part about Stick of Truth) this time around and the amount of different playable characters and their super powers is enough to make the battles interesting even towards the end of the game.
Aside from the battles, the interaction with the environment on the overworld has been improved drastically as well.
The looting has been streamlined, so you don't have to open a menu when you interact with a chest anymore, you just take everything inside it instantly.
The special overworld skills (which were annoying to use in Stick of Truth) are.. well far less annoying to use in Fractured But Whole. It's still not my cup of tea, especially towards the end where you have to do those special overworld skills back to back to back, but it still didn't annoy me as much as I thought it would.
It sounds really dumb to say this, but the graphics are more polished and just better, compared to Stick of Truth. Both have the distinct South Park look, but lighting and special effects just look far prettier in this game.
Lots and lots of old songs from the TV-Show and otherwise great background music.
Sadly, the voice acting sometimes cuts out towards the end of a sentence. No idea what causes that, I had that happen like 3 or 4 times during my 22 hours of playing the game.
I loved it. I'm not too much into the fantasy setting, so Stick of Truth wasn't my genre, but I love the super hero genre, so this fits perfectly.
Without spoiling anything, this is the only game I've ever played, that managed to actually confuse me about what was going on around the end. Deliberately so, I might add. It was a fun experience.
Well, sadly this game has some bugs. First of all, the long loading times. Jesus Christ are those long loading times. Due to another bug I experienced, I had to move the game from my HDD to my SSD. That improved it a little, but those loading times are still not acceptable for a game that has so little graphical assets to load.
Another bug (which required me to move the game to the SSD) was, that a cutscene didn't trigger for me. It was right after defeating the boss at the U-Store-It facilities. I had to defeat that boss 8 times, trying to find a way to get the cutscene to trigger. Eventually, I just had to move the game to an SSD, play on 720p, low graphics, medium difficulty. No idea why, but yeah, that worked for me. Was still frustrating as hell.
Pretty great game, would recommend it to every fan of the show. But maybe wait before buying it until they fixed some of the bugs.

I've invested many hours into the XBLA version of this game when it first came out, so I'd say I'm pretty experienced with Spelunky.  It's so deeply challenging and rewarding, with lots of secrets to uncover (assuming you don't just look up everything on the Wiki).  I'd say it's probably a bit more niche than most games; people tend to either love it or hate it.  The local coop is a ton of fun, though unfortunately the camera perspective cannot be shifted in coop, which puts everybody but Player 1 at a disadvantage.
The best part about Spelunky is that it's highly replayable.  Levels are procedurally generated to great effect, keeping a nice difficulty curve as levels go on.  The game is also mod-friendly, allowing players to create custom seeds, textures, sound effects, and music, all while maintaining the integrity of the leaderboards.  One particular mod, titled "Frozlunky", allows for the game's difficulty to be increased much further than it already is; so if you somehow become a god at the game (ha, right), you can still challenge yourself even further.
I fully recommend Spelunky.

El modo cooperativo local es muy divertido, aunque por desgracia la perspectiva de la cámara no puede ser cambiado en la cooperativa, que deja a todos pero el jugador primera en desventaja.
La mejor parte de Spelunky es que es altamente rejugable.  Los niveles se procesal generada con gran efecto, bien manteniendo una curva de dificultad como los niveles avance.  También mods son de fácil manejo, permitiendo a los jugadores crear semillas personalizados, texturas, efectos de sonido y música, mientras manteniendo la integridad de las tablas de posiciones.  Uno mod en particular, titulado "Frozlunky", permite la dificultad del juego que aumentar mucho más allá de la dificultad orignal; Así, si de alguna manera te convierte en un experto en el juego (ja, claro), todavía puedes ponerse a prueba aún más.
Recomiendo totalmente Spelunky.

Rating: 10/10 must buy - worth full price and then some ( WORK OF ART status)
Summary: Emotionally charged and beautifully designed adventure puzzle game. Can be played without controller but dont do it, use a 2 stick controller. Hits right in the feelings in the best possible way. No one will be left unmoved by the game.
Long review (SPOILER FREE):
Game is set in a fantasy world in which you play as two brothers on a epic quest to acquire a certain item. It is a very mature tale about growing up, brotherly bonds, effects of  trauma on a young person, overcoming those traumas and acceptance of death as part of life.
Art direction is really good and make the world seem very alive which in turn makes you get really immersed in the game. Game is not long around 2,5h (4h if you stop to take in scenery) but in that short time it will take you on a emotional roller coaster ranging from heartwarming to heartbreaking. You will not feel like you were cheated by how short it is in the end, it will feel perfectly timed.
I can honestly say this is one of the few games that ever induced such deep emotions and cathartic feeling at the end. I am talking about The Walking Dead Clementine affection or MGS Sniper Wolf death scene level of emotions. This game will stick with me for the rest of my life. Please play this game in ONE sitting.
Characters in this game speak in a made up language and there are no subtitles yet design is so masterful you will never not understand what is happening or get lost or not understand a puzzle. In fact i was impressed that i developed such strong feelings for the brothers despite it. Puzzles range from easy to medium. Sometimes they are a bit "hard" just because you are most likely not used to controlling 2 characters at once using both analog sticks and R2 L2 triggers. Personally i did not find them clunky it worked really well for such a design.
Most impressive thing that really hit me in the feels was how the game  managed to incorporate emotions into actuall controls. That blew my mind and if you play until the end you will know what i mean by that.
Only criticism i can possibly give would be that you should have a controller. Everything else is perfect at least for me. I will follow future similar releases from this studio. This game is a work of interactive art that can not be done in any other medium except video gaming.
GO BUY IT !!!

TLDR; One of the best fighting games on Steam. Complete with lots of features, Big roster, Great graphics, great performance, great controller support, great gameplay, great netcode, great ranking system.
One of the best fighting games, if not the absolute best fighting games ever released on steam. This game has all the features you would expect out of a fighting game and then some! You have the Staples such as arcade, online, versus, training and a story mode. This game's Tournament mode and customization mode are the first of their kind on Steam or at least not in any capacity close to what is found in this game. This game also has a huge roster of almost 40 characters to choose from. Players are almost certain to find at least one character they'd like to play as. The roster size also adds to the replayability because there will always be a character for players to try out for fun when another character starts getting stale to play.
If you are familiar with the Tekken series, the game play is as good as ever. The game is suitable for people who want to casually play with their friends because of some the easily executed attack strings but has a lot of depth to be explored if you want to play the game on a higher/competitive level.
As a competitive game there aren't many games better than this. The roster is very balanced according to high level players in Japan and Korea who have been playing it for a year now in arcades. Many players of  "low tier" characters have also done well in the prerelease tournament circuit last year. If ranked games are your thing, Tekken 7 has the absolute best ranking system in any game I've played, fighting game or not. The ranks in the Tekken games are a much better indicator of player skill than in most games since there are so many of them. There is usually markedly different level of skill between players who are found in a certain tier of ranks compared to another. Also, unlike other fighting games, this game assigns an individual rank to each character instead of one overall rank. In other fighting games players are often afraid to try new characters online because they're afraid to lose their rank that they fought so hard for.
This game is also excellent on a technical level as well. This is, so far, the most graphically impressive fighting game and has set a new standard for the graphics of future fighting games with non cell-shaded 3D graphics. Despite the pretty visuals the game is very well optimized and has a feature that can dynamically adjust the graphic settings as you play for those with less powerful PCs. The game's controller/keyboard support is some of the best I've seen so far and is certainly better than any other fighting game I own on PC.
Buy this game if you like fighting games! At the very least, if you are shopping for fighting games and this review does not convince you about its merits, the least you could do for yourself is not buy Street Fighter V. That game will just disappoint you. Consider any other fighting game with decent reviews.

Very rarely have I been sucked into a video game the way I have these past 24 hours with Tekken 7. To further compliment this game, I'm not as into fighting games as some people. I consider myself a casual fighting game enthuisiast bordering on above-average. But that didn't matter. This game brought me back to my childhood years of playing Tekken 2-3. Although I have played various Tekken since, I don't recall a time I was this encapsulated by a game since 3. It felt so good.
The game itself is amazing. Combat modes you expect are there. Arcade, practice, and my personal off line favorite treasure batlle. It also has a really nice story mode that gives insight into the Mishima family, for those paying attention. The story was a good time, you can beat it in a handful of hours and get some nice unlocks. Some of the battles are cruel just fyi. Online is fun! You have ranked and quick play, and an online tournament which is a nice way to earn some gold and talk trash. I had alot of fun with that. I definitely recommend this game to anyone looking to get back into the Tekken series, or those starting since the story fills you in somewhat. Also anyone into fighting game. Or great games in general. The combat is tight and responsive, the visuals are georgous, the story is fun and there's also plenty of characters. This is going to be my go to fighter for the summer, see you online!

Super Crate Box is a 2D run and gun arcade platformer. If that is tough to digest, the game is played in a single screen. The point is to get crates. Once you get a crate, a new one spawns. Inside each crate is a random weapon that you've unlocked. Why do you get crates? To unlock new weapons, characters and levels to play on. There are only three levels, but I'm happy with that. The first level feels so good to play on that you almost don't need the other two.
Enemies drop from a hole in the ceiling of the level. Standard left and right moving enemies, when they get to the edge they fall off to the next one. There are bigger versions of the standard enemies that take twice as much damage. Finally, there are hovering skull enemies that bounce around. Its a nice simple variety that still adds challenge. Since the enemies work their way to the bottom, there is a fire pit. If the enemies reach the fire pits, they come back red, angry and twice the speed! In a way it feels like the original Mario Bros. arcade game. One screen levels, and enemies that get angry, doubling their speed.
The major difference is the guns. Each gun has unlimited ammo and feels fun to use, with their own pro and con. Dual pistols will shoot left and right simultaneously, but do 1 bit of damage. The revolver shoots one bullet at a time, but does double damage. The machine gun shoots straight forward very quickly, but pushes you back. The flamethrower will effectively light platforms and enemies on fire, but if you stand in the fire, you can't jump. The katana has short range, but does a lot of damage and sends big enemies the other way. The shotgun has short range, but sends out a big blast of randomized bullets. The bazooka fires rockets that are slow to reload, but they do a lot of damage in a radius. Grenade launchers do the same thing, but they reload faster and arc when you shoot them. Mines take a while to arm themselves and can only drop straight down, but do the same big radius damage as rockets and grenades. Lasers take a long time to fire once you pull the trigger, but go through everything. The disc gun bounces off the first wall it hits and goes through enemies, but it will also kill you.
You can only carry one weapon, so when you get a crate, its a different weapon. Some weapons are better than others, so there is a dynamic of not getting a crate to use a good weapon to kill a screen full of enemies vs just getting the next crate.
You will unlock new characters, but they all play the same. They just different. The game will give you a random character when you play. One hit will kill you, but that's the balance. Guns vs swarms of enemies. With every death, the game will tell you what you've unlocked, how many more crates you need and send you right back in as if nothing happened. The whole thing takes a second or less. If the game gets too easy for you on normal mode, there is a hard mode.
The game keeps track of your high score in crates, but there are no points awarded. Hopefully there will be a more complete sequel with support for co-op and points, but that is in no way a complaint for this great FREE arcade game. In all, its a fun free game. If it came out in the 80s, Super Crate Box would have made millions of dollars in quarters. Not just that, but this free little game is enough to make me want to play other games from the developer.

The Hate Series is one of the more popular visual novel series, and for damn good reason.  These games are at once thrilling, soothing, hilarious and heartbreaking.  If you enjoy visual novels, there is absolutely no reason to deny yourself the experience of Analogue and Hate Plus, and I definitely recommend playing both of them in the proper sequential order to get the most out of your experience.
In Hate Plus, you reprise your role as a "space investigator" who is on his/her/their way back to Earth after investigating the fall of the Korean Generation Starship
, with one of the ship's two AI constructs (or, perhaps both?) in tow.  Over the course of the game's three-day setting, you'll read an entirely-new novel through uncovering old data logs, and your old friends *Mute and/or *Hyun-ae will offer their unique perspectives on the story as before; just like with Analogue, multiple playthroughs are encouraged to get the full story from both sides.
While Analogue: A Hate Story had more traditional video game elements to it, Hate Plus prefers to focus primarily on the novel and your interactions with the AI characters.  The data logs in Hate Plus are considerably longer, and the game forces you to take breaks throughout gameplay, perhaps since the subject matter becomes relatively intense at times.  The characters of *Mute and *Hyun-ae are filled out quite well in this sequel, and the game is much more immersive than its predecessor.
As before, this novel is not for the faint of heart.  There's profanity, sexuality, intrigue, and some incredibly dark undertones regarding the subjugation of women.  Balancing these tropes, however, is a healthy dose of humor and some straight-up, old-fashioned Asian cuteness; Hate Plus is one of very few video games that made me laugh out loud multiple times.
If all this sounds like your idea of a good time, then take the leap.  You won't regret it.

You get the chance to delve deeply into the political machinations that led to the year-0 reset and peculiar dynastic state of the Mugunghwa, and even if political machinations and conspiracies and election fraud and rebellion aren't your cup of tea, there's some great character development on each route, and the dialogue in all areas is top-notch.
One slight issue worth noting is that, much as with Analogue, it's very possible, if you choose the proper entries, to figure out the core of what happened within the first two days and be left skimming some fairly extraneous entries on the third. A few entries seem rather out of place for the intended purpose of explaining what happened, but hey, considering there's an impossible achievement that MIGHT have something to do with a secret message (okay, it's PROBABLY actually impossible), the benefit of the doubt is probably justifiable.
Regardless, it's a great game. Play Analogue, play this, and don't forget to stock up on baking supplies.

If you enjoyed Stick of Truth, I believe you'll also enjoy this game very much.

Clear sky is the weakest game in the STALKER series for me so far, however this does not make it a bad game. My main problem are the many bugs/crashes and the strange weapon-play. The balancing on many guns has been severely changed, with heavy impact on combat. You play as the Stalker Scar who is hunting Strelok, the story finds place before Shadow of Chernobyl.
Pros:
- As usual, an atmospheric, dynamic and dangerous world with lots of places to discover.
- Faction Wars: Help different factions to destroy their enemies and conquer the zone.
- Lots of guns and different enemies, artifacts to give you special advantages. Gunplay is actually complex with ammo types affecting ballistics.
- A lot to do: Do sidequests, get money to upgrade your weapons or just follow the quite long main quest.
Cons:
- Weapon play is a bit weirder than in the other STALKER games, many weapons are too inaccurate and don't shoot where you aim, even fully upgraded.
- Weird balancing: Even after pumping a whole magazine into an enemies body he might be still alive, however you fall with 4-7 hits even in a heavier body suit. Headshots are must because you can drop most human opponents in 1-2 hits depending on your ammo.
- AI problems: Enemies seeing you through bushes, after shooting one guy with a silenced gun they magically know where you are, enemies are horrifyingly accurate even with stock guns.
- Some bugs, glitches and crashes.
However in its core Clear Sky is a good game, I liked Shadow of Chernobyl more because of the narrative, Call of Pripyat had a better overall design and way more refined mechanics. I recommend to play this game with the Clear Sky COMPLETE mod, as it adds authentic weapon names and better graphics along iwth some bugfixes.

Mortal Kombat has been my favorite fighting game franchise since I first played Mortal Kombat 2. Over the years, there have been ups and downs with the franchise. From the bottom of the barrel we have Mortal Kombat: Special Forces and Mortal Kombat Vs. DC Universe, and some of the best we have the classic Mortal Kombat 2 and Mortal Kombat released in 2011. Now it's 2015 and a new Mortal Kombat has surfaced and, in my opinion, this one is probably the best I've seen in the series.
At first on release day, the Steam community started jabbing this game with negative reviews because of the new and experimental Steam download system where you play as the download goes. This had nothing to do with the Netherrealm devs, it was the flawed and buggy download system Steam chose to use for this game. After getting everything to download properly I was able to play properly, and I had a blast.
Gameplay is as solid as it has ever been. The controls are tight and extremely responsive. Combos are satisfying to pull off, X-Rays are pleasently unpleasent to witness, fatalities are back and as grusome as ever, and the return of brutalities has given players different means of slaughtering your opponent.
The game feels really balanced with all of the characters; I was able to easily pick up 4-5 fighters including Goro, Takeda, Kenshi, Ermac, and Reptile. The addition of variations gave players a their choice of playstyle. I'm eager to see what they have planned for new and old characters after the first season pass follows through.
Graphically, this game excels. The backdrops in each of the stages are beautiful and vibrant, the characters are all well detailed, and it doesn't hinder the gameplay. This game is very well optimized and I never drop under 60fps during fights. This is the best looking Mortal Kombat yet.
The Krypt is worth mentioning too, its dark, very chilling, and atmospheric. There's a plethora of stuff to unlock which is a good thing. I've never been frightened more in an area where you buy stuff ever. Plus the jumpscares are back and horrifying than ever.
The story was... okay. There were some really good shining moments in the story, but what almost ruined it was the forced ending. The story only took me 4 hours and I was expecting more than just 12 chapters. The played character on the last chapter was, in my opinion, weak against the final boss (Which is the cheapest son-of-a-♥♥♥♥♥ you'll ever see). I didn't feel accomplished when I finished the story, I wanted to play more as the new characters that have been added in the game. But it was an okay ride when it came to the story.
The online still needs some kinks like reducing server lag. My suggestion for right now is to play with friends, if ANY of your friends got this game on PC and not on console. Nothing else in this topic, just needs some fine tuning.
Last but not least, does it have replayability? Yes. Its an extremely fun ride that you can spend hours on learning new fighters, and pulling off combos. This is the best game in the series yet and I'll stand by that. If you're a fan of the fighting game genre, definitely pick this game up.

I will start of by saying that I played this game with a keyboard, not a controller as is recommended. While this was much more difficult, it only amplified the experience that this game provided. The game notes that it comes from a visionary director and this couldn't be more accurate. The landscape and environments are all beautiful and breathtaking, surely some of the best backdrops I have seen in a game in years. The gameplay is excellent, with the player controlling the two brothers in unison to accomplish tasks that would normally be impossible for only one. Though short, the game was extremely satisfying for me and was reminiscent of ICO on many levels. One thing that consistently stands out through the fantasy setting and the indiscernible language spoken by the characters, is the very serious emotion that is infused throughout this game. Sometimes you feel sad, other times you are happy...the game covers all spectrums of feeling brilliantly while inviting the player to experience the world these two brothers inhabit. All facets of the game (it's really more like a piece of art) are strong, music, graphics and gameplay. This is a real treat which I strongly recommend.

This game is a sequel to "Analogue: A Hate Story" and for a better experience, I really recommend you to not play it before playin' it's prequel.
The "Hate Project" (Analogue + Hate Plus) is pretty different from the usual visual novel formula. It isn't focused in dating or romance, but it consists in a needed and mature cross-cultural reflection with elements of feminism all over the main plotline. It does a perfect criticism of the patriarchal system, which is a needed reflection since a lot of it's traces remain in our modern society - and we should eliminate them as soon as possible.
You will play as a space explorer who was hired to investigate the wreckage of a long lost space ship whose disappearance has been a mystery for ages. The ship is inhabited, it's crew is long dead. The only remnants of life are two AI programs called Hyun-ae and Mute. Together, you will dig through the archives, records and digital letters from old members of the crew trying to piece together where and why everything went wrong.
Hate Plus is another heartwarming and unique Visual Novel experience, as Analogue. If you're a fan of Visual Novels with deep plotlines, I definitely recommend you to give this dramatic masterpiece a try.
WARNING: Avoid this game if you don't like heavy reading, because this game is all about reading (and re-reading) tons of texts and try to put small pieces of plot together. Also, if you are an achievement hunter this game might be trouble for you, since it has one impossible to get achievement.

I can tell that this is one of those games that you just absolutely love and dream about away from game (one achievement is to bake a real-life cake), or a game that you don't understand why anyone likes.
I don't really fall into either category.
I like narrative based games--and this is, after all, a digital novel--but the narrative simply doesn't capture me. The mode of narration, the concept, and the executaion are all excellent. I appreciate the clear differences in voice and interesting action occuring in the various logs the player reads with the AI. It is also a original way to present a narrative--at once one the player is part of through the interactions with the AI and the log interface, while remaining completely isolated from the narrative being read. I see why it's a game frequently talked about.
In the end, PLAY IT because it's an interesting premise--even if you don't play much of it.
DON'T PLAY IT if you won't like to read a digital novel

Welcome to The King of Iron Fist Tournament 7!
Tekken comes to PC with this fantastic Tekken 7, a great PC version of one of the most valued, famous and great series in the genre, with around 36 fighters to choose from.
Just like Street Fighter V, Tekken 7 runs on the Unreal Engine 4, which allowed Harada and Tekken Project to pull off a visually stunning title.
Gameplay wise it follows the trend already seen in Tekken 6 and Tekken Tag Tournament 2, so if you have played any of those, you'll know most of your character's move list (some changes have been made among the entries of course, so be sure to double check in Practice).
Single player game modes are missing a couple of classics like Team Battle and Survival, while Arcade is now 5 fights/opponents long (straight from Fated Retribution, if I am not mistaken). Versus battle returns, and in the Options menu there's a "Tournament" setting that can be activated to enable special conditions, such as not being able to pause in Versus and not skip the character intros, basically allowing you to easily organize tourneys, whether with friends or large events.
Ghost Battle has now become Treasure Battle, where you fight ghosts for rewards. This will be your main source of Fight Money and the character items that cannot be bought.
Customization comes back with many items, Tekken Tag Tournament 2 style. This time around though, the team has included specific alt costumes purchasable for each character (ie: Yoshimitsu's HO-1 costume), which I missed in the very last entry.
On top of this, the game has the best netcode in the series, and also includes a quite complete Online mode. You can practice while you search for your opponent, which is a great way to make the (quite short for now at least) waiting time for an opponent. Besides Ranked and Casual quick matches, there's also battle lounges and an Online Tournament mode, so groups of friends or Online communities can  have an easy time coming together to play.
All of the above, while including ALL (and I repeat, ALL) the Tekken saga Cinematics. All endings, Arcade Intros, Home version intros, and even the Tekken 6 prologues made for the Story Campaign are included, which will help refresh your memory or allow you to learn the story of the franchise in preparation of The Mishima Saga.
"The Mishima Saga", Tekken 7' story mode, is divided in 14 chapters, and works quite like Mortal Kombat's latest installments story mode, changing the playable character as you progress.
Technically, the game shows a great amount of care. The game runs incredibly well and is greatly optimized. My PC (GTX1060, i5 3570K and 24GB RAM DDR3@1600MHz) can run this flawlessly at both 1080p and 1440p at max settings. Most probably because Tekken Project built the Arcade versions on what's basically PC architecture.
The only negative point I can give is that Film Grain and Chromatic Aberration, which appear at High and Ultra post processing settings, cannot be disabled on their own, so you might want to turn that down to Medium after you're done with the story.
TL;DR:
Positives:
-Large roster with very varied styles.
-Great netcode and Online modes.
-Lots of character customization options and a few personal ones per character.
-Well executed story mode.
-Gallery includes all the franchise CGI cutscenes + Tekken 6 prologues.
-Lots of stages.
-Tournament Modes!
-Greatly optimized!
Negative:
-Film Grain and Chromatic Aberration not having their own sliders (the latter can be disabled through INI though).
-Lack of Survival and Team Battle.
-Some non returning characters could have made the cut, so it misses a few styles (Lei, Julia).
-Tekken Jukebox is PS4 exclusive, so a few Tekken 7 tracks can't be reassigned.
So, should you buy Tekken 7? My answer is... YES. WHAT ARE YOU DOING HERE STILL.

Brothers is a perfect example of where I think video games should be going. More than anything else, I am incredibly impressed by Brothers' ability to integrate gameplay mechanics and storytelling in such a way that each complement each other. The thing is, despite video games being an interactive medium, few games seem to take full advantage of this fact. I've played games with great mechanics. I've also played games with great stories.  Hell, I've even played games with both great mechanics and great stories. But Brothers is even more than that. What this game manages to do is give emotional weight to gameplay mechanics. By doing this, Brothers takes full advantage of the agency of the player, deepening the emotional bonds produced over a relatively short few hours. I hope developers take a close look at this game.

If you played Analogue:  A Hate Story, you owe it to yourself to buy and play this one too.  If you haven't played the first one, go and play that first because this is a direct sequel in every sense of the term.  It's shorter than the first game but features multiple routes and some intriguing gameplay choices.  Also, unless you are a monster and have no feelings, please be prepared to bake a cake while playing.

TL;DR: Like its predecessor "Analogue: A Hate Story" but with a better UI and more to look at.
This is a visual novel/narrative experience game, set in a sci-fi setting with a lot of mystery, romance and politics. It picks up after the original "Analogue: A Hate Story" via some quick multiple-choice about the way you ended the previous game - however you don't need to have played the previous game to appreciate it, in fact that would probably work better from the mystery angle. There are two possible companions, *Mute who is extremely traditional and *Hyun-Ae who is more flexible and open; both serve just to comment on the text that you read and very occasionally ask questions for a bit of branching narrative. Most of the gameplay is picking which email to read next and then reading through it so that you can work out what actually happened in the central catastrophe which is the main subject of the game.
The game limits how many emails you can "extract" at once, and once you've reached a certain number it'll declare the day over (this kind of makes sense in-game), encouraging you to literally wait until the next day until playing further. It's conspicuously designed to be immersive, and the wait is an element of that. Each "day" takes probably about 1 to 1.5 hours to run through, so it has an extremely casual pace, and the game takes place across three "days".
The content includes convoluted politics, a surprising amount of homosexuality, and some mildly explicit content. The secondary characters - the authors of the emails - are pretty interesting, and the pictures make them fairly easy to remember.
You might reasonably assume that there are romance plots with the companion characters; that's true but they are optional and not very extensive.
So, it's a somewhat immersive mystery experience. Good if you like mysteries, not so good if you like a lot of interactivity.

This series really is something special. This visual novel is a sequel to "Analogue: A Hate Story", and takes place moments after it. Gameplay remains similar while telling yet another story with dark and mature themes.
The story has you managing your remaining power on your 3-day trip back to earth, while you uncover the mystery of what happened "before year 0" onboard of the Mugungwha. The game lets you pick your wai-- I mean companion AI, and even how they act towards you (If you have a finished save file of Analogue you can load it and it will remember things, like how you acted and all). While the routes have you reading similar log files, their reactions and "break conversations" are unique and different, and you'll experience a different perspective of the story.
I'm being relaively vague in this review, as I don't want to spoil any possible surprises. Just know that this story tackles some themes you might not generally see in a visual novel, and you will probably find yourself conflicted and questioning things often.
It's a very unique story with many feels and laughs. It's definitely a series I've come to really enjoy, and hope there might be more at some point in the future. Highly recommended if you want a short, but very unique and interesting visual novel.

Playing this game on Day 1 of release, you'd never have known it was early access. Portal Knights is incredibly well polished for how early it is, and it brings together a lot of great features that (for some reason) have never been properly implemented together before; Building, Mining, Crafting, Leveling, Combat, Bosses, Dodging, Dungeon Crawling; The list goes on.
As others have said (and what really got me to try the game out), Portal Knights is not another Minecraft clone. It's much more of a casual RPG set in a voxel universe. You level up, you have talents (though currently pretty minute), you have proficiencies (again, currently very basic). When you attack an enemy, you enter a sort of Combat mode, where you lock on to your target and can dodge roll, attack etc. While in the mode (as well as while not), you can actually use your hotbar as a sort of 'spellbank', and since every class can use every item, you can have a bow on 1, sword on 2, fireball on 3, heal on 4 and utilize these in larger pulls/bosses etc.
----------------------------
The game has a lot of decorative items and nice looking blocks, tons of foliage, vegetation and a decent variety of mobs. All of which I am thoroughly excited to see grow and evolve. There are 4-5 bosses currently in the game (I've only fought two so far myself) and they have great mechanics, if only a bit too easy.
There are a lot of crafting recipes, some of which you learn by scroll drops (I love this and hope to see a lot more/more rare ones etc) and the models look fantastic and theres a ton of variety. Same goes for armor, but armor has something even more interesting to see in a game like this; Effects. Similar to set bonuses (though you dont need multiple pieces to gain the effect AFAIK) you get a sweet effect on your character just for having certain gear equipped. The effects are more specific to classes, but generally useful for everyone (Crit Chance etc). Can't wait to see this expanded.
-------------------------
CONS:
Difficulty (The game feels a bit too easy as-is)
Mob Variety (There are a decent number of different mobs, but I would love to see more)
It Ends (It appears on the map that after 40+ portals and 4-5 Bosses, there is an "Ending" so-to-speak, or at least a final portal after the (current) final boss.
-------------------------
-Hard/Hardcore Mode: While still very fun, I find the game very easy, even if you don't upgrade your item sets asap. Would love to see a more difficult mode that makes having a party more of a necessity
-Hunger/Thirst: Currently food and vegetables are mostly used for potions, as they barely restore any health. It would be great to have a reason to farm food as it being necessary to survival.
-Player Damage/Dueling: The lock-on combat style could be really fun; having to time dodges, plan combos, etc. Plus, sometimes I just want to kill my friends.
-Authorized Steam Workshop support/mode: I think what can really propel this game to a No Man's Sky/Starbound level of infinite potential would be to open Workshop portals (perhaps as a seperate mode entirely) that would be submitted, voted on, and only accepted by developers/the community (so as to not have a billion trash maps). I could see myself (and I'm sure many others) spend some serious time creating awesome worlds for other players to explore.
-Class Specific Items/Skills: This one I am tossed up about. When playing with two friends (each of us a different class) it really does not matter what any of us have/use. While it is kinda cool to be able to learn mage skills or craft incredible potions as well as build and use weapons etc, I do think it would be really cool to need a friend to use certain skills, or craft certain things. Plus, it could be fantastic to utilize mages healing as it being necessary sometimes.
All in All, this game is in fantastic state, especially for just hitting the market and has an immense amount of potential. Looks polished, plays extremely smoothly, and has a ton of nice stuff bundled extremely well into a unique Voxel based universe. I really want to see this game grow and would love to help any way I can. Plus, its cheap! I got it for $11USD on sale but 14.99 is a steal.

It's South Park - if you enjoy the show you'll enjoy the writing in this game. The story is a satire of classic comic book tropes; not just the modern Marvel movies and Netflix shows but old school comics as well. I found it to be quite brilliant.
Overworld gameplay is almost identical to Stick of Truth - walking around the town, talking to people to gain friends on social media and solving fairly simple puzzles.
Combat has been revamped to be a grid-based tactical RPG (as opposed to the turn-based RPG combat in Stick of Truth).
My first play-through took 23 hours, not quite completing every side-quest in the game, about twice as long as Stick of Truth for me.
I had literally zero technical issues playing the game, never had a crash and experienced a smooth framerate. It does require UPlay, and works like all Ubisoft games on Steam.

I loved this game, honestly, so far this is very hilarious game and in ways suprerior to the first one. I love the fact you can customize your character even more than before, with things like gender, etc, but that doesn't matter much.
Gameplay is solid, fun experience with easter eggs that will bring you satisfaction and quests that are more than fun to do. And the different classes you could choose were just a bless. It's more diverse compared to the four we had last time, and better yet, you could customize it! I also enjoy how you have to plan it very carefully. It added an extra fun to it in my opinion.
So, why don't I recommend the game?
Even though many will say things like "Oh it's pricey" and get mad at company taking 'money' or something about 'u play', I simply do not recommend it at least now (19th of October) because of game related problems. The game has A LOT of glitches, which most are gamebreaking or giving your gameplay unsatisfaction with massive dropping framerates and glitches that make you stuck in a fight or a mission because it won't let you proceed. Opening the game was a big struggle, and still for me it takes over a minute to boot up the game. Sometimes you have to close that game and then update your steam to make it work!
As I'm writing this review, I am stuck on a gamebreaking glitch that stops me from proceeding. This has been a huge problem for me the WHOLE GAME. People are disappearing, I disappear on massive spots, the massive delay in cutscenes. It's just not appealing to me or anyone else. I hope the company makes a patch that will fix this all.
If you are to look forwards to this game, wait for a while when you buy it, because so far it's far too glitchy and unplayable. Otherwise? It's a great successor to the first one and I'd recommend to this wholeheartedly if it wasn't for those glitches and bugs.

TLDR: (textual version will follow)
Yes, you can buy it, especially if you're a South Park fan; don't listen to those negative reviews: their only points are about super easy to avoid issues or about pre-order bonus/gold edition, which no one are forced to buy. If you still have doubts, just wait for a discount and you'll get even more bang for your bucks.
Pros:
- Better combat system than Stick of Truth.
- Tons of easter eggs and references to even the most recent South Park episodes.
- Class system allows you to change at anytime so don't worry about choosing a class you won't like.
- Crafting system is great and make collecting junk useful.
- Timed hits are replaced by a QTE attacks/defense system which makes missing a QTE less frustrating than missing a timed hits.
- Trey Parker and Matt Stone's voice over job is perfect, as always.
Cons:
- Lacks the novelty aspect of Stick of Truth.
- While tutorials are well placed and don't feel like forced choir, the game does take a long time to introduce all concepts one at a time.
- Come additions (DLC/preorder bonus) like Towelie are useless and not that funny.
So, the game is indeed great and much enjoyable. A lot of people made negative reviews out of frustration due to preorder bonus or super easy issues to avoid (like the black screen issue). The game may feel expensive to some, so you may want to wait for a discount to buy it if you're unsure. At least, Ubi learned from the last game and they are now making some story content driven DLCs rather than only adding classes like in Stick of Truth. The game still has very crude content and what I would call "epic moments". I'm not gonna spoil the surprise here. The grid combat system offers some deeper strategy options. Mixing classes also add to strategy and customization, giving more freedom and more options than in stick of Truth, in which you were stuck with one class for the whole game (or until you start a new one).

So I’ve been playing this game for quite a while now, at least I got to the Professor Chao’s U-Store Base and I’ve decided to right a review about this game.
But first, I want to clear something up (Don’t worry, the gameplay review is down below):
1. There is no micro-transaction (You can’t buy the Uplay coins using real money, you can obtain them by completing achievements)
2. There is no gated main story content (You can play the full main story even if you only bought the base game. You can play some special side quest that includes in some DLC but not all DLC have side quest contents)
3. The Day 1 DLC doesn’t gate any sort of story content at all (The Day 1 DLC only includes a few costumes which are purely cosmetics and doesn’t interfere anything at all, it makes no differences. And costumes in this game are pretty common so you can get another costume in the first 1 hour of the game)
4. There isn’t really that much bugs in the game like everyone is talking about (So far I’ve only encounter 1 bug which can be solve quite easily that takes about 5 seconds to solve it)
5. Denuvo only have problems in its infancy stage and are the problems are solved
6. The game is longer than 5-6 hours, although I haven’t beaten the game yet, I’ve seen people that are focused on the main quests but still took around 20+hours to beat the game.
Now time for the gameplay review:
Pros:
1. The combat system is definitely better than the first game (Stick Of Truth). Providing tactics and classes varieties. For the first game, you just melee melee potion melee. But in this game, you need to think for a tactic or strategy to beat the enemy in an effective way, which in my opinion is far better than the first.
2. More puzzle solving means more fun, no more “Go here, beat that guy, go there, beat that another guy, quest completed”. Although there are some puzzles in the first game, but this game’s puzzles are more challenging and more frequent.
3. The map is much bigger than the first. You can now enter those random buildings in main street, go to Raisins and many more.
4. New crafting system means that those junk you find in random trash cans actually do something instead of selling them to a buyer immediately
5. New DNA and Artefact system let you think of a strategy that suits your character the most instead of smacking the most op badge thing on to your weapon like the first game
Cons:
1. Because the battles takes longer than the first game, so you may start to feel like there aren’t enough jokes in the game. But why the devs decided extending the time of battles is a good idea you ask? Well, because you took time to think of a tactic to beat the enemies in an effective way. And the enemies are a bit spongier this time, need about 2-4 hits to take one down. But why spongier you ask? Because if all the enemies are 1-2 hit kills, there will be no space for tactics at all.
That’s all the pros and cons that I can think of right now. If you want me to add more, comment down below to suggest some pros and cons to me. Thank you all for taking time reading this review.

Ok, so this is a recommendation if you can get the game on console. I personally had no major bugs or issues with DRM, but clearly other people are having said issues and I just got lucky. The control scheme in my opinion is much more geared towards console, so it's a win-win situation.
Having said that, my experience was a good one albeit anticlimatic. The game here is good, but is a somewhat inversed version of the original. While the previous installment had very mediocre gameplay but rapid fire jokes, this game has significantly better combat but not as solid writing.
Combat now functions on a grid system, which is a massive step in the right direction. The only problem is that it fails to capitalise on this, and cuts many corners IE many moves are only usable left to right. It's strange, it ♥♥♥♥♥ up some of the basic bits, but then will throw in some really imaginative gameplay ideas such as positioning enemy henchmen to deal damage to the actually boss.
Out of combat gameplay though, is far from spectacular. While there are some decent puzzles, a lot of them are just waiting through cutscenes for teammate to help, then doing a slow boring task to finish it. At first some of South park is cordoned off, leaving a fantastic opportunity to gradually introduce the new character world moves but nope, you get access pretty quickly meaning you have to backtrack for all the god damn yaoi.
As for writing, the effort is clearly here. The first two thirds are absolutely fantastic with amazing presentation and two semi-parallel stories, the Coon's desire for franchise success and a real life kingpin aiming to ruin South park. When these two stories collide though, it was really ♥♥♥♥ing disappointing. Spoilers from here on out.
===========================SPOILERS=================================================
Long story short, the kingpin is Cartman's hand which he uses as a scapegoat. At first I thought to myself "for ♥♥♥♥'s sake, really? They could have done some really clever♥♥♥♥♥♥here". The last 30 minutes offered them a chance to do a real good twist, with the evil hand appearing on Kyle. That was the opportunity to make it all worthwhile. Make Mitch Connor some kind of experiment gone wrong, an alien symbiote, ANYTHING!!! But nope Kyle was just ♥♥♥♥ing with him.
There's also a kind of subplot with your Dad ♥♥♥♥ing your Mum (no seriously) which could have been an amazing twist if they came out and made that the genuine reason for your powers but nope, they go half the way. It was really disappointing and the climax of the game was far below par for South Park. An awkward ending might work for an episode, but not a game with a 20 hour campaign if you ♥♥♥♥ around doing some of the side stuff.
============================Spoilers over======================================
Now, despite this ♥♥♥♥♥ing I do recommend the game. Most of the flaws mentioned only start to grate or become an issue in the third act. Until then, the writing is clever, the gameplay is enjoyable, and it's just damn clever at points. If you really hate games with unsatisfying endings though, avoid it. There's also no real post game content as far as I can see.
If I had to choose one word to describe this game it would be "potential". I honestly think if Ubisoft had actually held off releasing it for another 6 months and not repeatedly make up release dates this could have been an amazing game. It's fine as it is, but godammit they could have taken it to a much higher level. If I had to rate it purely on enjoyment, 8/10, but when I look at it critically? 6/10. It's a very good game but damn, it could have been made so much better. Again, a part of me loves the game, but I'd understand why people would hate it (other than for ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DRM).

Basically You've got World of Tanks for your Tank combat, World of Warships for your naval combat, War Thunder for your air/mech combined arms combat.  This game fits into that genre as well, taking up the spot of infantry/mech/air combined arms. All these games have similar business models, which is why i'm comparing them. This brings me to my first point.
Look, yes it's a f2p game, yes it has a bit of a grind. No it's not unbalanced, or broken, or p2w. For a f2p shooter this game is honestly incredible. If you enjoy ww2 games at all, you owe it to yourself to give it a try. I mean ffs it's FREE. Spend a little money to get veteran status if the grind is too slow, but honestly, compared to most f2p games, this one's grind is actually pretty fast. The game isn't p2w at all, literally everything that can be purchased with RL money can also be unlocked in game. The game has a few quirks, for example you can't go from prone to crouch, you have to stand up first, which kinda sucks, but it hasn't ever gotten me killed, just don't be stupid.
Honestly, you gotta judge this game for what it is, a rather unique f2p ww2 shooter with a really fair business model when you actually look at the numbers.
The game has lots of weapons, upgrades, different classes and gametypes to keep you playing, as well as a unique RTS type element if you're the general type.  If you just want a straight ww2 shooter with no bells and whistles, go buy Red Orchestra 2. If you want something with a bit of an addictive progression to it to keep you going, and game-play reminiscent of the classic call of duty ww2 games, you'll love this.
It's not a perfect game, but it's also not a bad game, and that's why I'd recommend it. Because there's really no better choice out there for a game like this. If i had to compare it to something, I'd say it's most like Battlefield 1942, mixed with a little Planetside 2, on the side.
It's free, so it's not like you're losing anything if you end up not liking it, so give it a go, and  judge it for yourself, because I did, and I'm glad. If I had listened to the reviews here, I would have missed out on over 24 hours of fun already, and to me, that's already worth my time.
Steam reviews are really a stupid way to judge a game anyway, I could have come on here after being killed by a sniper in a bush and been like "This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t there's too many hackers not recommended."
Basically what I'm saying to all y'all is quit getting mad at video games, and enjoy the fact that you get so much game for literally nothing.
OVERALL SCORE 7.5/10

I avoided this game for so long because I thought I would hate it. I'm really not a fan of "frustration" games in which you die repeatedly as you struggle your way up the learning curve.
This is now one of my most played games and is in my top 5 most well designed games, as well as one of my top 5 favorite games of all time.
Yes, you will die often. However, most times you do you will say "I have learned something". There are countless interactions and mechanics but each one *makes intuitive sense*, even if you wouldn't have predicted it at first. So, when you die, you aren't frustrated because it doesn't feel like the game is mocking you with♥♥♥♥♥♥you couldn't have known, it feels like you are learning more about a sensical world.
As with any roguelikes, this is a story generator. The most fun you'll have in this game is when something has gone horribly wrong but you barely manage to scrape it by.
I could go on and on about how fantastic this game is. It's to the point that I use it as a shibboleth for a good designer - if you describe your game as "inspired by Spelunky" I will sit up and take notice.
